def stabOfInv : (φ : PLLFormula) → {Δ : List LJF.Neg} →
    LJF.Inv Δ [] (negOf φ) → LJF.Stab Δ (posOf φ)
  | .prop _, _, d     => LJF.unStable d
  | .falsePLL, _, d   => LJF.unStable d
  | .or _ _, _, d     => LJF.unStable d
  | .and _ _, _, d    => .rfoc (.rel d)
  | .ifThen _ _, _, d => .rfoc (.rel d)
  | .somehow φ, _, d  => stabOfInv φ d
docstring:
A proof of the negative translation is a stable proof of the positive
one.

name: LJFIPC.invOfStab
signature:
def invOfStab : (φ : PLLFormula) → {Δ : List LJF.Neg} →
    LJF.Stab Δ (posOf φ) → LJF.Inv Δ [] (negOf φ)
  | .prop _, _, s     => .stable s
  | .falsePLL, _, s   => .stable s
  | .or _ _, _, s     => .stable s
  | .and _ _, _, s    => LJF.negOfDownStab _ s
  | .ifThen _ _, _, s => LJF.negOfDownStab _ s
  | .somehow φ, _, s  => invOfStab φ s
docstring: …and conversely.

name: LJFIPC.upBranchLFoc
signature:
def upBranchLFoc {Q : LJF.Pos} {Δ : List LJF.Neg} {P : LJF.Pos}
    {b : List LJF.Neg} (hb : b ∈ LJF.invertPos Q) (hsub : ∀ X ∈ b, X ∈ Δ) :
    LJF.LFoc Δ (.up Q) P → LJF.Stab Δ P
  | .rel e =>
      LJF.unStable ((LJF.extract [] e b hb).wk (fun Z hZ => by
        rcases List.mem_append.mp hZ with hZ | hZ
        · exact hsub Z hZ
        · exact hZ))
docstring:
Discharge a left focus on a shifted hypothesis against a branch of its
positive.

name: LJFIPC.downBranchLFoc
docstring:
Discharge a left focus on a hypothesis whose positive is a shift: the
single branch *is* the hypothesis.

name: LJFIPC.branchLFoc
signature:
def branchLFoc : (φ : PLLFormula) → {Δ : List LJF.Neg} → {P : LJF.Pos} →
    {b : List LJF.Neg} → b ∈ LJF.invertPos (posOf φ) → (∀ X ∈ b, X ∈ Δ) →
    LJF.LFoc Δ (negOf φ) P → LJF.Stab Δ P
  | .prop _, _, _, _, hb, hsub, lf   => upBranchLFoc hb hsub lf
  | .falsePLL, _, _, _, hb, _, _     => by
      simp only [posOf, LJF.invertPos, List.not_mem_nil] at hb
  | .or _ _, _, _, _, hb, hsub, lf   => upBranchLFoc hb hsub lf
  | .and _ _, _, _, _, hb, hsub, lf  => downBranchLFoc hb hsub lf
  | .ifThen _ _, _, _, _, hb, hsub, lf => downBranchLFoc hb hsub lf
  | .somehow φ, _, _, _, hb, hsub, lf => branchLFoc φ hb hsub lf
docstring:

the inversion of `posOf φ`.

name: LJFIPC.PFree
signature:
def PFree (p : String) : PLLFormula → Prop
  | .prop a     => a ≠ p
  | .falsePLL   => True
  | .and a b    => PFree p a ∧ PFree p b
  | .or a b     => PFree p a ∧ PFree p b
  | .ifThen a b => PFree p a ∧ PFree p b
  | .somehow a  => PFree p a
docstring: `p` does not occur.

name: LJFIPC.pfree_unPos
signature:
theorem pfree_unPos {p : String} :
    ∀ P : LJF.Pos, LJF.PFreeP p P → PFree p (unPos P)
  | .atom _, h  => h
  | .fls, _     => trivial
  | .or P Q, h  => ⟨pfree_unPos P h.1, pfree_unPos Q h.2⟩
  | .down N, h  => pfree_unNeg N h

name: LJFIPC.pfree_unNeg
signature:
theorem pfree_unNeg {p : String} :
    ∀ N : LJF.Neg, LJF.PFreeN p N → PFree p (unNeg N)
  | .up P, h    => pfree_unPos P h
  | .imp Q N, h => ⟨pfree_unPos Q h.1, pfree_unNeg N h.2⟩
  | .and M N, h => ⟨pfree_unNeg M h.1, pfree_unNeg N h.2⟩

name: LJFIPC.uniform_interpolation_IPC
signature:
theorem uniform_interpolation_IPC (p : String) (Γ : List PLLFormula)
    (φ : PLLFormula) (hΓ : ∀ ψ ∈ Γ, PLLND.isIPL ψ) (hφ : PLLND.isIPL φ) :
    (PFree p (exI p Γ) ∧
      PLLND.SemUI.Deriv Γ (exI p Γ) ∧
      ∀ (Δ : List PLLFormula) (ψ : PLLFormula),
        (∀ χ ∈ Δ, PLLND.isIPL χ) → (∀ χ ∈ Δ, PFree p χ) →
        PLLND.isIPL ψ → PFree p ψ →
        PLLND.SemUI.Deriv (Γ ++ Δ) ψ →
        PLLND.SemUI.Deriv (exI p Γ :: Δ) ψ)
    ∧ (PFree p (allI p Γ φ) ∧
      PLLND.SemUI.Deriv (allI p Γ φ :: Γ) φ ∧
      ∀ Δ : List PLLFormula,
        (∀ χ ∈ Δ, PLLND.isIPL χ) → (∀ χ ∈ Δ, PFree p χ) →
        PLLND.SemUI.Deriv (Γ ++ Δ) φ →
        PLLND.SemUI.Deriv (exI p Γ :: Δ) (allI p Γ φ))
docstring:
**Uniform interpolation for IPC.**  For every `◯`-free context `Γ`, every
`◯`-free formula `φ` and every atom `p`, the two formulas `exI p Γ` and
`allI p Γ φ` avoid `p` and satisfy Pitts' properties with respect to natural
deduction on the `◯`-free fragment.

def compNucleus (j k : Nucleus X) (h : ∀ x, j (k x) = k (j x)) : Nucleus X where

docstring: The composite `k ∘ j` of two nuclei is a nucleus **when they commute**.

name: BeliefLax.compNucleus_apply

name: BeliefLax.isLUB_comp_of_comm
signature:
theorem isLUB_comp_of_comm (j k : Nucleus X) (h : ∀ x, j (k x) = k (j x)) :
    IsLUB {j, k} (compNucleus j k h)
docstring:
**Commuting nuclei: the join is the composite.** For nuclei `j`, `k` with
`j ∘ k = k ∘ j`, the composite `k ∘ j` is the least upper bound of `j` and `k`
in the lattice of nuclei — so their join terminates in one step.

name: BeliefLax.eq_of_transparent_comm
signature:
theorem eq_of_transparent_comm (j k : Nucleus X)
    (hjk : ∀ x, j (k x) ≤ k x) (hkj : ∀ x, k (j x) ≤ j x)
    (hc : ∀ x, j (k x) = k (j x)) : j = k
docstring:
**Mutual transparency plus commutation forces identity.** If each believer
sees through the other's beliefs — `j (k x) ≤ k x` and `k (j x) ≤ j x` — and
the two commute, then `j = k`. (The transparency inequalities are the
nontrivial halves; the reverse inequalities are inflationarity.)

name: sup_eq_comp_of_comm
signature:
theorem sup_eq_comp_of_comm (j k : Nucleus X) (h : ∀ x, j (k x) = k (j x)) :
    j ⊔ k = compNucleus j k h
docstring: The lattice join of two commuting nuclei is their composite.

name: sup_apply_of_comm
signature:
theorem sup_apply_of_comm (j k : Nucleus X) (h : ∀ x, j (k x) = k (j x)) (x : X) :
    (j ⊔ k) x = k (j x)
docstring: The join of two commuting nuclei, pointwise: `(j ⊔ k) x = k (j x)`.

name: PLLND.Async.cElemTm
signature: def cElemTm : Tm [Sa, Sb] Sab
docstring:
**The meet law as a proof term**: `◯a, ◯b ⊢ ◯(a ∧ b)`.  Run the belief in
`a`, then under its constraint run the belief in `b`, then return the pair.
Two `bind`s and a `val` --- the derivation is sequential.

name: PLLND.Async.envMeet
signature: def envMeet (δa δb : ℕ) : Env (M := ℕ) B [Sa, Sb]
docstring: The rendezvous environment: inputs settled at `δa` and `δb`.

name: PLLND.Async.cElem_sequential
signature:
theorem cElem_sequential (δa δb : ℕ) :
    (cElemTm.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envMeet δa δb)).1 = δa + δb
docstring:
**The derivation is sequential**: the canonical proof of the meet law pays
`μ = +` at each `bind`, so it extracts `δa + δb` --- believe `a`, *then*
believe `b`.

name: PLLND.Async.Γc
signature: abbrev Γc : List PLLFormula
docstring: The one-gate netlist `[C : ◯a ⊃ ◯b ⊃ ◯c, ◯a, ◯b]`.

name: PLLND.Async.cGateTm
signature: def cGateTm : Tm Γc Sc
docstring: The C-element applied to its two inputs: `Γc ⊢ ◯c`.

name: PLLND.Async.envC
signature: def envC (δC δa δb : ℕ) : Env (M := ℕ) B Γc
docstring:
The gate environment: a C-element of delay `δC`, inputs settled at `δa`,
`δb`.

name: PLLND.Async.cElem_parallel
signature:
theorem cElem_parallel (δC δa δb : ℕ) :
    (cGateTm.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envC δC δa δb)).1 = max δa δb + δC
docstring:
**The element is parallel**: `max(δa, δb) + δ_C` --- it waits for the later
input, not for one input after the other.

name: PLLND.Async.cElem_beats_sequential
signature:
theorem cElem_beats_sequential (δC δa δb : ℕ) :
    max δa δb + δC < δa + δb ↔ δC < min δa δb
docstring:
**When the rendezvous pays.**  The C-element realisation beats the
sequential derivation exactly when the element's own delay is below the
*faster* input's settling time.  (With `δ_C = 0` it is never worse, since
`max x y ≤ x + y`.)

name: PLLND.Async.dC

docstring: Nominal C-element delay (ps), of the same order as the other cells.

name: PLLND.Async.g1
signature: abbrev g1 : PLLFormula

name: PLLND.Async.g2
signature: abbrev g2 : PLLFormula

name: PLLND.Async.Ogrant
signature: abbrev Ogrant
docstring: "Some grant is issued."

name: PLLND.Async.OgOrOg
signature: abbrev OgOrOg
docstring: "Grant 1 is issued, or grant 2 is issued."

name: PLLND.Async.arbiterM
signature: def arbiterM : FinCM
docstring:
**The arbiter as a finite constraint model.**  World `0` is *contention*:
both requests are up and the arbiter has not resolved.  Worlds `1` and `2` are
the two resolutions, granting `g₁` and `g₂` respectively.  They are
`Rᵢ`-incomparable and neither is `Rₘ`-reachable from the other: **mutual
exclusion is exactly the absence of a reconvergent world**.  (This is the
split model of \[F&M 1997, Fig. 3\], read as a circuit.)

name: PLLND.Async.arbiter_believes_grant
signature: theorem arbiter_believes_grant : FinCM.forceB arbiterM 0 Ogrant = true
docstring: **Under contention some grant is believed.**

name: PLLND.Async.arbiter_denies_g1
signature: theorem arbiter_denies_g1 : FinCM.forceB arbiterM 0 (somehow g1) = false
docstring:
**But neither grant is believed.**  No constraint discharges to `g₁` along
every future --- the `g₂`-resolution is a future in which it never does.

name: PLLND.Async.arbiter_denies_g2
signature: theorem arbiter_denies_g2 : FinCM.forceB arbiterM 0 (somehow g2) = false

name: PLLND.Async.arbiter_no_distribution
signature: theorem arbiter_no_distribution : ¬ Nonempty (LaxND [Ogrant] OgOrOg)
docstring:
**The arbiter refutes `◯`-distribution over `∨`**, through the verified
checker: believing that *a* grant occurs does not amount to believing, of some
particular grant, that it occurs.

name: PLLND.Async.mutConfluentB
signature: def mutConfluentB (M : FinCM) : Bool
docstring:
Mutual confluence as a decidable check on a finite model, mirroring
`PLLFrames.MutuallyConfluent`: from `x`, an `Rₘ`-step to `w` and an `Rᵢ`-step
to `v` must close at some `u` with `w Rᵢ u` and `v Rₘ u`.

name: PLLND.Async.arbiter_not_confluent
signature: theorem arbiter_not_confluent : mutConfluentB arbiterM = false
docstring:
**The arbiter frame is not mutually confluent.**  From contention, the
`Rₘ`-step granting `g₁` and the `Rᵢ`-step to the `g₂`-resolution have no common
future: that is mutual exclusion.  Since mutually confluent frames are exactly
the models of PLL + the distribution scheme
(`PLLND.ConfluentU.derivU_iff_confluent_valid`), this non-confluence *is* the
reason `arbiter_no_distribution` holds.

name: PLLND.Candidate.LC
signature:
inductive LC (p : String) : List Neg → List Pos → JD → Neg → Prop
  | impR {Γ Ω Q N} : LC p Γ (Q :: Ω) .tru N → LC p Γ Ω .tru (.imp Q N)
  | andR {Γ Ω M N} : LC p Γ Ω .tru M → LC p Γ Ω .tru N → LC p Γ Ω .tru (.and M N)
  | circR {Γ Ω j P} : LC p Γ Ω .lax (.up P) → LC p Γ Ω j (.circ P)
  | orL {Γ Ω P Q j N} :
      LC p Γ (P :: Ω) j N → LC p Γ (Q :: Ω) j N → LC p Γ (.or P Q :: Ω) j N
  | fls {Γ Ω j N} : LC p Γ (.fls :: Ω) j N
  | downL {Γ Ω M j N} : LC p (M :: Γ) Ω j N → LC p Γ (.down M :: Ω) j N
  | atomL {Γ Ω a j N} :
      LC p (.up (.atom a) :: Γ) Ω j N → LC p Γ (.atom a :: Ω) j N
  | init {Γ j a} : Neg.up (Pos.atom a) ∈ Γ → a ≠ p → LC p Γ [] j (.up (.atom a))
  | orR {Γ j P Q} : LC p Γ [] j (.up P) → LC p Γ [] j (.up (.or P Q))
  | rel {Γ j N} : LC p Γ [] j N → LC p Γ [] j (.up (.down N))
  | impL {Γ j Q N P} : Neg.imp Q N ∈ Γ → LC p Γ [] .tru (.up Q) →
      LC p (N :: Γ) [] j (.up P) → LC p Γ [] j (.up P)
  | andL {Γ j M N P} : Neg.and M N ∈ Γ → LC p (M :: Γ) [] j (.up P) →
      LC p Γ [] j (.up P)
  | andL' {Γ j M N P} : Neg.and M N ∈ Γ → LC p (N :: Γ) [] j (.up P) →
      LC p Γ [] j (.up P)
  | circL {Γ Q P} : Neg.circ Q ∈ Γ → LC p Γ [Q] .lax (.up P) →
      LC p Γ [] .lax (.up P)
docstring:
**The least interpolation candidate**: the inductive predicate whose
constructors are the thirteen closure clauses.  A second-order object — a
least fixed point over predicates on inversion sequents — whose existence
needs no extremal formula.

name: PLLND.Candidate.LC.toCand
signature:
def toCand (p : String) : Cand p where
  C
docstring: `LC p` satisfies the thirteen clauses: it is itself a candidate.

name: PLLND.Candidate.LC.initial
signature:
theorem initial {p : String} (K : Cand p) :
    ∀ {Γ Ω j N}, LC p Γ Ω j N → K.C Γ Ω j N
docstring:
**Initiality**: the least candidate is contained in every candidate.
One structural induction; each constructor maps to its clause.

name: PLLND.Candidate.LC.le_budget
signature:
theorem le_budget {p : String} {θ : PLLFormula} {Γ Ω j N}
    (h : LC p Γ Ω j N) : CandOr.Cθ θ Γ Ω j N
docstring:
Initiality at the consequence candidates: `LC`-membership makes the
sequent derivable from **every** budget — in particular from `⊤`.  So `LC`
marks the sequents whose `p`-content is irrelevant, which is exactly what the
interpolant recursion must compute a formula-level witness FOR.

the clause the whole difficulty was traced to, and for the consequence

signature:

signature:

    (h : Cθ θ Γ [] j N) : Cθ θ Γ [] j (.up (.down N))
docstring: `cl_rel`: `⌜↑↓N⌝ = ⌜N⌝` definitionally.

name: PLLND.CandOr.cθ_impL
docstring: `cl_impL`: modus ponens into the continuation, via cut.

name: PLLND.CandOr.cθ_andL
docstring: `cl_andL`: projection into the continuation.

name: PLLND.CandOr.cθ_andL'
PLLND.CandOr.cθ_circL
docstring:
`cl_circL` — **the contraction clause, and it holds by `laxElim` with the
`◯`-hypothesis RETAINED**.  `Q` enters `Ω` while `◯Q` stays in `Γ`: this is
exactly the retention discipline of the `G4c` repairs, now a theorem about the
candidate rather than a rule design.

name: PLLND.CandOr.candOf
signature:
def candOf (p : String) (θ : PLLFormula) : Candidate.Cand p where
  C
docstring:
**Every `p`-free budget `θ` yields an interpolation candidate.**  All
thirteen clauses hold for `Cθ`; the `p`-freeness of `θ` is not even needed for
the closure clauses (only `cl_init`'s side condition mentions `p`, and `Cθ`
satisfies the unconditional strengthening).  So candidacy is NONVACUOUS, and
the entire remaining content of uniform interpolation is EXTREMALITY: for a
given antecedent, a least budget among those whose candidate holds.  That is
the ∃p question, and the ∀p question is its dual — exactly the split of
`docs/ui-two-routes.md` §1, reached this time through the candidate method.

name: PLLND.CandOr.cθ_strengthen
docstring: Budgets are closed under strengthening: a stronger budget serves.

name: PLLND.CandOr.ExtremalBudget
signature:
def ExtremalBudget (p : String) (Γ : List Neg) (Ω : List Pos) (j : JD)
    (N : Neg) : Type
docstring:
**The extremality target** (`∃p`, candidate form): a `p`-free budget for
the sequent that is entailed by every other `p`-free budget — the weakest
`p`-free formula whose candidate accepts the sequent.  Uniform interpolation
for the sequent IS the inhabitation of this type for every sequent.  Stated,
not proved; this is where the ∃p/∀p asymmetry of `docs/ui-two-routes.md` §1
re-enters, and the directedness criterion is what inhabitation will need.

name: PLLND.CandOr.seqFml
signature: def seqFml (Γ : List Neg) (Ω : List Pos) (j : JD) (N : Neg) : PLLFormula
docstring: The sequent as one formula: hypotheses curried into the wrapped conclusion.

name: PLLND.CandOr.curry
signature:
def curry : ∀ (L : List PLLFormula) {Δ : List PLLFormula} {g : PLLFormula},
    LaxND (L ++ Δ) g → LaxND Δ (L.foldr .ifThen g)
  | [], _, _, d => d
  | A :: L, Δ, g, d =>
      .impIntro (curry L (d.rename (fun ψ hψ => by
        simp only [List.mem_cons, List.mem_append] at hψ ⊢
        tauto)))
docstring: Currying: discharge a hypothesis block into the goal.

name: PLLND.CandOr.uncurry
signature:
def uncurry : ∀ (L : List PLLFormula) {Δ : List PLLFormula} {g : PLLFormula},
    LaxND Δ (L.foldr .ifThen g) → LaxND (L ++ Δ) g
  | [], _, _, d => d
  | A :: L, Δ, g, d => by
      have step : LaxND (A :: Δ) (L.foldr .ifThen g)
docstring: Uncurrying: reinstate a hypothesis block from the goal.

name: PLLND.CandOr.cθ_iff_entails
signature:
theorem cθ_iff_entails (θ : PLLFormula) (Γ : List Neg) (Ω : List Pos)
    (j : JD) (N : Neg) :
    Cθ θ Γ Ω j N ↔ Nonempty (LaxND [θ] (seqFml Γ Ω j N))
docstring: **Acceptance is entailment**: `Cθ θ S ↔ θ ⊢ ⌜S⌝`.

name: PLLND.CandOr.extremal_iff_forallp
signature:
theorem extremal_iff_forallp (p : String) (Γ : List Neg) (Ω : List Pos)
    (j : JD) (N : Neg) (θ : PLLFormula) :
    (Candidate.PFreeNeg p (polNeg θ) ∧ Cθ θ Γ Ω j N ∧
      ∀ θ' : PLLFormula, Candidate.PFreeNeg p (polNeg θ') → Cθ θ' Γ Ω j N →
        Nonempty (LaxND [θ'] θ))
    ↔ (Candidate.PFreeNeg p (polNeg θ) ∧
        Nonempty (LaxND [θ] (seqFml Γ Ω j N)) ∧
      ∀ θ' : PLLFormula, Candidate.PFreeNeg p (polNeg θ') →
        Nonempty (LaxND [θ'] (seqFml Γ Ω j N)) → Nonempty (LaxND [θ'] θ))
docstring:
**The convergence theorem.**  `ExtremalBudget p S` is precisely the
propositional quantifier `∀p ⌜S⌝`: a greatest `p`-free formula entailing the
sequent formula.  The candidate method, run to completion, lands on the same
object the algebraic route (`docs/ui-two-routes.md` §1) identified as the hard
half — and `∃p` never appears, because the closure clauses absorbed it.

Consequence, recorded in `PROGRESS-POLAR.md` §4: uniform interpolation for PLL
holds iff for every sequent formula `φ` the ideal
`T = {ψ p-free : ψ ⊢ φ}` is principal.  `T` is an ideal (downward closed, and
`∨`-closed since `ψ₁ ⊢ φ` and `ψ₂ ⊢ φ` give `ψ₁∨ψ₂ ⊢ φ`); principality can
fail only through an infinite strictly ascending chain of `p`-free formulas
below `φ`, and at one variable "p-free" means CLOSED, where the repository has
a mechanised strictly ascending chain — the boxed odd rungs
(`chain_step_strict`).  The refutation hunt is therefore: a one-variable `φ`
whose closed lower ideal is generated by that chain.

name: PLLND.CandOr.extremalOfPFree
docstring:
**The degenerate case, inhabited**: when the sequent formula is itself
`p`-free, it is its own extremal budget — self-acceptance is the identity
axiom curried, and minimality is currying of the acceptance.  Minimality here
does not even use `p`-freeness of the competitor.

name: PLLND.Candidate.PFreePos
signature:
def PFreePos (p : String) : Pos → Prop
  | .atom a => a ≠ p
  | .fls    => True
  | .or q r => PFreePos p q ∧ PFreePos p r
  | .down n => PFreeNeg p n
docstring: `p` does not occur in a positive proposition.

name: PLLND.Candidate.PFreeNeg
signature:
def PFreeNeg (p : String) : Neg → Prop
  | .up q    => PFreePos p q
  | .imp q n => PFreePos p q ∧ PFreeNeg p n
  | .and m n => PFreeNeg p m ∧ PFreeNeg p n
  | .circ q  => PFreePos p q
docstring: `p` does not occur in a negative proposition.

name: PLLND.Candidate.Cand
signature:
structure Cand (p : String) where
  /-- The predicate, on inversion sequents. -/
  C : List Neg → List Pos → JD → Neg → Prop
docstring:
An **interpolation candidate** for the variable `p`: a predicate on
**inversion sequents** closed under the clauses forced by the rules of
`PLLFocused`.

Every field is named for the rule that forced it. The two marked `★` carry the
difficulty; see the discussion after the structure.

The workhorse: transform a `disjOf`-derivation by handling each

      Nonempty (LaxND L (bigOr Ds))
  | _ :: _, .head _, p => ⟨.orIntro1 p⟩
  | _ :: _, .tail _ h, p => (bigOrIntro h p).elim fun q => ⟨.orIntro2 q⟩
docstring:
Introduce a finite disjunction at any disjunct.  (`Prop`-level:
the membership hypothesis is a `Prop`, so it can only be matched when
eliminating into `Prop`.)

name: PLLND.LaxND.bigOrElim
signature:
def bigOrElim {L : List PLLFormula} {χ : PLLFormula} :
    {Ds : List PLLFormula} → LaxND L (bigOr Ds) →
      (∀ φ, φ ∈ Ds → LaxND (φ :: L) χ) → LaxND L χ
  | [], p, _ => .falsoElim _ p
  | ψ :: Ds', p, br =>
      .orElim p (br ψ (.head _))
        (bigOrElim (.iden (List.mem_cons_self ..))
          (fun φ h => (br φ (.tail _ h)).rename (by
            intro χ' h'
            simp only [List.mem_cons] at h' ⊢
            exact h'.imp id .inr)))
docstring:
Eliminate a finite disjunction: if every disjunct yields `χ`, so does the
disjunction.  On the empty list `bigOr [] = ⊥` and falsity elimination
applies.

theorem bigOr_intro {Γ : Set PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula}
    {Ds : List PLLFormula} (hmem : φ ∈ Ds) (h : Γ ⊩ φ) : Γ ⊩ bigOr Ds
docstring: Finite-disjunction introduction, set level.

name: PLLND.SetDeriv.bigOr_elim
signature:
theorem bigOr_elim {Γ : Set PLLFormula} {χ : PLLFormula} :
    ∀ {Ds : List PLLFormula}, Γ ⊩ bigOr Ds →
      (∀ φ ∈ Ds, insert φ Γ ⊩ χ) → Γ ⊩ χ
  | [], h, _ => falso χ h
  | ψ :: Ds', h, br =>
      orE h (br ψ (.head _))
        (bigOr_elim (Ds := Ds') (of_mem (Set.mem_insert ..))
          (fun φ hφ => by
            have := br φ (.tail _ hφ)
            exact mono (by
              intro χ' h'
              rcases h' with rfl | h'
              · exact Set.mem_insert ..
              · exact Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ h')) this))
docstring: Finite-disjunction elimination, set level.

name: PLLND.SetDeriv.bigOr_collapse
docstring:
If every disjunct of `Ds` collapses to the single formula `χ`
(as happens for `Ds ⊆ {χ}`), the whole disjunction collapses.

name: PLLND.SetDeriv.bigOr_sub

docstring: Weakening a finite disjunction to a superlist.

name: PLLND.SetDeriv.somehow_mono

docstring:
`◯` is functorial, set level: from `insert φ Γ ⊩ ψ` and `Γ ⊩ ◯φ`
conclude `Γ ⊩ ◯ψ`.  (This is set-level `laxElim` with a non-`◯` minor
premise promoted by `laxIntro`.)

    Var Γ φ → Env (M := M) base Γ → sem (M := M) base φ
  | _, _, .here, ρ => ρ.1
  | _, _, .there v, ρ => v.look ρ.2
docstring: Variable lookup.

name: PLLND.Tm.eval
signature:
def Tm.eval : ∀ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula},
    Tm Γ φ → Env (M := M) base Γ → sem (M := M) base φ
  | _, _, .var v, ρ => v.look base ρ
  | _, _, .abort _ t, ρ => (t.eval ρ).elim
  | _, _, .lam t, ρ => fun a => t.eval (a, ρ)
  | _, _, .app t s, ρ => t.eval ρ (s.eval ρ)
  | _, _, .pair t s, ρ => (t.eval ρ, s.eval ρ)
  | _, _, .fst t, ρ => (t.eval ρ).1
  | _, _, .snd t, ρ => (t.eval ρ).2
  | _, _, .inl t, ρ => .inl (t.eval ρ)
  | _, _, .inr t, ρ => .inr (t.eval ρ)
  | _, _, .case t u₁ u₂, ρ =>
      match t.eval ρ with
      | .inl a => u₁.eval (a, ρ)
      | .inr b => u₂.eval (b, ρ)
  | _, _, .val t, ρ => (e, t.eval ρ)
  | _, _, .bind t u, ρ =>
      let p
docstring: Evaluation of proof terms — constraint extraction.

name: PLLND.FinCM
signature:
structure FinCM where
  n : Nat
  ri : List (Nat × Nat)
  rm : List (Nat × Nat)
  fall : List Nat
  val : List (Nat × String)
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
docstring:
A finite constraint model as printable, decidable data.  Worlds are
`0, …, n-1`; `ri`/`rm` list the non-reflexive relation pairs; `fall` lists
the fallible worlds; `val` lists the true `(world, atom)` pairs.

docstring: `Rᵢ` test, reflexive closure built in.

docstring: `Rₘ` test, reflexive closure built in.

docstring: Fallibility test.

docstring: Valuation test; fallible worlds validate every atom by construction.

name: PLLND.FinCM.forceB
signature:
def forceB (M : FinCM) : Nat → PLLFormula → Bool
  | w, .prop a => M.valB w a
  | w, .falsePLL => M.fallB w
  | w, .and φ ψ => M.forceB w φ && M.forceB w ψ
  | w, .or φ ψ => M.forceB w φ || M.forceB w ψ
  | w, .ifThen φ ψ =>
      (List.range M.n).all fun v =>
        !(M.riB w v) || !(M.forceB v φ) || M.forceB v ψ
  | w, .somehow φ =>
      (List.range M.n).all fun v =>
        !(M.riB w v) ||
        (List.range M.n).any fun u => M.rmB v u && M.forceB u φ
docstring:
**Computable forcing**: structural recursion on the formula, world
quantifiers as folds over `List.range n`.

    FinCM × List (List PLLFormula × List PLLFormula)
docstring: Assemble the finite model from the `(T, P)` worlds.

name: PLLND.CounterEmit.emit
signature:
partial def emit (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula)
    (budget : Option Nat := none) (precheck : Bool := true) :
    Option (FinCM × Nat)
docstring:
**The countermodel emitter.**  Returns a finite model and a refuting
world for underivable sequents — every candidate is validated by the
*verified* `checkB` before being returned, so a wrong guess can only yield
`none`, never a wrong certificate.

The first thing it does is *run proof search*: `build` is exponential in
the closure, so it is worth a search to avoid building the model of a
provable sequent.  Two parameters control that search, and both exist to
stop this stage from being the unbounded one.

* `budget` caps it at that many visited sequents.  A **cutoff** returns
  `none`: the sequent might be provable, and building the model of a
  sequent that might be provable is exactly the work the budget was set to
  avoid.  So under a budget this emitter answers only about sequents whose
  search space it could exhaust — which is what `Search.Config.findBudget`
  promises everywhere else.
* `precheck := false` skips the search altogether.  Pass it when the
  caller has *already* run a search to exhaustion and found nothing, as
  `Search.settleWhy` has by the time it reaches this stage; the saving is
  one whole search on the expensive case.

name: PLLND.CounterEmit.restrict
signature: def restrict (M : FinCM) (keep : List Nat) : FinCM
docstring:
Restrict a model to the listed worlds (renumbered in list order).
Every frame condition is universally quantified over the worlds present,
so any restriction of a well-formed model is well-formed; forcing, of
course, changes — which is why every use below is checker-gated.

name: PLLND.CounterEmit.minimise
signature:
partial def minimise (M : FinCM) (w : Nat) (Γ : List PLLFormula)
    (C : PLLFormula) (accept : FinCM → Bool := fun _ => true) : FinCM × Nat
docstring:
**Greedy countermodel minimisation**: repeatedly remove any single
world whose removal leaves the checker satisfied, until none can go.
Untrusted, checker-gated at every step — the result is certified by the
same `checkB` as the input.

`accept` is an extra property the intermediate models must keep, the same
untrusted pre-filter as `Search.Config.accept`.  It matters when the
property is *not* inherited by submodels: mutual confluence (`RNC.confB`)
is the case in hand — deleting a world can destroy it — so a PCLL search
must pass `confB` here, or minimisation would hand back a model that no
longer refutes PCLL.  The default keeps every model.

name: PLLND.CounterEmit.cleanStep
signature:
def cleanStep (M : FinCM) (w : Nat) (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula)
    (accept : FinCM → Bool := fun _ => true) : FinCM
docstring:
One sweep of checker-gated attribute deletions: each fallible flag,
then each valuation pair, then each non-reflexive `ri`/`rm` pair is
removed if `checkB` still certifies the sequent afterwards.  Deleting a
relation pair can break transitivity or `Rₘ ⊆ Rᵢ`; the `wellB` conjunct
of `checkB` rejects exactly those edits, so gating on the full check
suffices.

name: PLLND.CounterEmit.clean
signature:
partial def clean (M : FinCM) (w : Nat) (Γ : List PLLFormula)
    (C : PLLFormula) (accept : FinCM → Bool := fun _ => true) : FinCM × Nat
docstring:
**Checker-gated attribute cleaning**: `minimise` deletes worlds but
never edits the survivors' attributes, so a minimised model can carry
vestigial data — a fallible flag no longer doing any work, a valuation
pair or relation pair the refutation never uses.  `clean` sweeps the
attributes with `cleanStep` and iterates to a fixpoint.  Worlds are never
deleted or renumbered, so the refuting world `w` passes through
unchanged.  Untrusted and greedy, like `minimise`: every step is gated by
the verified `checkB`, so a wrong edit can only be rejected, never
mis-certify.

name: PLLND.CounterEmit.simplify
signature:
partial def simplify (M : FinCM) (w : Nat) (Γ : List PLLFormula)
    (C : PLLFormula) (accept : FinCM → Bool := fun _ => true) : FinCM × Nat
docstring:
**The countermodel simplifier**: `minimise` and `clean` run
alternately to a joint fixpoint.

Neither pass subsumes the other, and each can re-enable the other:
deleting a world can leave a relation pair with nothing to do, and
deleting a relation pair can leave a world unreachable, so a single
`minimise`-then-`clean` is not in general a fixpoint of either.  The loop
terminates because every round that changes anything deletes at least one
world, pair or flag.

`accept` is threaded through both passes; see `minimise`.  Untrusted and
greedy like its two components: every intermediate model is gated by the
verified `FinCM.checkB`, so the result is certified exactly as the input
was, and a wrong edit can only be rejected.

docstring:
Semantic profile of a world: which of the given formulas it forces —

name: PLLND.CounterEmit.emitMin
signature:
partial def emitMin (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) :

docstring:
Emit and then minimise: the systematic countermodel, cut down to a

name: PLLND.CounterEmit.emitMinClean
signature:
partial def emitMinClean (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) :
    Option (FinCM × Nat)
docstring:
Emit, minimise, then clean: the systematic countermodel cut down by
checker-gated world deletion, then stripped of vestigial attributes by
checker-gated edits.  The result is certified by the same `checkB` as
every intermediate model.

One pass of each, in that order — `simplify` is the version that alternates
the two to a fixpoint, and is what `Search.Config.simplify` runs.  The two
agree on every model in this file; they can differ when a cleaned edge
leaves a world with nothing to do.

PLLND.SC.trueR
signature: theorem SC.trueR {Γ : List PLLFormula} : SC Γ truePLL
docstring: `⊤` (definitionally `⊥ ⊃ ⊥`) is derivable in any context.

name: PLLND.SCh.maehara
signature:
theorem SCh.maehara : ∀ {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula},
    SCh n Γ C → ∀ Γ₁ Γ₂ : List PLLFormula,
    (∀ ψ ∈ Γ, ψ ∈ Γ₁ ∨ ψ ∈ Γ₂) →
    ∃ I : PLLFormula,
      SC Γ₁ I ∧ SC (I :: Γ₂) C ∧
      I.atoms ⊆ atomsList Γ₁ ∧ I.atoms ⊆ finUnion (atomsList Γ₂) C.atoms
docstring:
**Maehara's lemma** for the cut-free calculus, membership-split form:
from a derivation of `Γ ⊢ C` and an assignment of each hypothesis of `Γ`
to `Γ₁` or to `Γ₂`, an interpolant `I` with `Γ₁ ⊢ I`, `I, Γ₂ ⊢ C`, and
`I`'s atoms contained both in `Γ₁`'s and in `Γ₂, C`'s.

Interpolant construction, by the last rule and the side of its
principal formula (`Γ₁`-side / `Γ₂`-side):

| rule       | `Γ₁`-side              | `Γ₂`-side       |
|------------|------------------------|-----------------|
| `init`     | the atom itself        | `⊤`             |
| `botL`     | `⊥`                    | `⊤`             |
| `andR`     | `I₁ ∧ I₂`              | (same — right rule) |
| `andL`     | pass through           | pass through    |
| `orR1/2`   | pass through           | (right rule)    |
| `orL`      | `I₁ ∨ I₂`              | `I₁ ∧ I₂`       |
| `impR`     | pass through           | (right rule)    |
| `impL`     | `I₁ ⊃ I₂` (split swapped for the minor premise) | `I₁ ∧ I₂` |
| `laxR`     | pass through           | (right rule)    |
| `laxL`     | **`◯I`**               | pass through    |

name: PLLND.SC.maehara'
signature:
theorem SC.maehara' {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula} :
    SC Γ C → ∀ Γ₁ Γ₂ : List PLLFormula, Γ.Perm (Γ₁ ++ Γ₂) →
    ∃ I : PLLFormula,
      SC Γ₁ I ∧ SC (I :: Γ₂) C ∧
      I.atoms ⊆ atomsList Γ₁ ∧ I.atoms ⊆ finUnion (atomsList Γ₂) C.atoms
docstring:
**Maehara interpolation** for `SC`, choice-free form: every
permutation-splitting of the context of a derivable sequent has an
interpolant over the shared atoms, the sharing stated as two subset
facts through the choice-free `finUnion`.

name: PLLND.craig_interpolation'
signature:
theorem craig_interpolation' {Γ₁ Γ₂ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula}
    (h : SC (Γ₁ ++ Γ₂) C) :
    ∃ I : PLLFormula,
      SC Γ₁ I ∧ SC (I :: Γ₂) C ∧
      I.atoms ⊆ atomsList Γ₁ ∧ I.atoms ⊆ finUnion (atomsList Γ₂) C.atoms
docstring:
**Craig interpolation for PLL**, sequent form, choice-free: if
`Γ₁ ++ Γ₂ ⊢ C` is derivable then some interpolant `I` has `Γ₁ ⊢ I`,
`I, Γ₂ ⊢ C`, and atoms in `Γ₁`'s and in `Γ₂, C`'s.

name: PLLND.craig_implication'
signature:
theorem craig_implication' {A B : PLLFormula} (h : SC [] (A.ifThen B)) :
    ∃ I : PLLFormula,
      SC [] (A.ifThen I) ∧ SC [] (I.ifThen B) ∧
      I.atoms ⊆ A.atoms ∧ I.atoms ⊆ B.atoms
docstring:
**Craig interpolation for PLL**, implication form, choice-free: if
`⊢ A ⊃ B` then there is an interpolant `I` over the common atoms of `A`
and `B` with `⊢ A ⊃ I` and `⊢ I ⊃ B`.

name: PLLND.SC.maehara
signature:
theorem SC.maehara {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula} :
    SC Γ C → ∀ Γ₁ Γ₂ : List PLLFormula, Γ.Perm (Γ₁ ++ Γ₂) →
    ∃ I : PLLFormula,

**Maehara interpolation** for `SC`: every permutation-splitting of the

name: PLLND.craig_interpolation
signature:
theorem craig_interpolation {Γ₁ Γ₂ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula}
    (h : SC (Γ₁ ++ Γ₂) C) :
    ∃ I : PLLFormula,
      SC Γ₁ I ∧ SC (I :: Γ₂) C ∧

docstring:
**Craig interpolation for PLL**, sequent form: if `Γ₁ ++ Γ₂ ⊢ C` is
derivable then some interpolant `I` has `Γ₁ ⊢ I`, `I, Γ₂ ⊢ C`, and atoms

name: PLLND.craig_implication
signature:
theorem craig_implication {A B : PLLFormula} (h : SC [] (A.ifThen B)) :
    ∃ I : PLLFormula,
      SC [] (A.ifThen I) ∧ SC [] (I.ifThen B) ∧

**Craig interpolation for PLL**, implication form: if `⊢ A ⊃ B` then
there is an interpolant `I` over the common atoms of `A` and `B` with

name: PLLND.Ctx.basic
signature: def basic (K L x : PLLFormula) : PLLFormula
docstring: A basic constraint `[K,L]` acts on `x` as `K ⊃ (x ∨ L)`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.StdCtx
signature: abbrev StdCtx
docstring:
A standard constraint is a finite list of `(K,L)` pairs.  It acts on `x` as the
conjunction `⋀ᵢ (Kᵢ ⊃ (x ∨ Lᵢ))`; the empty list is depth-0 `⊤`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.applyC
signature:
def applyC : StdCtx → PLLFormula → PLLFormula
  | [], _ => truePLL
  | (K, L) :: rest, x => (basic K L x).and (applyC rest x)
docstring: `C[x]` — the standard constraint `C` applied to `x`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.subC
signature:
def subC (C : StdCtx) : PLLFormula → PLLFormula
  | .prop a     => .prop a
  | .falsePLL   => .falsePLL
  | .and φ ψ    => .and (subC C φ) (subC C ψ)
  | .or φ ψ     => .or (subC C φ) (subC C ψ)
  | .ifThen φ ψ => .ifThen (subC C φ) (subC C ψ)
  | .somehow φ  => applyC C (subC C φ)
docstring: The constraint substitution `φ^C`: replace every `◯ψ` by `C[ψ^C]`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.truePLL_intro
signature: def truePLL_intro (Δ : List PLLFormula) : LaxND Δ truePLL
docstring: `⊤` is derivable in any context.

name: PLLND.Ctx.unitC
signature:
def unitC (C : StdCtx) {Δ : List PLLFormula} {A : PLLFormula}
    (p : LaxND Δ A) : LaxND Δ (applyC C A)
docstring: **Unit** `A ⊢ C[A]`: the translation of `◯I`.  (Paper's `C_I`.)

name: PLLND.Ctx.bindC
docstring:
**Bind** `Γ ⊢ C[A]`, `A::Γ ⊢ C[B]`  ⟹  `Γ ⊢ C[B]`: the translation of `◯E`.
For a conjunction of basic constraints the bind is componentwise.

name: PLLND.Ctx.translate
signature:
def translate (C : StdCtx) : {Γ : List PLLFormula} → {φ : PLLFormula} →
    LaxND Γ φ → LaxND (Γ.map (subC C)) (subC C φ)
  | _, _, .iden h        => .iden (List.mem_map_of_mem h)
  | _, _, .falsoElim φ p => .falsoElim (subC C φ) (translate C p)
  | _, _, .impIntro p    => .impIntro (translate C p)
  | _, _, .impElim p₁ p₂ => .impElim (translate C p₁) (translate C p₂)
  | _, _, .andIntro p₁ p₂ => .andIntro (translate C p₁) (translate C p₂)
  | _, _, .andElim1 p    => .andElim1 (translate C p)
  | _, _, .andElim2 p    => .andElim2 (translate C p)
  | _, _, .orIntro1 p    => .orIntro1 (translate C p)
  | _, _, .orIntro2 p    => .orIntro2 (translate C p)
  | _, _, .orElim p₀ p₁ p₂ => .orElim (translate C p₀) (translate C p₁) (translate C p₂)
  | _, _, .laxIntro p    => unitC C (translate C p)
  | _, _, .laxElim p₁ p₂ => bindC C (translate C p₁) (translate C p₂)
docstring:
**Theorem 6, soundness direction (sequent form).**  Every standard constraint
`C` gives a sound interpretation of PLL in IPL: a PLL derivation `Γ ⊢ φ` translates
to an IPL derivation `Γ^C ⊢ φ^C`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.thm6_soundness
signature:
theorem thm6_soundness (C : StdCtx) {φ : PLLFormula}
    (h : Nonempty (LaxND [] φ)) : Nonempty (LaxND [] (subC C φ))
docstring:
**Theorem 6, soundness direction (closed form).**  If `PLL ⊢ φ` then
`IPL ⊢ φ^C` for every standard constraint `C`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.not_provable_of_subC
signature:
theorem not_provable_of_subC (C : StdCtx) {φ : PLLFormula}
    (h : ¬ Nonempty (LaxND [] (subC C φ))) : ¬ Nonempty (LaxND [] φ)
docstring:
Contrapositive, the form used to refute PLL-entailments: if some standard
constraint `C` makes `φ^C` IPL-**un**provable, then `φ` is not a PLL theorem.

name: PLLND.Ctx.CtxIsIPL
signature: def CtxIsIPL (C : StdCtx) : Prop
docstring: A standard constraint is IPL when all its `K,L` are `◯`-free.

name: PLLND.Ctx.applyC_isIPL
signature:
theorem applyC_isIPL {C : StdCtx} (hC : CtxIsIPL C) {x : PLLFormula}
    (hx : isIPL x) : isIPL (applyC C x)

name: PLLND.Ctx.subC_isIPL
signature:
theorem subC_isIPL {C : StdCtx} (hC : CtxIsIPL C) : ∀ φ, isIPL (subC C φ)
  | .prop _     => trivial
  | .falsePLL   => trivial
  | .and φ ψ    => ⟨subC_isIPL hC φ, subC_isIPL hC ψ⟩
  | .or φ ψ     => ⟨subC_isIPL hC φ, subC_isIPL hC ψ⟩
  | .ifThen φ ψ => ⟨subC_isIPL hC φ, subC_isIPL hC ψ⟩
  | .somehow φ  => applyC_isIPL hC (subC_isIPL hC φ)
docstring: If every `K,L` in `C` is `◯`-free, then `φ^C` is `◯`-free for every `φ`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.exists_min_strict
signature:
theorem exists_min_strict {W : Type} [Finite W] (R : W → W → Prop)
    (hrefl : ∀ x, R x x) (htrans : ∀ {a b c}, R a b → R b c → R a c)
    (S : Set W) (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    ∃ m ∈ S, ∀ x ∈ S, R x m → R m x
docstring:
In a finite preorder, every nonempty set has an `R`-minimal *cluster*
element: some `m ∈ S` with no element of `S` strictly below it.

name: PLLND.Ctx.exists_max_cluster
signature:
theorem exists_max_cluster {W : Type} [Finite W] (R : W → W → Prop)
    (hrefl : ∀ x, R x x) (htrans : ∀ {a b c}, R a b → R b c → R a c) (v : W) :
    ∃ u, R v u ∧ ∀ t, R u t → R t u
docstring: From any `v`, a maximal cluster is reachable: `∃ u, R v u ∧ ∀ t, R u t → R t u`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.exists_cover
signature:
theorem exists_cover {W : Type} [Finite W] (R : W → W → Prop)
    (hrefl : ∀ x, R x x) (htrans : ∀ {a b c}, R a b → R b c → R a c)
    (u v : W) (huv : R u v) (hvu : ¬ R v u) :
    ∃ u', (R u u' ∧ ¬ R u' u ∧ ∀ t, R u t → R t u' → R t u ∨ R u' t) ∧ R u' v
docstring:
A strict `R`-step `R u v`, `¬ R v u` factors through a *cover* of `u`: an
immediate strict successor `u'` (in the cluster sense) with `R u' v`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.atoms
signature:
def atoms : PLLFormula → Finset String
  | .prop a     => {a}
  | .falsePLL   => ∅
  | .and φ ψ    => atoms φ ∪ atoms ψ
  | .or φ ψ     => atoms φ ∪ atoms ψ
  | .ifThen φ ψ => atoms φ ∪ atoms ψ
  | .somehow φ  => atoms φ
docstring: The propositional atoms occurring in a formula.

name: PLLND.Ctx.exists_freshNames
signature:
theorem exists_freshNames (M : ConstraintModel) [Finite M.W] (A : Finset String) :
    ∃ f : M.W → String, Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ w, f w ∉ A
docstring:
A finite type admits an injective naming by strings avoiding any given finite
set — the fresh atoms `α_w` of the completion.

name: PLLND.Ctx.nm
signature: noncomputable def nm : M.W → String
docstring: The fresh naming `α_·` for the completion, avoiding `atoms φ₀`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.nm_inj
signature: theorem nm_inj : Function.Injective (nm M φ₀)

name: PLLND.Ctx.nm_fresh
signature: theorem nm_fresh (w : M.W) : nm M φ₀ w ∉ atoms φ₀

name: PLLND.Ctx.Vstar
signature: noncomputable def Vstar : String → Set M.W
docstring:
Valuation of the completion: at fresh names `nm w`, force `{x | Ri w x} ∪ F`
(the up-set of `w`, closed under `F` for fullness); elsewhere unchanged.

name: PLLND.Ctx.Vstar_name
signature:
theorem Vstar_name (w : M.W) :
    Vstar M φ₀ (nm M φ₀ w) = {x | M.Ri w x ∨ x ∈ M.F}

name: PLLND.Ctx.Vstar_eq_of_not_range
signature:
theorem Vstar_eq_of_not_range {a : String} (h : ¬ ∃ w, nm M φ₀ w = a) :
    Vstar M φ₀ a = M.V a

name: PLLND.Ctx.Vstar_hered
signature:
theorem Vstar_hered : ∀ {a : String} {x y : M.W},
    M.Ri x y → x ∈ Vstar M φ₀ a → y ∈ Vstar M φ₀ a

name: PLLND.Ctx.Vstar_full
signature: theorem Vstar_full : ∀ {a : String} {x : M.W}, x ∈ M.F → x ∈ Vstar M φ₀ a

name: PLLND.Ctx.Mstar
signature: noncomputable def Mstar : ConstraintModel
docstring: The semantic completion `M*`: `M` with the enriched valuation.

name: PLLND.Ctx.Mstar_W
signature: @[simp] theorem Mstar_W : (Mstar M φ₀).W = M.W

name: PLLND.Ctx.Mstar_Ri
signature: @[simp] theorem Mstar_Ri : (Mstar M φ₀).Ri = M.Ri

name: PLLND.Ctx.Mstar_Rm
signature: @[simp] theorem Mstar_Rm : (Mstar M φ₀).Rm = M.Rm

name: PLLND.Ctx.Mstar_F
signature: @[simp] theorem Mstar_F : (Mstar M φ₀).F = M.F

name: PLLND.Ctx.alpha
signature: noncomputable def alpha (w : M.W) : PLLFormula
docstring: The fresh propositional variable `α_w`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.force_alpha
signature:
theorem force_alpha (w x : M.W) :
    (Mstar M φ₀).force x (alpha M φ₀ w) ↔ M.Ri w x ∨ x ∈ M.F
docstring:
Characterisation of `α_w` in `M*` (`property (a)`): forced at `x` iff `Ri w x`
(or `x` fallible).

name: PLLND.Ctx.force_coincide
signature:
theorem force_coincide : ∀ (ψ : PLLFormula), (∀ w, nm M φ₀ w ∉ atoms ψ) →
    ∀ (x : M.W), ((Mstar M φ₀).force x ψ ↔ M.force x ψ)
docstring:
Coincidence (`property (b)`): `M*` agrees with `M` on any formula whose atoms
avoid the fresh names — in particular on `φ₀` and its subformulas.

name: PLLND.force_applyC_iff
signature:
theorem force_applyC_iff (D : ConstraintModel) (C : StdCtx) (x : PLLFormula)
    (w : D.W) :
    D.force w (applyC C x) ↔ ∀ p ∈ C, D.force w (basic p.1 p.2 x)
docstring:
Forcing of a constraint conjunction `C[x]` is the conjunction of the basic
constraints, over any model.

name: PLLND.bigOr
signature:
def bigOr : List PLLFormula → PLLFormula
  | []       => .falsePLL
  | q :: rest => q.or (bigOr rest)
docstring: Finite disjunction of a list of formulas (empty = `⊥`).

name: PLLND.force_bigOr_iff
signature:
theorem force_bigOr_iff (D : ConstraintModel) (L : List PLLFormula) (w : D.W) :
    D.force w (bigOr L) ↔ (∃ q ∈ L, D.force w q) ∨ w ∈ D.F
docstring:
Forcing of `bigOr L`: some disjunct is forced, or the world is fallible
(the empty disjunction `⊥` is still forced at fallible worlds).

name: PLLND.Stab
signature: def Stab (u : M.W) : Prop
docstring:
A world is **stable** if it is `Rm`-maximal *up to cluster*: every `Rm`-successor
maps back.  (Preorder-correct form of the paper's "no proper modal successor".)

name: PLLND.iSucc
signature: def iSucc (u v : M.W) : Prop
docstring:
`v` is an **immediate successor** (cover) of `u`: strictly `Ri`-above with
nothing strictly in between (up to cluster).

name: PLLND.Ldis
signature: noncomputable def Ldis (u : M.W) : PLLFormula
docstring: The disjunction `⋁_{u'∈iSucc u} α_{u'}` (empty = `⊥`).

name: PLLND.C0
signature: noncomputable def C0 : StdCtx
docstring: The single standard constraint `C = ⨅_{u∈Stab} [α_u , ⋁_{u'∈iSucc u} α_{u'}]`.

name: PLLND.force_Ldis
signature:
theorem force_Ldis (u w : M.W) :
    (Mstar M φ₀).force w (Ldis M φ₀ u) ↔
      (∃ u', iSucc M u u' ∧ (Mstar M φ₀).force w (alpha M φ₀ u')) ∨ w ∈ M.F
docstring: Forcing of `Ldis u` in `M*`: some cover's variable is forced, or fallible.

name: PLLND.force_applyC_C0
signature:
theorem force_applyC_C0 (ψ : PLLFormula) (w : M.W) :
    (Mstar M φ₀).force w (applyC (C0 M φ₀) ψ) ↔
      ∀ u, Stab M u →
        (Mstar M φ₀).force w (basic (alpha M φ₀ u) (Ldis M φ₀ u) ψ)
docstring: Forcing of `C[ψ]` in `M*`, unfolded over stable worlds.

name: PLLND.lemma7
signature:
theorem lemma7 (ψ : PLLFormula) (w : M.W) :
    (Mstar M φ₀).force w (.somehow ψ) ↔
      (Mstar M φ₀).force w (applyC (C0 M φ₀) ψ)
docstring:
**Lemma 7.**  Over the completion `M*`, the modality `◯ψ` is forced exactly
where the single standard constraint `C0` applied to `ψ` is forced.  Uses only
finiteness (reachable maximal cluster + cover factorization), no antisymmetry.

name: PLLND.force_subC_C0
signature:
theorem force_subC_C0 : ∀ (ψ : PLLFormula) (w : M.W),
    (Mstar M φ₀).force w (subC (C0 M φ₀) ψ) ↔ (Mstar M φ₀).force w ψ
docstring:
**Congruence under uniform `◯`-replacement.**  Substituting `C0[·]` for every
`◯` (i.e. `subC (C0 M φ₀)`) preserves forcing in `M*` — structural induction with
Lemma 7 at each `◯`.

name: thm6_completeness
signature:
theorem thm6_completeness {φ : PLLFormula}
    (h : ∀ C : StdCtx, Nonempty (LaxND [] (subC C φ))) : Nonempty (LaxND [] φ)
docstring:
**Theorem 6, completeness direction.**  If every standard-constraint expansion
`φ^C` is IPL-provable, then `φ` is a PLL theorem.  (Contrapositive: a finite
countermodel `M ⊭ φ`, completed to `M*`, refutes the single constraint `C0`, and
`subC C0 φ` being `◯`-free this is an IPL refutation.)

name: thm6
signature:
theorem thm6 {φ : PLLFormula} :
    Nonempty (LaxND [] φ) ↔ ∀ C : StdCtx, Nonempty (LaxND [] (subC C φ))
docstring:
**Theorem 6** (full context-completeness).  `PLL ⊢ φ` iff every standard
constraint expansion `φ^C` is IPL-provable.  (`subC C φ` is `◯`-free when `C`'s
`K,L` are — `subC_isIPL` — so `Nonempty (LaxND [] (subC C φ))` is genuine IPL
provability via `conservativity`; the witness `C0` built in the completeness proof
has propositional `K,L`, so `CtxIsIPL (C0 M φ)` holds.)

name: PLLND.Ctx.pname
signature: noncomputable def pname : ℕ → String
docstring: Distinct propositional names `p₁, p₂, …` (an injective `ℕ ↪ String`).

name: PLLND.Ctx.pname_inj
signature: theorem pname_inj : Function.Injective pname

name: PLLND.Ctx.pvar
signature: noncomputable def pvar (i : ℕ) : PLLFormula
docstring: The propositional variable `p_i`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.chi
signature:
noncomputable def chi : ℕ → PLLFormula
  | 0     => .somehow .falsePLL
  | (m+1) => .somehow (.ifThen (.somehow (pvar (m+1))) (.or (pvar (m+1)) (chi m)))
docstring: The characteristic schemes `χ_m` (Fairtlough–Mendler p. 12).

name: PLLND.Ctx.step
signature: inductive step of `M_m ⊭ χ_m` is a shift-by-2 bisimulation. -/

name: PLLND.Ctx.Rmrel
signature: def Rmrel (a b : ℕ) : Prop
docstring:
Modal accessibility of `M_k`: the diagonal together with the "odd ↦ successor"
edges `2j+1 ⊑ₘ 2j+2`.  (`a % 2 = 1` keeps everything in linear-arithmetic range,
so `omega` handles all the modal bookkeeping.)

name: PLLND.Ctx.Vval
signature: noncomputable def Vval (k : ℕ) : String → Set ℕ
docstring:
Valuation of `M_k`: `p_i` holds at world `j` iff `2k+2 ≤ j + 2i`
(equivalently `j ≥ 2(k+1-i)`; written additively to stay on ℕ).  Paper:
`V(2r)=V(2r+1)={p_{k-r+1},…,p_k}`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.Mmod
signature:
@[reducible] noncomputable def Mmod (k : ℕ) : ConstraintModel where
  W
docstring:
The linear constraint model `M_k`: carrier `ℕ`, `⊑ᵢ = ≤`, `⊑ₘ = Rmrel`,
no fallible worlds, valuation `Vval k`.  Marked `@[reducible]` so that the world
type `(Mmod k).W` is transparently `ℕ` for instance resolution and `omega`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.force_pvar
signature:
theorem force_pvar (k i j : ℕ) :
    (Mmod k).force j (pvar i) ↔ 2 * k + 2 ≤ j + 2 * i
docstring: Valuation characterisation: `p_i` is forced at `j` in `M_k` iff `2k+2 ≤ j+2i`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.Rm_zero
signature: theorem Rm_zero {u : ℕ} (h : Rmrel 0 u) : u = 0
docstring: `0` has no proper modal successor: `0 ⊑ₘ u` forces `u = 0`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.force_box_pvar
signature:
theorem force_box_pvar (m : ℕ) :
    (Mmod (m+1)).force 1 (.somehow (pvar (m+1)))
docstring:
`1 ⊨ ◯p_{m+1}` in `M_{m+1}`: from every `v ≥ 1` a world forcing `p_{m+1}`
(i.e. a world `≥ 2`) is `⊑ₘ`-reachable.

name: PLLND.Ctx.bisim
signature:
theorem bisim (m : ℕ) (φ : PLLFormula) :
    ∀ t : ℕ, (Mmod (m+1)).force (t+2) φ ↔ (Mmod m).force t φ
docstring:
**Suffix isomorphism as a shift-by-2 bisimulation.**  `M_{m+1}` at world `t+2`
forces exactly what `M_m` forces at world `t`.  (The suffix of `M_{m+1}` starting at
`2` is `M_m`.)

name: PLLND.Ctx.chi_not_forced
signature: theorem chi_not_forced : ∀ m, ¬ (Mmod m).force 0 (chi m)
docstring: `M_m ⊭ χ_m` at world `0`, by induction on `m` (Fairtlough–Mendler p. 13).

name: PLLND.Ctx.lemma9
signature: theorem lemma9 (m : ℕ) : ¬ Nonempty (LaxND [] (chi m))
docstring: **Lemma 9.**  `χ_m` is refuted by the model `M_m`, hence is not a PLL theorem.

name: PLLND.Ctx.subC_chi_succ
signature:
theorem subC_chi_succ (C : StdCtx) (m : ℕ) :
    subC C (chi (m+1)) =
      applyC C (.ifThen (applyC C (pvar (m+1)))
        (.or (pvar (m+1)) (subC C (chi m))))
docstring: One-step unfolding of `subC C (χ_{m+1})`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.force_subC_drop
signature:
theorem force_subC_drop (D : ConstraintModel) (K L : PLLFormula) (s t : StdCtx)
    (u : D.W) (hL : ∀ x, D.Ri u x → D.force x L) :
    ∀ (φ : PLLFormula) (v : D.W), D.Ri u v →
      (D.force v (subC (s ++ (K, L) :: t) φ) ↔ D.force v (subC (s ++ t) φ))
docstring:
**Substitution-drop congruence.**  If `L` is hereditarily forced from `u`, then
the constraint `[K,L]` is vacuous there, so `subC (s ++ (K,L) :: t) φ` and
`subC (s ++ t) φ` are forced at exactly the same worlds `≥ u`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.lemma8_valid
signature:
theorem lemma8_valid : ∀ (m : ℕ) (C : StdCtx), C.length ≤ m →
    ∀ (D : ConstraintModel) (w : D.W), D.force w (subC C (chi m))
docstring:
**Lemma 8 (semantic form).**  Every standard constraint `C` of depth `≤ m`
makes `subC C χ_m` valid in every constraint model.

name: PLLND.Ctx.lemma8
signature:
theorem lemma8 (C : StdCtx) (m : ℕ) (h : C.length ≤ m) :
    Nonempty (LaxND [] (subC C (chi m)))
docstring:
**Lemma 8.**  A standard constraint `C` of depth `n` makes `χ_m` (after
expansion `χ_m^C`) an IPL theorem, for every `m ≥ n`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.corollary10
signature:
theorem corollary10 (𝔻 : Finset StdCtx) :
    ∃ φ : PLLFormula,
      (∀ C ∈ 𝔻, Nonempty (LaxND [] (subC C φ))) ∧ ¬ Nonempty (LaxND [] φ)
docstring:
**Corollary 10.**  No finite set of standard constraints is complete for PLL:
for every finite `𝔻 ⊆ 𝕊` there is a formula `φ` — namely `χ_m` with `m` the maximum
depth in `𝔻` — that every `C ∈ 𝔻` expands to an IPL theorem `φ^C`, yet `φ` is not a
PLL theorem.

name: PLLND.Ctx.Cmeet
signature: def Cmeet (C D : StdCtx) : StdCtx
docstring: Meet `C ⊓ D`: componentwise conjunction of actions, i.e. list append.

name: PLLND.Ctx.Cjoin
signature: def Cjoin (C D : StdCtx) : StdCtx
docstring: Join `C ⊔ D` (Def 1): the pairwise product `⨅_{i,j} [K₁ᵢ∧K₂ⱼ, L₁ᵢ∨L₂ⱼ]`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.Ctop

name: PLLND.Ctx.Cbot
signature: def Cbot : StdCtx

name: PLLND.Ctx.Cle

name: PLLND.Ctx.Cequiv
signature: def Cequiv (C D : StdCtx) : Prop
docstring: `C ≡ D`: `C[x] ⊣⊢ D[x]` at every world of every model, for all `x`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.Cle.trans

name: PLLND.Ctx.Cequiv_iff_le

name: PLLND.Ctx.Cle_iff_provable
signature:
theorem Cle_iff_provable (C D : StdCtx) :
    Cle C D ↔ ∀ x, Nonempty (LaxND [] ((applyC C x).ifThen (applyC D x)))
docstring:
**Faithfulness of `Cle`.**  The semantic order coincides with the paper's:
`C ≤ D` iff `C[x] ⊃ D[x]` is IPL-provable for every `x`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.force_basic

theorem force_basic (M : ConstraintModel) (K L x : PLLFormula) (w : M.W) :

name: PLLND.Ctx.force_Cmeet

theorem force_Cmeet (M : ConstraintModel) (C D : StdCtx) (x : PLLFormula) (w : M.W) :

      M.force w (applyC C x) ∧ M.force w (applyC D x)

name: PLLND.Ctx.force_Cjoin

    M.force w (applyC (Cjoin C D) x) ↔
      ∀ p ∈ C, ∀ q ∈ D, M.force w (basic (p.1.and q.1) (p.2.or q.2) x)

name: PLLND.Ctx.unit_sem

theorem unit_sem (M : ConstraintModel) (C : StdCtx) (x : PLLFormula) (w : M.W)

docstring: The monad `unit`, semantically: `x` forces `C[x]` (so `x ⊃ C[x]` is valid).

name: PLLND.Ctx.force_Ctop

**`C ≤ D` iff `C ⊔ D ≡ D`** — the join adjunction, whose hard direction
instantiates `C ≤ D` at the proposition `x ∨ q.2`.

theorem force_Cjoin_left (M : ConstraintModel) (C D E : StdCtx) (x : PLLFormula)

    Cequiv (Cjoin C (Cmeet D E)) (Cmeet (Cjoin C D) (Cjoin C E))

Definition 1": `∀ q ∈ D ++ E` splits into `∀ q ∈ D` and `∀ q ∈ E`.

docstring: Forcing of a single basic constraint `[K,L]`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.Catom
signature: def Catom (L : PLLFormula) : StdCtx
docstring: Disjunctive atom `L = [true, L]` (`L[x] ≡ x ∨ L`).

name: PLLND.Ctx.CatomBar
signature: def CatomBar (L : PLLFormula) : StdCtx
docstring: Its implicational complement `L̄ = [L, false]` (`L̄[x] ≡ L ⊃ x`).

name: PLLND.Ctx.atom_meet_bar
signature:
theorem atom_meet_bar (L : PLLFormula) :
    Cequiv (Cmeet (Catom L) (CatomBar L)) Cbot
docstring: Generators are complemented, part 1: `L ⊓ L̄ ≡ ⊥`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.atom_join_bar
signature:
theorem atom_join_bar (L : PLLFormula) :
    Cequiv (Cjoin (Catom L) (CatomBar L)) Ctop
docstring: Generators are complemented, part 2: `L ⊔ L̄ ≡ ⊤`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.thm2_bounded_distributive_lattice
signature:
theorem thm2_bounded_distributive_lattice :
    (∀ C D, Cequiv (Cmeet C D) (Cmeet D C)) ∧
    (∀ C D E, Cequiv (Cmeet (Cmeet C D) E) (Cmeet C (Cmeet D E))) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cmeet C C) C) ∧
    (∀ C D, Cequiv (Cjoin C D) (Cjoin D C)) ∧
    (∀ C D E, Cequiv (Cjoin (Cjoin C D) E) (Cjoin C (Cjoin D E))) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cjoin C C) C) ∧
    (∀ C D, Cequiv (Cmeet C (Cjoin C D)) C) ∧
    (∀ C D, Cequiv (Cjoin C (Cmeet C D)) C) ∧
    (∀ C D E, Cequiv (Cjoin C (Cmeet D E)) (Cmeet (Cjoin C D) (Cjoin C E))) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cmeet C Ctop) C) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cjoin C Cbot) C) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cmeet C Cbot) Cbot) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cjoin C Ctop) Ctop) ∧
    (∀ L, Cequiv (Cmeet (Catom L) (CatomBar L)) Cbot) ∧
    (∀ L, Cequiv (Cjoin (Catom L) (CatomBar L)) Ctop)

name: PLLND.Ctx.meet_congr
signature:
theorem meet_congr {A A' B B' : StdCtx} (hA : Cequiv A A') (hB : Cequiv B B') :
    Cequiv (Cmeet A B) (Cmeet A' B')
docstring: Meet respects `≈` (immediate, since `(C⊓D)[x] ⊣⊢ C[x] ∧ D[x]`).

name: PLLND.Ctx.join_mono_left
signature:
theorem join_mono_left {A A' B : StdCtx} (h : Cle A A') :
    Cle (Cjoin A B) (Cjoin A' B)
docstring:
**Left-monotonicity of `⊔`.**  `A ≤ A'` gives `A ⊔ B ≤ A' ⊔ B`.  Proof: to certify the
`(p', q)`-conjunct of `(A'⊔B)[x]` at `v`, build `A[x ∨ q.2]` at `v` from the join
hypothesis, transport it along `A ≤ A'`, and read off the `p'`-conjunct.

name: PLLND.Ctx.join_mono_right
signature:
theorem join_mono_right {A B B' : StdCtx} (h : Cle B B') :
    Cle (Cjoin A B) (Cjoin A B')
docstring: Right-monotonicity of `⊔`, by commutativity.

name: PLLND.Ctx.join_mono
signature:
theorem join_mono {A A' B B' : StdCtx} (h1 : Cle A A') (h2 : Cle B B') :
    Cle (Cjoin A B) (Cjoin A' B')
docstring: `⊔` is monotone in both arguments.

name: PLLND.Ctx.join_congr
signature:
theorem join_congr {A A' B B' : StdCtx} (hA : Cequiv A A') (hB : Cequiv B B') :
    Cequiv (Cjoin A B) (Cjoin A' B')
docstring: **`⊔` respects `≈`** — the congruence the complement induction rewrites with.

name: PLLND.Ctx.join_lub
signature:
theorem join_lub {C D E : StdCtx} (h1 : Cle C E) (h2 : Cle D E) :
    Cle (Cjoin C D) E
docstring: **Least-upper-bound property of `⊔`.**  `C ≤ E`, `D ≤ E` ⟹ `C ⊔ D ≤ E`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.meet_join_distrib
signature:
theorem meet_join_distrib (A B C : StdCtx) :
    Cequiv (Cmeet A (Cjoin B C)) (Cjoin (Cmeet A B) (Cmeet A C))
docstring:
**Meet distributes over join** `A ⊓ (B ⊔ C) ≡ (A⊓B) ⊔ (A⊓C)` — the second
distributive law (the dual `join_meet_distrib` is already proved).  Direct from
Definition 1: every conjunct of the right-hand join is a monotone weakening of a conjunct
supplied by `A[x]` (when its index lies in `A`) or by `(B⊔C)[x]` (indices in `B×C`).

name: PLLND.Ctx.basicBar
signature: def basicBar (p : PLLFormula × PLLFormula) : StdCtx
docstring:
Complement of a single basic constraint: `[K,L]‾ = [⊤,K] ⊓ [L,⊥]`, the 2-basic
standard constraint `[(⊤,K),(L,⊥)]` (De Morgan applied to `[K,L] = [K,⊥] ⊔ [⊤,L]`).

name: PLLND.Ctx.Cbar
signature:
def Cbar : StdCtx → StdCtx
  | []        => Cbot
  | p :: rest => Cjoin (basicBar p) (Cbar rest)
docstring:
The complement `C̄` of a standard constraint `C = ⨅ᵢ [Kᵢ,Lᵢ]`: the finite join
`⨆ᵢ [Kᵢ,Lᵢ]‾` (`foldr ⊔ ⊥`).  A join of standard constraints, hence standard.

name: PLLND.Ctx.single_meet_bar
signature:
theorem single_meet_bar (p : PLLFormula × PLLFormula) :
    Cequiv (Cmeet [p] (basicBar p)) Cbot
docstring:
**Single-basic complement, meet law:** `[K,L] ⊓ [K,L]‾ ≡ ⊥`.  Semantically, the three
conjuncts `K⊃(x∨L)`, `⊤⊃(x∨K)`, `L⊃(x∨⊥)` force `x` outright (chase `x∨K`, then `x∨L`,
then `x∨⊥`), and conversely `x` forces each.

name: PLLND.Ctx.single_join_bar
signature:
theorem single_join_bar (p : PLLFormula × PLLFormula) :
    Cequiv (Cjoin [p] (basicBar p)) Ctop
docstring:
**Single-basic complement, join law:** `[K,L] ⊔ [K,L]‾ ≡ ⊤`.  Every pairwise conjunct
`(K∧⊤)⊃(x∨L∨K)` and `(K∧L)⊃(x∨L∨⊥)` is a tautology (the antecedent supplies `K`, resp.
`L`, already among the disjuncts), so the join acts as `⊤`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.compl_inf_le
signature: theorem compl_inf_le (C : StdCtx) : Cle (Cmeet C (Cbar C)) Cbot
docstring:
`C ⊓ C̄ ≤ ⊥` by induction on `C`.  For `C = [p] ⊓ R` with `C̄ = p̄ ⊔ R̄`, distribute the
meet over the join and bound each summand: `([p]⊓R)⊓p̄ ≤ [p]⊓p̄ ≡ ⊥` (single-basic law) and
`([p]⊓R)⊓R̄ ≤ R⊓R̄ ≡ ⊥` (induction hypothesis).

name: PLLND.Ctx.compl_inf
signature: theorem compl_inf (C : StdCtx) : Cequiv (Cmeet C (Cbar C)) Cbot
docstring: **Complement law (meet):** `C ⊓ C̄ ≡ ⊥`.  With `⊥ ≤ C ⊓ C̄` always (`bot_le`).

name: PLLND.Ctx.compl_sup_ge
signature: theorem compl_sup_ge (C : StdCtx) : Cle Ctop (Cjoin C (Cbar C))
docstring:
`⊤ ≤ C ⊔ C̄` by induction on `C`.  For `C = [p] ⊓ R` with `C̄ = p̄ ⊔ R̄`, commute and
distribute the join over the meet: `⊤ ≡ [p]⊔p̄ ≤ (p̄⊔R̄)⊔[p]` (single-basic law) and
`⊤ ≡ R⊔R̄ ≤ (p̄⊔R̄)⊔R` (induction hypothesis) bound the two meet factors.

name: PLLND.Ctx.compl_sup
signature: theorem compl_sup (C : StdCtx) : Cequiv (Cjoin C (Cbar C)) Ctop
docstring: **Complement law (join):** `C ⊔ C̄ ≡ ⊤`.  With `C ⊔ C̄ ≤ ⊤` always (`le_top`).

name: PLLND.Ctx.thm2_boolean_algebra
signature:
theorem thm2_boolean_algebra :
    -- bounded distributive lattice (both distributive laws)
    (∀ C D, Cequiv (Cmeet C D) (Cmeet D C)) ∧
    (∀ C D E, Cequiv (Cmeet (Cmeet C D) E) (Cmeet C (Cmeet D E))) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cmeet C C) C) ∧
    (∀ C D, Cequiv (Cjoin C D) (Cjoin D C)) ∧
    (∀ C D E, Cequiv (Cjoin (Cjoin C D) E) (Cjoin C (Cjoin D E))) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cjoin C C) C) ∧
    (∀ C D, Cequiv (Cmeet C (Cjoin C D)) C) ∧
    (∀ C D, Cequiv (Cjoin C (Cmeet C D)) C) ∧
    (∀ C D E, Cequiv (Cjoin C (Cmeet D E)) (Cmeet (Cjoin C D) (Cjoin C E))) ∧
    (∀ C D E, Cequiv (Cmeet C (Cjoin D E)) (Cjoin (Cmeet C D) (Cmeet C E))) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cmeet C Ctop) C) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cjoin C Cbot) C) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cmeet C Cbot) Cbot) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cjoin C Ctop) Ctop) ∧
    -- Boolean complement: every `C` is complemented by `Cbar C`
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cmeet C (Cbar C)) Cbot) ∧
    (∀ C, Cequiv (Cjoin C (Cbar C)) Ctop)
docstring:
**Theorem 2 (Fairtlough–Mendler, TYPES 2000, §3).**  The standard constraints `𝕊`,
ordered by `Cle` modulo `Cequiv`, form a **Boolean algebra**: a bounded distributive
lattice (meet `⊓`, join `⊔`, bounds `⊥ ≤ · ≤ ⊤`, *both* distributive laws) in which every
`C` has a complement `C̄ = Cbar C ∈ 𝕊` satisfying `C ⊓ C̄ ≡ ⊥` and `C ⊔ C̄ ≡ ⊤`.

`𝕊` carries only *finitary* meets and joins (`Cmeet`, `Cjoin` are binary), so this is an
**incomplete** Boolean algebra — the intended result: the *complete* Boolean algebras are
the fixpoints of the assembly tower, whereas the syntactic constraint algebra is finitary.
The complement `Cbar` avoids the paper's `2^|I|` powerset normal form (it is a `foldr ⊔ ⊥`
of the 2-basic De Morgan duals `[Kᵢ,Lᵢ]‾ = [⊤,Kᵢ] ⊓ [Lᵢ,⊥]`), yet agrees with it up to `≈`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.compl_unique
signature:
theorem compl_unique {C B : StdCtx} (hm : Cequiv (Cmeet C B) Cbot)
    (hj : Cequiv (Cjoin C B) Ctop) : Cequiv B (Cbar C)
docstring: **Complements are unique.**  Any `B` with `C ⊓ B ≡ ⊥` and `C ⊔ B ≡ ⊤` equals `Cbar C`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.compl_congr
signature: theorem compl_congr {C C' : StdCtx} (h : Cequiv C C') : Cequiv (Cbar C) (Cbar C')
docstring:
**`Cbar` respects `≈`.**  `C ≡ C'` ⟹ `C̄ ≡ C̄'` (the complement is well-defined on
`𝕊/≈`): `C̄'` also complements `C` by transporting the two laws along `C ≡ C'`.

name: PLLND.Ctx.stdSetoid
signature:
def stdSetoid : Setoid StdCtx where
  r
docstring: Constraint-equivalence `≈` as a `Setoid` on standard constraints.

name: PLLND.Ctx.CQuot
signature: def CQuot : Type
docstring: The constraint algebra `𝕊 = StdCtx / ≈`, carrying the Boolean-algebra instance below.

name: PLLND.Ctx.CQuot.mk

docstring:

strictly below the conclusion in the Dershowitz–Manna order on weight
multisets.  Case sweep matching `succs_sound`, each case exhibiting the
`X/Y/Z` decomposition; the only arithmetic is Dyckhoff's weight bookkeeping
(`weight_pos` + `omega`).

name: PLLND.G4.decBAll
signature:
private def decBAll {α : Type _} (p : α → Prop) :
    (l : List α) → (∀ x ∈ l, Decidable (p x)) → Decidable (∀ x ∈ l, p x)
  | [], _ => isTrue fun _ hx => nomatch hx
  | a :: l, h =>
      match h a (.head _), decBAll p l (fun x hx => h x (.tail _ hx)) with
      | isTrue ha, isTrue hl => isTrue (by
          intro x hx
          rcases List.mem_cons.mp hx with rfl | hx
          · exact ha
          · exact hl x hx)
      | isFalse ha, _ => isFalse fun H => ha (H a (.head _))
      | _, isFalse hl => isFalse fun H => hl fun x hx => H x (.tail _ hx)
docstring:
Dependent bounded-∀ decidability: decide `∀ x ∈ l, p x` from
deciders available only for members.

name: PLLND.G4.decBEx
signature:
private def decBEx {α : Type _} (p : α → Prop) :
    (l : List α) → (∀ x ∈ l, Decidable (p x)) → Decidable (∃ x ∈ l, p x)
  | [], _ => isFalse fun ⟨_, hx, _⟩ => nomatch hx
  | a :: l, h =>
      match h a (.head _), decBEx p l (fun x hx => h x (.tail _ hx)) with
      | isTrue ha, _ => isTrue ⟨a, .head _, ha⟩
      | isFalse _, isTrue hl =>
          isTrue (hl.imp fun _ ⟨hx, hp⟩ => ⟨.tail _ hx, hp⟩)
      | isFalse ha, isFalse hl => isFalse (by
          rintro ⟨x, hx, hp⟩
          rcases List.mem_cons.mp hx with rfl | hx
          · exact ha hp
          · exact hl ⟨x, hx, hp⟩)
docstring: Dependent bounded-∃ decidability.

name: PLLND.BeliefReal.Pca
signature:
structure Pca where
  Carrier : Type
  app : Carrier → Carrier → Option Carrier
  pair : Carrier → Carrier → Carrier
  fst : Carrier → Carrier
  snd : Carrier → Carrier
  tag : Bool → Carrier → Carrier
  untag : Carrier → Bool × Carrier
  fst_pair : ∀ a b, fst (pair a b) = a
  snd_pair : ∀ a b, snd (pair a b) = b
  untag_tag : ∀ i a, untag (tag i a) = (i, a)
docstring:
A partial applicative structure with total pairing and tag decoding.
Application is partial (`Option`); `untag` is **total** — every element decodes
as a tagged value (as in Kleene's first algebra under Cantor pairing).  No
combinatory laws are required at this stage.

name: PLLND.BeliefReal.Evidence
signature:
structure Evidence (P : Pca) (C : ConstraintModel) where
  E : String → C.W → Set P.Carrier
  hered_E : ∀ {s : String} {w v : C.W}, C.Ri w v → E s w ⊆ E s v
  full_E : ∀ {s : String} {w : C.W}, w ∈ C.F → ∀ x : P.Carrier, x ∈ E s w
docstring:
Evidence over a constraint frame: for each atom and world, the set of
elements evidencing that atom there — hereditary along `Rᵢ` and full on the
fallible worlds.

name: PLLND.BeliefReal.realP
signature:
def realP (P : Pca) {C : ConstraintModel} (Ev : Evidence P C) (κ : C.W → P.Carrier) :
    PLLFormula → P.Carrier → C.W → Prop
  | .prop s, x, w => w ∈ C.F ∨ x ∈ Ev.E s w
  | .falsePLL, _x, w => w ∈ C.F
  | .and φ ψ, x, w =>
      w ∈ C.F ∨ (realP P Ev κ φ (P.fst x) w ∧ realP P Ev κ ψ (P.snd x) w)
  | .or φ ψ, x, w =>
      w ∈ C.F ∨ ((P.untag x).1 = false ∧ realP P Ev κ φ (P.untag x).2 w)
             ∨ ((P.untag x).1 = true ∧ realP P Ev κ ψ (P.untag x).2 w)
  | .ifThen φ ψ, x, w =>
      ∀ v, C.Ri w v → v ∈ C.F ∨
        (∀ b, realP P Ev κ φ b v →
          ∃ y, P.app x (P.pair (κ v) b) = some y ∧ realP P Ev κ ψ y v)
  | .somehow φ, x, w =>
      ∀ v, C.Ri w v → v ∈ C.F ∨
        (∃ y, P.app x (κ v) = some y ∧
          ∃ u, C.Rm v u ∧ P.fst y = κ u ∧ realP P Ev κ φ (P.snd y) u)
docstring:
`⊩ᵖ` — **presented-strategy** realisability: `realS` with the one
repair the obstruction demands.  In the `⊃`-clause the realiser is applied
to `pair (κ v) b` — the presented future together with the argument — just
as the `◯`-clause already presents `κ v` to the strategy.

name: PLLEvidence (notation)
signature: scoped notation:50 x:51 " ⊩ᵖ[" Ev ", " κ ", " w "] " φ:51 => realP _ Ev κ φ x w
docstring: `x ⊩ᵖ[Ev, κ, w] φ` — `x` presented-strategy-realises `φ` at `w`.

name: PLLND.BeliefReal.tokenEvidence
docstring:
**Token evidence** on a checked frame: one token per atom, exactly where
the atom holds (fallible worlds evidence everything, as required).

name: PLLND.BeliefReal.realP_adequate_and_full
signature:
theorem realP_adequate_and_full (h : M.WellFormed) (tok : String → P.Carrier)
    (κ : Fin M.n → P.Carrier)
    (htab : ∀ g : Fin M.n → P.Carrier, ∃ s, ∀ i, P.app s (κ i) = some (g i))
    (htabP : ∀ g : Fin M.n → P.Carrier,
      ∃ s, ∀ i b, P.app s (P.pair (κ i) b) = some (g i)) :
    ∀ φ : PLLFormula,
      (∀ (w : Fin M.n) (x : P.Carrier),
        (x ⊩ᵖ[tokenEvidence P M h tok, κ, w] φ) → (M.toModel h).force w φ) ∧
      (∃ wit : Fin M.n → P.Carrier, ∀ w : Fin M.n,
        (M.toModel h).force w φ →
          (wit w) ⊩ᵖ[tokenEvidence P M h tok, κ, w] φ)
docstring:
**Adequacy and fullness for `⊩ᵖ`**, jointly, over any checked frame with
token evidence: realised implies forced, and forced formulas have explicit
realisers given by a per-world witness function.  The construction is
choice-free: all branch decisions are made by the executable `forceB`, and
the `◯`-witness is found by searching the finite frame.

name: PLLND.BeliefReal.realP_refutes_sequent
signature:
theorem realP_refutes_sequent {w : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula}
    {C : PLLFormula} (hcheck : FinCM.checkB M w Γ C = true)
    (tok : String → P.Carrier) (κ : Fin M.n → P.Carrier)
    (htab : ∀ g : Fin M.n → P.Carrier, ∃ s, ∀ i, P.app s (κ i) = some (g i))
    (htabP : ∀ g : Fin M.n → P.Carrier,
      ∃ s, ∀ i b, P.app s (P.pair (κ i) b) = some (g i)) :
    ∃ hwf : M.WellFormed, ∃ hlt : w < M.n,
      (∀ ψ ∈ Γ, ∃ x, x ⊩ᵖ[tokenEvidence P M hwf tok, κ, ⟨w, hlt⟩] ψ) ∧
      ¬ ∃ x, x ⊩ᵖ[tokenEvidence P M hwf tok, κ, ⟨w, hlt⟩] C
docstring:
**The completeness squeeze**: every countermodel validated by the
verified checker is a `⊩ᵖ`-refutation of its sequent — at the refuting
world every hypothesis is realised, and the conclusion is unrealisable.

name: PLLND.BeliefReal.somehow_p_not_p_realP
signature:
theorem somehow_p_not_p_realP (P : Pca) (tok : String → P.Carrier)
    (κ : Fin demoM.n → P.Carrier)
    (htab : ∀ g : Fin demoM.n → P.Carrier,
      ∃ s, ∀ i, P.app s (κ i) = some (g i))
    (htabP : ∀ g : Fin demoM.n → P.Carrier,
      ∃ s, ∀ i b, P.app s (P.pair (κ i) b) = some (g i)) :
    ∃ hwf : demoM.WellFormed, ∃ hlt : 2 < demoM.n,
      (∃ x, x ⊩ᵖ[tokenEvidence P demoM hwf tok, κ, ⟨2, hlt⟩]
        (prop "p").somehow) ∧
      ¬ ∃ x, x ⊩ᵖ[tokenEvidence P demoM hwf tok, κ, ⟨2, hlt⟩] (prop "p")
docstring:
**Flagship instance**: at the pinned emitted countermodel for
`◯p ⊢ p` (`demoM`, `PLLCountermodelEmit.lean`), the hypothesis `◯p` is
`⊩ᵖ`-realised at the refuting world while `p` is unrealisable — the sequent
is realisability-refuted, not merely truth-refuted.  The checker certificate
discharges by `decide`.

signature:
theorem tbl_htab {n : ℕ} (g : Fin n → Tbl) :
    ∃ s, ∀ i, tblPca.app s (tblκ i) = some (g i)
docstring: The table algebra meets the `◯`-witness table hypothesis.

name: PLLND.tbl_htabP
signature:
theorem tbl_htabP {n : ℕ} (g : Fin n → Tbl) :
    ∃ s, ∀ i b, tblPca.app s (tblPca.pair (tblκ i) b) = some (g i)
docstring: …and the `⊃`-witness pair-table hypothesis.

name: PLLND.realP_refutes_sequent_tbl
signature:
theorem realP_refutes_sequent_tbl {M : FinCM} {w : Nat}
    {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula}
    (hcheck : FinCM.checkB M w Γ C = true) :
    ∃ hwf : M.WellFormed, ∃ hlt : w < M.n,
      (∀ ψ ∈ Γ, ∃ x,
        x ⊩ᵖ[tokenEvidence tblPca M hwf (fun _ => Tbl.base 0), tblκ,
          ⟨w, hlt⟩] ψ) ∧
      ¬ ∃ x, x ⊩ᵖ[tokenEvidence tblPca M hwf (fun _ => Tbl.base 0), tblκ,
          ⟨w, hlt⟩] C
docstring:
**The squeeze over the explicit algebra — nothing assumed**: every
countermodel validated by the verified checker is `⊩ᵖ`-refuted over
`tblPca`.

name: PLLND.somehow_p_not_p_realP_tbl
signature:
theorem somehow_p_not_p_realP_tbl :
    ∃ hwf : demoM.WellFormed, ∃ hlt : 2 < demoM.n,
      (∃ x, x ⊩ᵖ[tokenEvidence tblPca demoM hwf (fun _ => Tbl.base 0), tblκ,
        ⟨2, hlt⟩] (prop "p").somehow) ∧
      ¬ ∃ x, x ⊩ᵖ[tokenEvidence tblPca demoM hwf (fun _ => Tbl.base 0), tblκ,
        ⟨2, hlt⟩] (prop "p")
docstring:
**Fully closed flagship**: `◯p ⊢ p` is realisability-refuted — explicit
finite model, explicit evidence, explicit algebra; no hypotheses.

name: PLLND.AlgModel
signature:
structure AlgModel where
  meet : Nat → Nat → Nat
  join : Nat → Nat → Nat
  imp  : Nat → Nat → Nat
  bot  : Nat
  top  : Nat
  box  : Nat → Nat
  elems : List Nat
docstring:
A finite algebraic model: a bounded lattice with `→` and a nucleus
`box`, carried on an explicit list of elements (so valuations can be
enumerated).

name: PLLND.chain3
signature: def chain3 (j : Nat → Nat) : AlgModel
docstring:
The 3-chain `0 < 1 < 2` (Heyting arrow `x ≤ y ↦ 2`), parametrised by
its nucleus.

name: PLLND.diamond
signature: def diamond (j : Nat → Nat) : AlgModel
docstring:
The Boolean diamond `2×2` on bits `{0,1,2,3}` (`meet`/`join` bitwise,
`imp x y = ¬x ∨ y`), parametrised by its nucleus.

name: PLLND.zoo
signature: def zoo : List AlgModel
docstring:
The zoo: four nuclei on the chain, three on the diamond — enough
disagreement to refute most non-theorems in linear time.

name: PLLND.aeval
signature:
def aeval (M : AlgModel) (v : String → Nat) : PLLFormula → Nat
  | .prop s => v s
  | .falsePLL => M.bot
  | .and A B => M.meet (aeval M v A) (aeval M v B)
  | .or A B => M.join (aeval M v A) (aeval M v B)
  | .ifThen A B => M.imp (aeval M v A) (aeval M v B)
  | .somehow A => M.box (aeval M v A)
docstring: Evaluate a formula in a model under a valuation of its atoms.

name: PLLND.vals
signature:
def vals (M : AlgModel) : List String → List (String → Nat)
  | [] => [fun _ => M.bot]
  | a :: as =>
      (vals M as).flatMap (fun v =>
        M.elems.map (fun x => fun s => if s = a then x else v s))
docstring:
All valuations of the given atoms into the model (as functions
`String → Nat`, defaulting unlisted atoms to `bot`).

name: PLLND.leFails
signature: def leFails (atoms : List String) (X Y : PLLFormula) : Nat
docstring:
Count, across every model in the zoo and every valuation of `atoms`,
how often `X ≤ Y` fails semantically.  `0` is necessary (not sufficient)
for `X ⊢ Y`; used as a fast semantic difference test between two
candidate interpolants.

name: PLLND.eqFails
signature: def eqFails (atoms : List String) (X Y : PLLFormula) : Nat × Nat
docstring:
Both directions of `leFails`: `(0, 0)` means "semantically equal over
the zoo", i.e. no model/valuation tested distinguishes `X` and `Y`.

name: PLLND.fsize
signature:
def fsize : PLLFormula → Nat
  | .prop _ => 1
  | .falsePLL => 1
  | .and A B => fsize A + fsize B + 1
  | .or A B => fsize A + fsize B + 1
  | .ifThen A B => fsize A + fsize B + 1
  | .somehow A => fsize A + 1
docstring:
Plain AST node count (distinct from `PLLFormula.weight`, which is
Dyckhoff's proof-theoretic weight) — the size metric the quantifier
probes actually tracked.

name: PLLND.renderCutoff

docstring:
Interpolants can be large; don't dump an unreadable wall of text.
Raise this if you want to see bigger ones.

name: PLLND.showFormula

docstring: Size, and the rendered formula only if it is within `renderCutoff`.

Contexts lifted from `wip/v3probe4.lean`'s v3.1 stress probe (`G0`the

structure ZooInstance where

A named semantic-differencing pair: two formulas plus the atoms to
range valuations over. `eqFails` on them is the payload.

name: PLLND.zooInstances
signature: def zooInstances : List ZooInstance
docstring:
Pairs lifted from `wip/v3probe4.lean`'s headline/regression checks:
each compares the v3 truncated quantifier against the v2 legacy one on
the same context, at the fuel/budget pairing the probe found stable.

name: PLLND.runTiming
signature: def runTiming : IO Unit
docstring:
`laxrun timing` — the standalone delay calculator: the `Tm.eval`
extractions on the `CIRC` (`PLLTiming.lean`) and carry-skip-adder
(`PLLTimingAdder.lean`) proof terms, at the nominal sky130 operating point.

Each printed value is the closed form that the library *proves* equal to
the `Tm.eval` extraction of the corresponding proof term — `circUp_rising`,
`circUp_a1_bound`, `coutSkip_bound`, `ripple_bound` (all `rfl`/`omega`,
kernel-checked at build time) — so these numbers are certified extraction
results.  We evaluate the closed forms rather than calling `Tm.eval` at
runtime because the dependently-typed evaluator (its result type is the
type family `sem`) crashes the v4.22.0-rc3 interpreter with SIGBUS
(erased-type arity confusion; minimal repro: `#eval (circUp.eval (· + ·) 0 B
(envCIRC 120 40 90) (0, ()) (0, ())).1`).  The theory files never hit this
because they pin these numbers by `rfl`/`decide` — kernel reduction, not
the interpreter.  Once a toolchain bump fixes the exe/codegen path, the
`Tm.eval` calls can be restored verbatim here.

name: PLLND.runSearch
signature: def runSearch (args : List String) : IO Unit
docstring:
`laxrun search <instance> <fuel>` — run the `G4c` backward decider
(`PLLG4Dec.search`) on a named sequent with a user-supplied fuel (`W`/`as`
— the space parameters — are computed automatically from the sequent via
`listWeight`/`listAtoms`, exactly as `G4c_iff_search` does; only the fuel
is left for the caller to pick, since `decideFuel`'s automatic bound can
be far more expensive to even compute than the search itself).

name: PLLND.runQuant
signature: def runQuant (args : List String) : IO Unit
docstring:
`laxrun quant <instance>` — evaluate the v3 truncated quantifiers
`itpE`/`itpA` (`PLLG4UITrunc.lean`) and the legacy v2 `interE`/`interA`
(`PLLG4UI.lean`) on a named instance, printing sizes (`fsize`) and, below
`renderCutoff`, the rendered formula.

name: PLLND.runZoo
signature: def runZoo (args : List String) : IO Unit
docstring:
`laxrun zoo <instance>` — the algebra-zoo semantic differencing:
`eqFails` between a named pair of formulas. `(0, 0)` means no model in the
zoo distinguishes them.

name: PLLND.runHelp

docstring: `laxrun help` (and the no-argument default).

theorem le_trans {T₁ T₂ T₃ : FTheory} (h : T₁.le T₂) (h' : T₂.le T₃) :

name: PLLND.FinComp.FTheory.insFal

docstring: Insert into the falsified part.

name: PLLND.FinComp.setDeriv_coe_iff
signature:
theorem setDeriv_coe_iff {V : Finset PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula} :
    (↑V : Set PLLFormula) ⊩ φ ↔ Nonempty (LaxND V.toList φ)
docstring:
Set-derivability from a finset coercion is list-derivability from its
`toList`.

name: PLLND.FinComp.setDerivB
signature: def setDerivB (V : Finset PLLFormula) (φ : PLLFormula) : Bool
docstring:
Set-derivability from a finset coercion, as a Boolean: lift
`decide (Nonempty (Tm l φ))` over any representative list of the
underlying multiset — the value is permutation-invariant because
derivability is stable under renaming, and `decidablePLL` decides each
representative.  Choice-free, unlike the `Finset.toList` route.

name: PLLND.FinComp.setDerivB_iff
signature:
theorem setDerivB_iff (V : Finset PLLFormula) (φ : PLLFormula) :
    setDerivB V φ = true ↔ (↑V : Set PLLFormula) ⊩ φ

name: PLLND.FinComp.cons_iff_check
signature:
theorem cons_iff_check (T : FTheory) :
    T.Cons ↔ (T.fal = ∅ ∧ T.mfal = ∅) ∨
      ¬ (↑T.val : Set PLLFormula) ⊩ disjOf T.fal.toList T.mfal.toList
docstring:
Consistency of a finite triple is a single derivability check on the
full selection (empty selections aside): `disjOf` is monotone, so the full
lists are the worst case.

name: PLLND.FinComp.cons_iff_rep
signature:
theorem cons_iff_rep (T : FTheory) {lf lm : List PLLFormula}
    (hlf : ∀ x, x ∈ lf ↔ x ∈ T.fal) (hlm : ∀ x, x ∈ lm ↔ x ∈ T.mfal) :
    T.Cons ↔ (lf = [] ∧ lm = []) ∨
      ¬ (↑T.val : Set PLLFormula) ⊩ disjOf lf lm
docstring:
The consistency check phrased over *any* lists enumerating `fal`
and `mfal` (membership is all the proof consumes, so duplicates and
order are irrelevant).  This is the choice-free replacement for the
`Finset.toList`-phrased `cons_iff_check`.

name: PLLND.FinComp.bool_eq_of_iff
signature:
private theorem bool_eq_of_iff {a b : Bool} (h : a = true ↔ b = true) :
    a = b

name: PLLND.FinComp.consB
signature: def consB (T : FTheory) : Bool
docstring:
Consistency of a finite triple, as a Boolean — lifted over
representatives of `fal` and `mfal`; permutation-invariance is by
`disjOf_mono` (membership-monotonicity of the consistency formula).

name: PLLND.FinComp.consB_iff
signature: theorem consB_iff (T : FTheory) : consB T = true ↔ T.Cons

name: PLLND.FinComp.cons_insVal_or_insFal
signature:
theorem cons_insVal_or_insFal {T : FTheory} (hT : T.Cons) (φ : PLLFormula) :
    (T.insVal φ).Cons ∨ (T.insFal φ).Cons
docstring:
**The decided extension is safe**: a consistent triple stays consistent
when a formula is added to `val` or, failing that, to `fal` — the finite
mirror of the classical `mem_val_or_mem_fal` combination argument.

name: PLLND.FinComp.extendStep

docstring:
One decided extension step: add `φ` to `val` if that is consistent,
otherwise to `fal` — the decision by the computable, choice-free
consistency check `consB`.

name: PLLND.FinComp.MaxIn
signature: def MaxIn (cl : Finset PLLFormula) (T : FTheory) : Prop
docstring:
Closure-maximality: consistent, inside the closure, and total on it —
every closure formula is validated or falsified.  (This is what the
classical Lemma 4.2 suite actually consumes: extension-failure witnesses
for closure formulas are derivable from totality plus consistency.)

name: PLLND.FinComp.lindenbaum
docstring:
**Constructive Lindenbaum**: every consistent triple inside the closure
extends — by a computable fold of decided steps, no Zorn — to a
closure-maximal one with the *same* promises (`mfal` untouched, as the
truth-lemma constructions require).

docstring: Deductive closure on the closure.

def canonFin (cl : Finset PLLFormula) : ConstraintModel where
  W
docstring:
The finite canonical model over a closure: worlds are the
closure-maximal triples; `Rᵢ` is inclusion on `val`, `Rₘ` inclusion on
`val` and `mfal`; atoms outside the closure hold everywhere (the
filtration's convention, needed for `full_F`).

name: PLLND.FinComp.not_mem_coe_empty
signature:
private theorem not_mem_coe_empty {K : PLLFormula}
    (h : K ∈ (↑(∅ : Finset PLLFormula) : Set PLLFormula)) : False

name: PLLND.FinComp.eq_of_mem_coe_singleton
signature:
private theorem eq_of_mem_coe_singleton {K ψ : PLLFormula}
    (h : K ∈ (↑({ψ} : Finset PLLFormula) : Set PLLFormula)) : K = ψ

name: PLLND.FinComp.truth_lemma
signature:
theorem truth_lemma {cl : Finset PLLFormula} (hcl : SubClosed cl) :
    ∀ (φ : PLLFormula), φ ∈ cl → ∀ T : (canonFin cl).W,
      (φ ∈ T.1.val → (canonFin cl).force T φ) ∧
        (φ ∈ T.1.fal → ¬ (canonFin cl).force T φ)
docstring:
**The truth lemma**, finitely: on the finite canonical model over a
subformula-closed closure, membership in `val` forces and membership in
`fal` refutes — with all three extension steps supplied by the
constructive `lindenbaum`.

name: PLLND.FinComp.clOf

docstring: The subformula closure of a sequent, `⊥` included.

name: PLLND.FinComp.mem_foldr_subF

name: PLLND.FinComp.mem_clOf

name: PLLND.FinComp.clOf_subClosed

name: PLLND.FinComp.finite_canonical_countermodel

    (h : ¬ Nonempty (LaxND Γ C)) :
    ∃ T : (canonFin (clOf Γ C)).W,
      (∀ ψ ∈ Γ, (canonFin (clOf Γ C)).force T ψ) ∧
        ¬ (canonFin (clOf Γ C)).force T C
docstring:
**Countermodel existence, finitely and without Zorn**: every
underivable sequent is refuted at a world of its finite canonical model —
the hypotheses forced, the conclusion not.

name: PLLND.FinComp.wl_get_eq
signature:
