name: PLLND.Tm.subst_var
signature:
theorem Tm.subst_var : ∀ {Γ Δ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula}
    (t : Tm Γ φ) (ρ : Ren Γ Δ), t.subst (fun {_} v => .var (ρ v)) = t.rename ρ
  | _, _, _, .var v, ρ => rfl
  | _, _, _, .abort φ t, ρ => by simp [Tm.subst, Tm.rename, t.subst_var]
  | _, _, _, .lam t, ρ => by
      simp only [Tm.subst, Tm.rename]
      rw [show t.subst (Sub.lift fun {_} v => .var (ρ v))
          = t.subst (fun {_} v => .var (ρ.lift v)) from
        t.subst_congr (by lift_cases), t.subst_var]
  | _, _, _, .app t s, ρ => by
      simp [Tm.subst, Tm.rename, t.subst_var, s.subst_var]
  | _, _, _, .pair t s, ρ => by
      simp [Tm.subst, Tm.rename, t.subst_var, s.subst_var]
  | _, _, _, .fst t, ρ => by simp [Tm.subst, Tm.rename, t.subst_var]
  | _, _, _, .snd t, ρ => by simp [Tm.subst, Tm.rename, t.subst_var]
  | _, _, _, .inl t, ρ => by simp [Tm.subst, Tm.rename, t.subst_var]
  | _, _, _, .inr t, ρ => by simp [Tm.subst, Tm.rename, t.subst_var]
  | _, _, _, .case t u₁ u₂, ρ => by
      simp only [Tm.subst, Tm.rename]
      rw [t.subst_var]
      congr 1
      · rw [show u₁.subst (Sub.lift fun {_} v => .var (ρ v))
            = u₁.subst (fun {_} v => .var (ρ.lift v)) from
          u₁.subst_congr (by lift_cases), u₁.subst_var]
      · rw [show u₂.subst (Sub.lift fun {_} v => .var (ρ v))
            = u₂.subst (fun {_} v => .var (ρ.lift v)) from
          u₂.subst_congr (by lift_cases), u₂.subst_var]
  | _, _, _, .val t, ρ => by simp [Tm.subst, Tm.rename, t.subst_var]
  | _, _, _, .bind t u, ρ => by
      simp only [Tm.subst, Tm.rename]
      rw [t.subst_var]
      congr 1
      rw [show u.subst (Sub.lift fun {_} v => .var (ρ v))
          = u.subst (fun {_} v => .var (ρ.lift v)) from
        u.subst_congr (by lift_cases), u.subst_var]

name: PLLND.certSyntax
signature:
private def certSyntax : {Γ : List PLLFormula} → {C : PLLFormula} →
    G4cTm Γ C → TacticM Term
  | Γ, _, @G4cTm.init _ a _ => do
      `(G4cTm.init $(← memSyntax (.prop a) Γ))
  | Γ, _, .botL _ => do
      `(G4cTm.botL $(← memSyntax .falsePLL Γ))
  | _, _, .andR a b => do
      `(G4cTm.andR $(← certSyntax a) $(← certSyntax b))
  | _, _, .orR1 a => do `(G4cTm.orR1 $(← certSyntax a))
  | _, _, .orR2 a => do `(G4cTm.orR2 $(← certSyntax a))
  | _, _, .impR a => do `(G4cTm.impR $(← certSyntax a))
  | _, _, .laxR a => do `(G4cTm.laxR $(← certSyntax a))
  | Γ, _, @G4cTm.laxL _ A _ _ a => do
      `(G4cTm.laxL $(← memSyntax (.somehow A) Γ) $(← certSyntax a))
  | Γ, _, @G4cTm.andL _ A B _ _ a => do
      `(G4cTm.andL $(← memSyntax (.and A B) Γ) $(← certSyntax a))
  | Γ, _, @G4cTm.orL _ A B _ _ a b => do
      `(G4cTm.orL $(← memSyntax (.or A B) Γ)
        $(← certSyntax a) $(← certSyntax b))
  | Γ, _, @G4cTm.impLProp _ a B _ _ _ t => do
      `(G4cTm.impLProp $(← memSyntax (.ifThen (.prop a) B) Γ)
        $(← memSyntax (.prop a) Γ) $(← certSyntax t))
  | Γ, _, @G4cTm.impLAnd _ A B D _ _ t => do
      `(G4cTm.impLAnd $(← memSyntax (.ifThen (.and A B) D) Γ)
        $(← certSyntax t))
  | Γ, _, @G4cTm.impLOr _ A B D _ _ t => do
      `(G4cTm.impLOr $(← memSyntax (.ifThen (.or A B) D) Γ)
        $(← certSyntax t))
  | Γ, _, @G4cTm.impLImp _ A B D _ _ t₁ t₂ => do
      `(G4cTm.impLImp $(← memSyntax (.ifThen (.ifThen A B) D) Γ)
        $(← certSyntax t₁) $(← certSyntax t₂))
  | Γ, _, @G4cTm.impLLax _ A B _ _ t₁ t₂ => do
      `(G4cTm.impLLax $(← memSyntax (.ifThen (.somehow A) B) Γ)
        $(← certSyntax t₁) $(← certSyntax t₂))
  | Γ, _, @G4cTm.impLLaxLax _ A B X _ _ _ t₁ t₂ => do
      `(G4cTm.impLLaxLax $(← memSyntax (.ifThen (.somehow A) B) Γ)
        $(← memSyntax (.somehow X) Γ)
        $(← certSyntax t₁) $(← certSyntax t₂))
docstring:
Quote a `G4cTm` certificate back into surface syntax.  The quoted
membership proofs pin the principal formulas of the left rules, so
every implicit argument is determined by unification against the
goal.

The gap-sequent derivation, spliced in as a bare G4iLL″ proof
term (for the axiom audit below).

name: unit_nd
signature: theorem unit_nd : Nonempty (LaxND [] (A₀.ifThen A₀.somehow))
docstring:
A named specimen of a `pll_g4c`-produced natural-deduction proof,
for the axiom audit.

name: myCfg
signature: def myCfg : Config

name: PLLND.Search.isTop
signature:
def isTop : PLLFormula → Bool
  | .ifThen .falsePLL .falsePLL => true
  | _ => false
docstring: Is this literally `⊤` (i.e. `⊥ → ⊥`)?

name: PLLND.Search.smash
signature:
def smash : PLLFormula → PLLFormula
  | .and A B =>
      if A == .falsePLL || B == .falsePLL then .falsePLL
      else if isTop A then B else if isTop B then A
      else if A == B then A
      else .and A B
  | .or A B =>
      if isTop A || isTop B then truePLL
      else if A == .falsePLL then B else if B == .falsePLL then A
      else if A == B then A
      else .or A B
  | .ifThen A B =>
      if A == .falsePLL || isTop B then truePLL
      else if isTop A then B
      else if A == B then truePLL
      else .ifThen A B
  | .somehow A =>
      if isTop A then truePLL
      else match A with
        | .somehow B => .somehow B
        | _ => .somehow A
  | F => F
docstring: One layer of PLL-equivalence simplification at the root of a formula.

name: PLLND.Search.nf
signature:
def nf : PLLFormula → PLLFormula
  | .and A B    => smash (.and (nf A) (nf B))
  | .or A B     => smash (.or (nf A) (nf B))
  | .ifThen A B => smash (.ifThen (nf A) (nf B))
  | .somehow A  => smash (.somehow (nf A))
  | F => F
docstring: Recursive normaliser: `smash` applied bottom-up.  A PLL equivalence.

name: PLLND.Search.Frame
signature:
structure Frame where
  /-- Number of worlds; the carrier is `{0, …, n-1}`. -/
  n : Nat
  /-- Strict part of the intuitionistic order `Rᵢ`, transitively closed. -/
  ri : List (Nat × Nat)
  /-- The constraint relation `Rₘ`, a subset of `ri`. -/
  rm : List (Nat × Nat)
  /-- The fallible worlds (they force every formula, `⊥` included). -/
  fall : List Nat
docstring:
A finite intuitionistic-with-fallibility frame, as raw data.  Worlds are
`0, …, n-1`; `ri` lists the *strict* intuitionistic order (assumed
transitively closed, reflexivity added on use); `rm ⊆ ri` is the constraint
relation; `fall` lists the fallible worlds (which force everything).

name: PLLND.Search.defaultFrames
signature: def defaultFrames : List Frame
docstring:
The default battery: ten small frames — the generic shapes that refute
most non-theorems of PLL.  Reading the list: (1) the classical point;
(2) the fallible point; (3) a two-world chain with `Rₘ = Rᵢ`; (4) the same
chain with `Rₘ` empty (a *rigid* modal step); (5) the chain with no
fallible top; (6) a three-world chain, rigid except for the middle step;
(7) the full three-world chain; (8) a four-world fork; (9) a three-world
`V`/branch; (10) a doubled two-world chain.  They are deliberately small
(≤ 4 worlds) and cheap to decorate; a caller who needs more can prepend
their own to `Config.frames`.

name: PLLND.Search.riStep
signature: def riStep (f : Frame) (w v : Nat) : Bool
docstring: Strict `Rᵢ`-edge test on a `Frame`.

name: PLLND.Search.Config
signature:
structure Config where
  /-- Frames used by the countermodel battery.  Defaults to `defaultFrames`;
  prepend your own frames (as extra shapes) to search a wider space. -/
  frames : List Frame
docstring:
Tuning parameters for `decide`.  All fields default, so `({} : Config)`
gives the standard search.

name: PLLND.Search.Config.default
signature: def Config.default : Config
docstring: The standard configuration (all defaults).

name: PLLND.Search.defaultFindBudget
signature: def defaultFindBudget : Nat
docstring:
The default node budget used by the *sequent-first* wrappers of §11 and
by the `#search` / `#refute` commands — comfortably above every sequent in
the cost table of the module header, so it costs a verdict only on searches
that were going to grind.

name: PLLND.Search.budgetedConfig
signature: def budgetedConfig : Config
docstring:
The configuration used by the sequent-first wrappers and the
`#search` / `#refute` commands: the standard search with the node budget
**on** at `defaultFindBudget`.  Pass `{ findBudget := none }` (or
`Config.default`) to turn the budget off again.

name: PLLND.Search.riR
signature: def riR (M : FinCM) (w v : Nat) : Bool
docstring: Reflexive `Rᵢ` test on a `FinCM`.

name: PLLND.Search.rmR
signature: def rmR (M : FinCM) (w v : Nat) : Bool
docstring: Reflexive `Rₘ` test on a `FinCM`.

name: PLLND.Search.forceV
signature:
def forceV (M : FinCM) : PLLFormula → Array Bool
  | .prop a => (Array.range M.n).map fun w =>
      decide ((w, a) ∈ M.val) || decide (w ∈ M.fall)
  | .falsePLL => (Array.range M.n).map fun w => decide (w ∈ M.fall)
  | .and A B =>
      let vA
docstring:
Forcing as a world-indexed Boolean vector.  Each entry `w` says whether
world `w` forces the formula; fallible worlds force everything.  This mirrors
`FinCM.forceB` but computes each subformula once.

name: PLLND.Search.admissible
signature: def admissible (f : Frame) : List Nat
docstring:
The admissible truth-sets of a frame, as bitmasks: hereditary along `ri`
and containing every fallible world.

name: PLLND.Search.assigns
signature:
def assigns : List String → List Nat → List (List (String × Nat))
  | [], _ => [[]]
  | a :: as, adm =>
      (assigns as adm).flatMap fun rest => adm.map fun m => (a, m) :: rest
docstring: All assignments of admissible masks to a list of atoms.

name: PLLND.Search.toFinCM
signature: def toFinCM (f : Frame) (asgn : List (String × Nat)) : FinCM
docstring: Turn a frame together with a mask assignment into a concrete `FinCM`.

name: PLLND.Search.atomList
signature:
def atomList : PLLFormula → List String
  | .prop a => [a]
  | .falsePLL => []
  | .and A B | .or A B | .ifThen A B => atomList A ++ atomList B
  | .somehow A => atomList A
docstring: The atoms occurring in a formula.

name: PLLND.Search.atomsOf
signature: def atomsOf (l : List PLLFormula) : List String
docstring: The distinct atoms occurring in a list of formulas.

name: PLLND.Search.Witness
signature: abbrev Witness (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) : Type
docstring:
A certified countermodel witness: a finite model `M`, a world `w`, and a
proof that the verified checker accepts it for the original sequent.

name: PLLND.Search.Witness.simplify
docstring:
**Simplify a witness**: run `CounterEmit.simplify` on its model and
re-derive the certificate for the smaller one.

The simplifier is untrusted, so the result is not assumed to check: the
proof `h` is obtained afresh by a dependent `if`, and a model that
somehow failed to check would leave the original witness untouched.  A
simplified witness is therefore exactly as trustworthy as an unsimplified
one — the certificate is a fact about the model that is returned.

`accept` is threaded into the simplifier (see `CounterEmit.minimise`), so
a search that is filtering candidates by some property keeps it.

name: PLLND.Search.simplifyWith
signature:
def simplifyWith {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula} (cfg : Config)
    (wit : Witness Γ C) : Witness Γ C
docstring:
`Witness.simplify` under a `Config`: a no-op when `cfg.simplify` is
`false`.

name: PLLND.Search.sweepCert
docstring:
Scan the battery for a certified countermodel.  Candidates are picked by
the fast scan on the normalised forms `Γ'`, `C'`, filtered by `cfg.accept`
(the identity filter by default); each candidate is gated by the verified
checker on the **original** `Γ`, `C`.

name: PLLND.Search.emitCert
signature:
def emitCert (Γ' : List PLLFormula) (C' : PLLFormula)
    (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula)
    (accept : FinCM → Bool := fun _ => true)
    (budget : Option Nat := none) (precheck : Bool := true) :
    Option (Witness Γ C)
docstring:
Run the closure-based emitter on `Γ'`, `C'`; gate any proposal through the
verified checker on the original `Γ`, `C`, returning a certified witness.

The trailing `accept` argument is the same untrusted pre-filter as
`Config.accept`; it defaults to the identity filter, so every existing call
site keeps its behaviour.  `budget` and `precheck` control the proof search
`emit` runs first (see `CounterEmit.emit`): `budget` is `Config.findBudget`
at both call sites here, so a `#refute` that reaches this stage is bounded
like a `#search`, and `settleWhy` passes `precheck := false` because its own
positive stage has just searched the same sequent to exhaustion.

name: PLLND.Search.Answer
signature:
inductive Answer (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) where
  | proved  : G4cTm Γ C → Answer Γ C
  | refuted : (M : FinCM) → (w : Nat) → FinCM.checkB M w Γ C = true → Answer Γ C
  | unknown : Answer Γ C

name: PLLND.Search.Reason
signature:
inductive Reason where
  /-- The positive stage was truncated by `Config.findBudget` (the recorded
  `Nat` is the budget that ran out).  Raise `findBudget`, or set it to
  `none`; the search space was *not* exhausted, so nothing at all is known. -/
  | budgetExhausted (budget : Nat)
  /-- The `emit` stage was skipped because the subformula closure (first
  `Nat`) exceeded `Config.emitClosureCap` (second `Nat`).  Raise
  `emitClosureCap` if you are prepared to pay for the exponential stage. -/
  | closureTooBig (size cap : Nat)
  /-- Every stage ran to completion and none produced a certificate: the
  frame battery found no countermodel, the (search-space-exhausted) proof
  search found no proof, and the emitter proposed nothing that cleared
  `checkB`.  Widen `Config.frames`, or `Config.comboCap`. -/
  | allStagesMissed
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
docstring: Why a search returned no verdict.  Each constructor names the knob.

name: PLLND.Search.Reason.describe
signature:
def Reason.describe : Reason → String
  | .budgetExhausted b =>
      s!"positive stage truncated: the node budget of {b} ran out \
(raise Config.findBudget, or set it to none)"
  | .closureTooBig size cap =>
      s!"emit stage skipped: subformula closure has {size} formulas, \
cap is {cap} (raise Config.emitClosureCap)"
  | .allStagesMissed =>
      "all stages ran and missed: no battery countermodel, no proof, \
no emitted countermodel (widen Config.frames or Config.comboCap)"
docstring: A human-readable reading of a `Reason`, naming the knob to turn.

name: PLLND.Search.Verdict
signature:
inductive Verdict (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) where
  /-- `t : G4cTm Γ C` is a proof term of G4iLL″. -/
  | proved  : G4cTm Γ C → Verdict Γ C
  /-- `h` proves the verified checker accepts `M` at `w`. -/
  | refuted : (M : FinCM) → (w : Nat) → FinCM.checkB M w Γ C = true → Verdict Γ C
  /-- No certificate; the `Reason` says which bound bit. -/
  | unknown : Reason → Verdict Γ C
docstring:
The result of a search, carrying its certificate **and**, when there is
no verdict, the reason.  `Answer` is `Verdict` with the reason forgotten.

name: PLLND.Search.Verdict.toAnswer
signature:
def Verdict.toAnswer {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula} :
    Verdict Γ C → Answer Γ C
  | .proved t      => .proved t
  | .refuted M w h => .refuted M w h
  | .unknown _     => .unknown
docstring: Forget the reason: the backward-compatible `Answer` view of a verdict.

name: PLLND.Search.Verdict.reason?
signature:
def Verdict.reason? {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula} :
    Verdict Γ C → Option Reason
  | .unknown r => some r
  | _          => none
docstring: The reason, when there is no verdict.

name: PLLND.Search.settleWhy
signature:
def settleWhy (cfg : Config := {}) (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) :
    Verdict Γ C
docstring:
**The staged decision procedure, with reasons.**  In order:

1. the certified battery sweep (`sweepCert`) — a cheap certified refutation;
2. the fuel-free backward searcher `G4cTm.find` on the **original** sequent —
   the positive engine, returning a kernel-checkable proof term for `Γ ⊢ C`
   (capped at `cfg.findBudget` visited nodes when that is set, via
   `G4cTm.findBounded`; exhaustion degrades this stage to a failed search,
   never to a negative verdict);
3. the closure emitter `emitCert`, gated by `emitClosureCap` — a
   complete-over-the-closure but exponential refuter;
4. `unknown`.

The normaliser feeds only stages 1 and 3 (the untrusted proposers); the
proof term from stage 2 and both refutation certificates are about the
original `Γ`, `C`.

The budget cutoff is told apart from a genuine search-space exhaustion by
the remainder returned by `G4cTm.findBounded`: remainder `0` is a cutoff.

name: PLLND.Search.settle
signature:
def settle (cfg : Config := {}) (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) :
    Answer Γ C
docstring:
**The staged decision procedure** (`settleWhy` with the reason
forgotten).  This is the two-sided entry point; it was called `decide` until
the rename, and `decide` remains as an alias below.

The stages, in order: the certified battery sweep, the (optionally
budgeted) backward searcher `G4cTm.find`, the closure emitter gated by
`emitClosureCap`, then `unknown`.

name: PLLND.Search.decide
signature:
def decide (cfg : Config := {}) (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) :
    Answer Γ C
docstring:
Compatibility alias for `settle`, under the name this entry point had
before the rename.

Kept as a plain definition rather than `@[deprecated]` on purpose: the name
is used at several dozen call sites across `wip/`, and a deprecation warning
at each of them would drown the build log.  New code should say `settle`
(or, better, the sequent-first `verdict` of §11): `PLLND.Search.decide`
shadows `Decidable.decide` under `open PLLND.Search`, which is exactly what
the rename fixes.

name: PLLND.Search.proved_sound
signature:
theorem proved_sound {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula} (t : G4cTm Γ C) :
    Nonempty (LaxND Γ C)
docstring:
A `.proved` certificate yields a natural-deduction derivation.  The chain
is `G4cTm.toG4c` (proof term ⇒ G4c derivation) followed by `G4c.equiv_nd`
(G4c = PLL natural deduction).

name: PLLND.Search.refuted_sound
docstring:
A `.refuted` certificate yields underivability, by the certificate theorem
`FinCM.not_provable_of_check` (Kripke soundness of natural deduction).

name: PLLND.Search.Decision
signature:
inductive Decision (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) where
  | derivable   : Nonempty (LaxND Γ C) → Decision Γ C
  | underivable : ¬ Nonempty (LaxND Γ C) → Decision Γ C
  | dontKnow    : Decision Γ C
docstring:
A certified verdict: the derivability status of `Γ ⊢ C` together with a
proof of it (or `dontKnow`).

name: PLLND.Search.Answer.toDecision
signature:
def Answer.toDecision {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula} :
    Answer Γ C → Decision Γ C
  | .proved t      => .derivable (proved_sound t)
  | .refuted _ _ h => .underivable (refuted_sound h)
  | .unknown       => .dontKnow
docstring: Discharge an `Answer` into a certified `Decision` in one call.

name: PLLND.Search.Verdict.toDecision
signature:
def Verdict.toDecision {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula} :
    Verdict Γ C → Decision Γ C
  | .proved t      => .derivable (proved_sound t)
  | .refuted _ _ h => .underivable (refuted_sound h)
  | .unknown _     => .dontKnow
docstring:
Discharge a `Verdict` into a certified `Decision` in one call.  The
reason is dropped: a `Decision` is about the sequent, a `Reason` about the
search.

name: PLLND.Search.prove?
signature: def prove? (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) : Option (G4cTm Γ C)
docstring:
Positive engine only: the fuel-free backward searcher for `Γ ⊢ C`,
returning a proof term.  `none` proves nothing (see the trust note above).

name: PLLND.Search.prove?Bounded
signature:
def prove?Bounded (budget : Nat) (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) :
    Option (G4cTm Γ C)
docstring:
Positive engine with a **node budget**: `G4cTm.findBounded` capped at
`budget` visited sequents.  A found term is kernel-checkable exactly as with
`prove?`; `none` means only "not settled within `budget` nodes" — an honest
unknown, never a negative verdict.  To tell a genuine search-space
exhaustion (the same `none` as `prove?`) from a budget cutoff, call
`G4cTm.findBounded` directly and inspect the remaining budget; the
difference `budget - remaining` also serves as a node-count profile for
tuning budgets.

name: PLLND.Search.refute?
signature:
def refute? (cfg : Config := {}) (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) :
    Option (Witness Γ C)
docstring:
Negative engines only (battery, then the closure emitter): a certified
countermodel witness, or `none`.

"No proof search" is true of this function but not of its second stage:
`CounterEmit.emit` runs a search of its own, to avoid building an
exponential model for a provable sequent.  `cfg.findBudget` is passed down
to cap it.

name: PLLND.Search.verdictWhy
signature:
def verdictWhy (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula)
    (cfg : Config := budgetedConfig) : Verdict Γ C
docstring:
Sequent-first `settleWhy`: the two-sided procedure with reasons, with a
node budget on by default (`budgetedConfig`).

name: PLLND.Search.verdict
signature:
def verdict (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula)
    (cfg : Config := budgetedConfig) : Answer Γ C
docstring:
Sequent-first `settle`: the two-sided procedure, with a node budget on by
default (`budgetedConfig`).  See §10 for the difference from `settle {} Γ C`.

name: PLLND.Search.countermodel
signature:
def countermodel (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula)
    (cfg : Config := budgetedConfig) : Option (Witness Γ C)
docstring:
Sequent-first `refute?`: the negative engines only (battery, then emit),
returning a certified countermodel witness.

name: PLLND.Search.proof

Sequent-first positive engine, budgeted by default: `G4cTm.findBounded`
at `cfg.findBudget` nodes, or the fuel-free `G4cTm.find` when that is `none`.
`none` proves nothing (see the trust note in the module header).

name: PLLND.Search.srcOf
signature:
def srcOf : PLLFormula → String
  | .prop a      => s!"(PLLFormula.prop \"{a}\")"
  | .falsePLL    => "PLLFormula.falsePLL"
  | .and A B     => s!"({srcOf A}.and {srcOf B})"
  | .or A B      => s!"({srcOf A}.or {srcOf B})"
  | .ifThen A B  => s!"({srcOf A}.ifThen {srcOf B})"
  | .somehow A   => s!"({srcOf A}.somehow)"
docstring:
A `PLLFormula` as Lean source that elaborates back to it.  Fully
qualified and fully parenthesised, so it can be pasted anywhere.

name: PLLND.Search.srcOfCtx
signature: def srcOfCtx (Γ : List PLLFormula) : String
docstring: A hypothesis list as Lean source.

name: PLLND.Search.srcOfCM
signature: def srcOfCM (M : FinCM) : String
docstring:
A `FinCM` as Lean source (the anonymous-constructor form used in every
pinned countermodel in this repository).

name: PLLND.Search.strictRi'
signature: private def strictRi' (M : FinCM) (i j : Nat) : Bool
docstring: Strict `Rᵢ`: below and not above.

name: PLLND.Search.coversFrom
signature: private def coversFrom (M : FinCM) (i : Nat) : List Nat
docstring: Cover (Hasse) edges of the strict part of `Rᵢ`, from world `i`.

name: PLLND.Search.renderCM
signature: def renderCM (M : FinCM) (w? : Option Nat := none) : String
docstring:
**Compact renderer for a finite constraint model.**  Header line, then
one line per world.  `w?` marks the refuting world.

```
3 worlds, refuting world 0; fallible {2}
  *w0  ⊑> {1}  ⊳ {1}  ⊩ p
   w1  ⊑> {2}  ⊳ {}   ⊩ p, q
   w2  ⊑> {}   ⊳ {}   ⊩ ⊥ (fallible)
```

`⊑>` lists the `Rᵢ`-**cover** successors (transitive reduction; reflexive
pairs suppressed), `⊳` the `Rₘ` successors, `⊩` the atoms forced; `*` marks
the refuting world.  A fallible world forces everything, so its atom list is
written `⊥`.

name: PLLND.Search.summaryCM
signature: def summaryCM (M : FinCM) (w : Nat) : String
docstring: A one-line summary of a model: worlds, refuting world, edge counts.

name: PLLND.Search.Witness.render
signature:
def Witness.render {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula}
    (wit : Witness Γ C) : String
docstring:
The witness's model, rendered compactly by `renderCM`, with its refuting
world marked.

name: PLLND.Search.Witness.summary
signature:
def Witness.summary {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula}
    (wit : Witness Γ C) : String
docstring: One-line summary of the witness's model.

name: PLLND.Search.Witness.snippet
signature:
def Witness.snippet {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula}
    (name : String := "underivable") (wit : Witness Γ C) : String
docstring:
The paste-ready underivability theorem certified by this witness: the
model copied into a `FinCM.not_provable_of_check` application, with the
`#print axioms` audit line.  Only `checkB` on concrete data remains, so the
`by decide` is a kernel evaluation and the search drops out entirely.

name: PLLND.Search._root_.PLLND.G4cTm.src
signature:
def _root_.PLLND.G4cTm.src {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula} :
    G4cTm Γ C → String
  | .init _              => "(.init (by decide))"
  | .botL _              => "(.botL (by decide))"
  | .andR a b            => s!"(.andR {a.src} {b.src})"
  | .orR1 a              => s!"(.orR1 {a.src})"
  | .orR2 a              => s!"(.orR2 {a.src})"
  | .impR a              => s!"(.impR {a.src})"
  | .laxR a              => s!"(.laxR {a.src})"
  | @G4cTm.laxL _ A _ _ a => s!"(.laxL (A := {srcOf A}) (by decide) {a.src})"
  | @G4cTm.andL _ A B _ _ a =>
      s!"(.andL (A := {srcOf A}) (B := {srcOf B}) (by decide) {a.src})"
  | @G4cTm.orL _ A B _ _ a b =>
      s!"(.orL (A := {srcOf A}) (B := {srcOf B}) (by decide) {a.src} {b.src})"
  | @G4cTm.impLProp _ a B _ _ _ t =>
      s!"(.impLProp (a := \"{a}\") (B := {srcOf B}) (by decide) (by decide) {t.src})"
  | @G4cTm.impLAnd _ A B D _ _ t =>
      s!"(.impLAnd (A := {srcOf A}) (B := {srcOf B}) (D := {srcOf D}) \
(by decide) {t.src})"
  | @G4cTm.impLOr _ A B D _ _ t =>
      s!"(.impLOr (A := {srcOf A}) (B := {srcOf B}) (D := {srcOf D}) \
(by decide) {t.src})"
  | @G4cTm.impLImp _ A B D _ _ t u =>
      s!"(.impLImp (A := {srcOf A}) (B := {srcOf B}) (D := {srcOf D}) \
(by decide) {t.src} {u.src})"
  | @G4cTm.impLLax _ A B _ _ t u =>
      s!"(.impLLax (A := {srcOf A}) (B := {srcOf B}) (by decide) {t.src} {u.src})"
  | @G4cTm.impLLaxLax _ A B X _ _ _ t u =>
      s!"(.impLLaxLax (A := {srcOf A}) (B := {srcOf B}) (X := {srcOf X}) \
(by decide) (by decide) {t.src} {u.src})"
docstring:
A proof term as the Lean source of the corresponding `G4cTm`
constructor tree.  The implicit formula arguments that the goal does *not*
determine — which hypothesis a left rule decomposes — are supplied by name,
so the term elaborates on its own; the side conditions are list memberships,
emitted as `(by decide)`.

name: PLLND.Search._root_.PLLND.G4cTm.snippet
signature:
def _root_.PLLND.G4cTm.snippet {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula}
    (name : String := "derivable") (t : G4cTm Γ C) : String
docstring:

name: PLLND.Search.scopeLines
signature: def scopeLines (M : FinCM) : List String
docstring:
**How far a countermodel reaches**: the `scope` line of a refutation
report.

A finite countermodel refutes `LaxND` (PLL) always, and `ConfluentU.DerivU`
(PCLL, PLL + `◯(A ∨ B) ⊃ ◯A ∨ ◯B`) only when it is mutually confluent.  The
distinction is invisible in the model picture and easy to forget, and using a
non-confluent model against a PCLL claim is simply a wrong proof — so every
refutation report states which of the two it has, and names the command to
use when the answer is the narrow one.

`RNC.confB` is the same Boolean test `#refuteConf` filters by, so this line
is a fact about the model returned, not a guess.

name: PLLND.G4cTm.memSrc
signature: def memSrc (Γ : List PLLFormula) (φ : PLLFormula) : String
docstring:
The membership chain for `φ ∈ Γ`, or a marker if `φ` is somehow absent
(which cannot happen when the argument came from a real derivation).

The marker is a deliberately **unknown identifier** rather than `sorry`: emitted
source is meant to be pasted into a file, and a fallback that elaborated to
`sorry` could turn a broken emission into a silently unsound theorem.  An
unknown identifier fails loudly at elaboration.

name: PLLND.G4cTm.toLeanSrc
signature:
def toLeanSrc : {Γ : List PLLFormula} → {C : PLLFormula} →
    G4cTm Γ C → String
  | Γ, _, .init (a := a) _ => s!"(.init {memSrc Γ (prop a)})"
  | Γ, _, .botL _ => s!"(.botL {memSrc Γ falsePLL})"
  | _, _, .andR a b => s!"(.andR {toLeanSrc a} {toLeanSrc b})"
  | _, _, .orR1 a => s!"(.orR1 {toLeanSrc a})"
  | _, _, .orR2 a => s!"(.orR2 {toLeanSrc a})"
  | _, _, .impR a => s!"(.impR {toLeanSrc a})"
  | _, _, .laxR a => s!"(.laxR {toLeanSrc a})"
  | Γ, _, .laxL (A := A) _ a => s!"(.laxL {memSrc Γ A.somehow} {toLeanSrc a})"
  | Γ, _, .andL (A := A) (B := B) _ a =>
      s!"(.andL {memSrc Γ (A.and B)} {toLeanSrc a})"
  | Γ, _, .orL (A := A) (B := B) _ a b =>
      s!"(.orL {memSrc Γ (A.or B)} {toLeanSrc a} {toLeanSrc b})"
  | Γ, _, .impLProp (a := q) (B := B) _ _ a =>
      s!"(.impLProp {memSrc Γ ((prop q).ifThen B)} {memSrc Γ (prop q)} \
{toLeanSrc a})"
  | Γ, _, .impLAnd (A := A) (B := B) (D := D) _ a =>
      s!"(.impLAnd {memSrc Γ ((A.and B).ifThen D)} {toLeanSrc a})"
  | Γ, _, .impLOr (A := A) (B := B) (D := D) _ a =>
      s!"(.impLOr {memSrc Γ ((A.or B).ifThen D)} {toLeanSrc a})"
  | Γ, _, .impLImp (A := A) (B := B) (D := D) _ a b =>
      s!"(.impLImp {memSrc Γ ((A.ifThen B).ifThen D)} {toLeanSrc a} \
{toLeanSrc b})"
  | Γ, _, .impLLax (A := A) (B := B) _ a b =>
      s!"(.impLLax {memSrc Γ (A.somehow.ifThen B)} {toLeanSrc a} \
{toLeanSrc b})"
  | Γ, _, .impLLaxLax (A := A) (B := B) (X := X) _ _ a b =>
      s!"(.impLLaxLax {memSrc Γ (A.somehow.ifThen B)} {memSrc Γ X.somehow} \
{toLeanSrc a} {toLeanSrc b})"
docstring:
**A proof term as Lean source.**  Emits constructor names and membership
chains only; every formula index is recovered by unification against the
expected type.

name: PLLND.G4cTm.size
signature:
def size : {Γ : List PLLFormula} → {C : PLLFormula} → G4cTm Γ C → Nat
  | _, _, .init _ => 1
  | _, _, .botL _ => 1
  | _, _, .andR a b => 1 + size a + size b
  | _, _, .orR1 a => 1 + size a
  | _, _, .orR2 a => 1 + size a
  | _, _, .impR a => 1 + size a
  | _, _, .laxR a => 1 + size a
  | _, _, .laxL _ a => 1 + size a
  | _, _, .andL _ a => 1 + size a
  | _, _, .orL _ a b => 1 + size a + size b
  | _, _, .impLProp _ _ a => 1 + size a
  | _, _, .impLAnd _ a => 1 + size a
  | _, _, .impLOr _ a => 1 + size a
  | _, _, .impLImp _ a b => 1 + size a + size b
  | _, _, .impLLax _ a b => 1 + size a + size b
  | _, _, .impLLaxLax _ _ a b => 1 + size a + size b
docstring: Node count of a proof term, for reporting.

name: PLLND.Search.pinReport
signature: def pinReport (cfg : Config) (Γ : List PLLFormula) (C : PLLFormula) : String
docstring: Run the oracle and report a pasteable proof term, or why there is none.

name: PLLND.SemUI.ABisim
signature:
structure ABisim (A : String → Prop) (M N : ConstraintModel) where
  Z : M.W → N.W → Prop
  atoms : ∀ {w w'}, Z w w' → ∀ a, A a → (w ∈ M.V a ↔ w' ∈ N.V a)
  fall  : ∀ {w w'}, Z w w' → (w ∈ M.F ↔ w' ∈ N.F)
  iforth : ∀ {w w'}, Z w w' → ∀ {v}, M.Ri w v → ∃ v', N.Ri w' v' ∧ Z v v'
  iback  : ∀ {w w'}, Z w w' → ∀ {v'}, N.Ri w' v' → ∃ v, M.Ri w v ∧ Z v v'
  mforth : ∀ {w w'}, Z w w' → ∀ {u}, M.Rm w u → ∃ u', N.Rm w' u' ∧ Z u u'
  mback  : ∀ {w w'}, Z w w' → ∀ {u'}, N.Rm w' u' → ∃ u, M.Rm w u ∧ Z u u'
docstring:
**A-bisimulation** between constraint models: zigzag for both
relations, matching fallibility, matching atoms in the protected
alphabet `A`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.force_iff_of_bisim
signature:
theorem force_iff_of_bisim {A : String → Prop} {M N : ConstraintModel}
    (B : ABisim A M N) :
    ∀ {φ : PLLFormula}, (∀ a ∈ φ.atoms, A a) →
    ∀ {w : M.W} {w' : N.W}, B.Z w w' → (M.force w φ ↔ N.force w' φ)

name: PLLND.SemUI.ABisim.id
signature:
def ABisim.id (A : String → Prop) (M : ConstraintModel) : ABisim A M M where
  Z
docstring: The identity bisimulation (any alphabet).

name: PLLND.SemUI.PBisim
signature: abbrev PBisim (p : String)
docstring:
Bisimulation protecting every atom except `p`: its related worlds
are each other's *p-variants*.

name: PLLND.SemUI.IsSemEx
signature: def IsSemEx (p : String) (φ ψ : PLLFormula) : Prop
docstring:
`ψ` is a **semantic ∃p-quantifier** for `φ`: p-free, and forced
exactly at the worlds having a p-variant forcing `φ`.  (Persistence of
the right-hand side follows from i-forth, so the spec is coherent.)

name: PLLND.SemUI.IsSemAll
signature: def IsSemAll (p : String) (φ ψ : PLLFormula) : Prop
docstring:
`ψ` is a **semantic ∀p-quantifier** for `φ`: p-free, and forced
exactly at the worlds ALL of whose futures' p-variants force `φ` (the
Rᵢ-guard makes the right-hand side hereditary).

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_upper
signature:
theorem semEx_upper {p : String} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} (h : IsSemEx p φ ψ) :
    Nonempty (LaxND [φ] ψ)

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_adjunction
docstring: **The ∃p adjunction**: for p-free `χ`,  `φ ⊢ χ  iff  ∃p.φ ⊢ χ`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_lower
signature:
theorem semAll_lower {p : String} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} (h : IsSemAll p φ ψ) :
    Nonempty (LaxND [ψ] φ)

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_adjunction
docstring: **The ∀p adjunction**: for p-free `χ`,  `χ ⊢ φ  iff  χ ⊢ ∀p.φ`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_unique
docstring:
Any two ∃p-spec-satisfiers are interderivable: the value is unique
up to ≡.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_unique
docstring: Any two ∀p-spec-satisfiers are interderivable.

name: PLLND.SemUI.SemExDefinable
signature: def SemExDefinable : Prop
docstring:
OPEN (Ghilardi step, ∃-side): the definability CONJECTURE.  Stated
as a `Prop` so the library carries no `sorry`; a proof would be a term
of this type.  Everything below that mentions definability proves
CONDITIONAL statements (reductions) or INSTANCES, never this.

name: PLLND.SemUI.SemAllDefinable
signature: def SemAllDefinable : Prop
docstring: OPEN (Ghilardi step, ∀-side): the definability CONJECTURE.

name: PLLND.SemUI.redecorate

def redecorate (M : ConstraintModel) (p : String) (S : Set M.W)
    (hh : ∀ {w v}, M.Ri w v → w ∈ S → v ∈ S)
    (hf : ∀ {w}, w ∈ M.F → w ∈ S) : ConstraintModel where

name: PLLND.SemUI.redecorate_pbisim
signature:
def redecorate_pbisim (M : ConstraintModel) (p : String) (S : Set M.W)

    (hf : ∀ {w}, w ∈ M.F → w ∈ S) :
    PBisim p M (redecorate M p S hh hf) where

docstring: Redecoration is a p-variant: the identity carrier is a `PBisim p`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_prop_self
signature: theorem semEx_prop_self (p : String) : IsSemEx p (.prop p) truePLL
docstring:
`∃p.p = ⊤` — every world has a p-variant forcing p (redecorate with
the universal set).

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_prop_self
signature: theorem semAll_prop_self (p : String) : IsSemAll p (.prop p) falsePLL
docstring:
`∀p.p = ⊥` — only fallible worlds have p forced by ALL p-variants
(redecorate with the fallible set).

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_prop_ne
signature:
theorem semEx_prop_ne {p q : String} (h : q ≠ p) :
    IsSemEx p (.prop q) (.prop q)
docstring: `∃p.q = q` for `q ≠ p`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_prop_ne
signature:
theorem semAll_prop_ne {p q : String} (h : q ≠ p) :
    IsSemAll p (.prop q) (.prop q)
docstring: `∀p.q = q` for `q ≠ p`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_false
signature: theorem semEx_false (p : String) : IsSemEx p .falsePLL .falsePLL

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_false
signature: theorem semAll_false (p : String) : IsSemAll p .falsePLL .falsePLL

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_or
docstring: ∃p commutes with ∨ (the SAME p-variant serves whichever disjunct).

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_and
docstring: ∀p commutes with ∧.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_neg_p
signature: theorem semEx_neg_p (p : String) : IsSemEx p ((PLLFormula.prop p).ifThen .falsePLL) truePLL
docstring:
`∃p.¬p = ⊤`: decorate p by the fallible set; then p ⊃ ⊥ holds
everywhere.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_neg_p
signature: theorem semAll_neg_p (p : String) : IsSemAll p ((PLLFormula.prop p).ifThen .falsePLL) .falsePLL
docstring:
`∀p.¬p = ⊥`: against the ⊤-decoration, ¬p forces only where
everything ahead is fallible — i.e. exactly on F.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_box_p
signature: theorem semEx_box_p (p : String) : IsSemEx p (PLLFormula.prop p).somehow truePLL
docstring:
`∃p.◯p = ⊤`: under the ⊤-decoration every world Rₘ-reaches itself
forcing p.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_box_p
signature:
theorem semAll_box_p (p : String) :
    IsSemAll p (PLLFormula.prop p).somehow PLLFormula.falsePLL.somehow
docstring:
**`∀p.◯p = ◯⊥`** — the first genuinely modal quantifier value.
Forward: ◯⊥ is p-free, so it crosses any p-bisimulation, and `full_F`
turns its fallible witnesses into p-witnesses.  Backward: the
F-decoration is a legal p-variant on which ◯p IS ◯⊥.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_p_and_neg_p
signature:
theorem semEx_p_and_neg_p (p : String) :
    IsSemEx p ((PLLFormula.prop p).and ((PLLFormula.prop p).ifThen .falsePLL)) .falsePLL
docstring:
`∃p.(p ∧ ¬p) = ⊥`: a p-variant forcing both p and ¬p is fallible,
and fallibility crosses the bisimulation.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_pfree_fixpoint
signature:
theorem semAll_pfree_fixpoint {p : String} {ψ : PLLFormula}
    (hp : p ∉ ψ.atoms) : IsSemAll p ψ ψ
docstring: ∀p fixes every p-free formula.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_pfree_fixpoint
signature:
theorem semEx_pfree_fixpoint {p : String} {ψ : PLLFormula}
    (hp : p ∉ ψ.atoms) : IsSemEx p ψ ψ
docstring: ∃p fixes every p-free formula.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_hits_every_closed
signature:
theorem semAll_hits_every_closed (p : String) {ξ : PLLFormula}
    (h : ξ.atoms = ∅) : ∃ M, IsSemAll p M ξ
docstring:
**Every closed formula is a ∀p-value** (Matthew's conjecture,
2026-07-18): the ∀p-image covers all of RN(◯,{}).

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_hits_every_closed
signature:
theorem semEx_hits_every_closed (p : String) {ξ : PLLFormula}
    (h : ξ.atoms = ∅) : ∃ M, IsSemEx p M ξ
docstring: Dually for ∃p.

name: PLLND.SemUI.oneW
signature:
def oneW : ConstraintModel where
  W
docstring: The trivial one-world, nowhere-fallible model.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_and_pointwise_fails
signature:
theorem semEx_and_pointwise_fails (p : String) :
    ¬ IsSemEx p ((PLLFormula.prop p).and ((PLLFormula.prop p).ifThen .falsePLL))
        (truePLL.and truePLL)
docstring:
**The amalgamation obstruction, machine-checked**: ∃p does NOT
commute with ∧.  The pointwise candidate for `∃p.(p ∧ ¬p)` from
`semEx_prop_self` and `semEx_neg_p` is `⊤ ∧ ⊤`; it fails the spec,
because at the non-fallible world of `oneW` the two conjuncts demand
INCOMPATIBLE p-decorations (everywhere vs nowhere-but-F).

name: PLLND.SemUI.Inessential
signature: def Inessential (p : String) (M : PLLFormula) : Prop
docstring:
`p` is inessential in `M`: `M` is interderivable with some p-free
formula.  (*Essential* = the negation.)

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_true_derivable
signature:
theorem semAll_true_derivable {p : String} {M : PLLFormula}
    (h : IsSemAll p M truePLL) : Nonempty (LaxND [] M)
docstring:
If ⊤ meets the ∀p-spec for `M`, then `⊢ M`: instantiate the spec's
right-hand side at the world itself and the identity bisimulation.

name: PLLND.SemUI.inessential_of_semAll_true
signature:
theorem inessential_of_semAll_true {p : String} {M : PLLFormula}
    (h : IsSemAll p M truePLL) : Inessential p M
docstring: **⊤ is never an essential ∀p-value**: `∀p.M = ⊤` forces `M ≡ ⊤`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_false_refutes
signature:
theorem semEx_false_refutes {p : String} {M : PLLFormula}
    (h : IsSemEx p M .falsePLL) : Nonempty (LaxND [M] .falsePLL)
docstring:
If ⊥ meets the ∃p-spec for `M`, then `M ⊢ ⊥`: the world itself is a
p-variant of itself forcing `M`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.inessential_of_semEx_false
signature:
theorem inessential_of_semEx_false {p : String} {M : PLLFormula}
    (h : IsSemEx p M .falsePLL) : Inessential p M
docstring: **⊥ is never an essential ∃p-value**: `∃p.M = ⊥` forces `M ≡ ⊥`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.substP
signature:
def substP (p : String) (χ : PLLFormula) : PLLFormula → PLLFormula
  | .prop a     => if a = p then χ else .prop a
  | .falsePLL   => .falsePLL
  | .and A B    => .and (substP p χ A) (substP p χ B)
  | .or A B     => .or (substP p χ A) (substP p χ B)
  | .ifThen A B => .ifThen (substP p χ A) (substP p χ B)
  | .somehow A  => .somehow (substP p χ A)
docstring: Substitute `χ` for the atom `p`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.substP_of_not_mem
signature:
theorem substP_of_not_mem {p : String} {χ M : PLLFormula} (h : p ∉ M.atoms) :
    substP p χ M = M
docstring: Substitution is vacuous on p-free formulas.

name: PLLND.SemUI.truthDeco
signature:
def truthDeco (C : ConstraintModel) (p : String) (χ : PLLFormula) :
    ConstraintModel
docstring:
The truth-set decoration: `p` re-decorated to hold exactly where `χ`
is forced.

name: PLLND.SemUI.truthDeco_pbisim
signature:
def truthDeco_pbisim (C : ConstraintModel) (p : String) (χ : PLLFormula) :
    PBisim p C (truthDeco C p χ)
docstring: The truth-set decoration is a p-variant of the original model.

name: PLLND.SemUI.force_truthDeco
signature:
theorem force_truthDeco (C : ConstraintModel) (p : String) (χ : PLLFormula) :
    ∀ (M : PLLFormula) (w : C.W),
      (truthDeco C p χ).force w M ↔ C.force w (substP p χ M)
docstring:
**Forcing a substitution instance = forcing under the truth-set
decoration.**

name: PLLND.SemUI.isSemEx_of_certificates
docstring:
**∃-side certificate criterion**: if `ψ` is p-free, `M ⊢ ψ`, and
`ψ ⊢ M[p:=χ]` for some formula `χ`, then `ψ` is the ∃p-value of `M`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.isSemAll_of_certificates
signature:
theorem isSemAll_of_certificates {p : String} {M ψ : PLLFormula}
    {χs : List PLLFormula} (hp : p ∉ ψ.atoms) (d₁ : LaxND [ψ] M)
    (d₂ : LaxND (χs.map (fun χ => substP p χ M)) ψ) :
    IsSemAll p M ψ
docstring:
**∀-side certificate criterion**: if `ψ` is p-free, `ψ ⊢ M`, and some
finite family of substitution instances derives it back,
`M[p:=χ₁], …, M[p:=χₖ] ⊢ ψ`, then `ψ` is the ∀p-value of `M`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.force_subst_iff_of_pfree_equiv
signature:
theorem force_subst_iff_of_pfree_equiv {p : String} {M ψ : PLLFormula}
    (hp : p ∉ ψ.atoms) (d₁ : LaxND [M] ψ) (d₂ : LaxND [ψ] M)
    (χ : PLLFormula) (C : ConstraintModel) (w : C.W) :
    C.force w (substP p χ M) ↔ C.force w ψ
docstring:
Substitution instances of a formula interderivable with a p-free `ψ`
force exactly like `ψ` — semantic substitution-admissibility, via the
truth-set decoration; no proof-theoretic substitution lemma is needed.

name: PLLND.SemUI.essential_of_separation
signature:
theorem essential_of_separation {p : String} {M χ₁ χ₂ : PLLFormula}
    (C : ConstraintModel) (w : C.W)
    (h₁ : C.force w (substP p χ₁ M)) (h₂ : ¬ C.force w (substP p χ₂ M)) :
    ¬ Inessential p M
docstring:
**Separation criterion for essentiality**: if two substitution
instances of `M` disagree at a single world of a single model, then `M`
is equivalent to no p-free formula.

name: PLLND.SemUI.exists_countermodel
signature:
theorem exists_countermodel {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula}
    (h : ¬ Nonempty (LaxND Γ φ)) :
    ∃ (C : ConstraintModel) (w : C.W),
      (∀ ψ ∈ Γ, C.force w ψ) ∧ ¬ C.force w φ
docstring:
Classically, non-derivability yields a countermodel (contrapositive
of `completeness`).

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_or_p
signature:
theorem semAll_or_p (p : String) {ξ : PLLFormula} (hp : p ∉ ξ.atoms) :
    IsSemAll p (ξ.or (.prop p)) ξ
docstring: `∀p.(ξ ∨ p) = ξ` for p-free ξ.

name: PLLND.SemUI.essential_or_p
signature:
theorem essential_or_p (p : String) {ξ : PLLFormula} (hp : p ∉ ξ.atoms)
    (hξ : ¬ Nonempty (LaxND [] ξ)) : ¬ Inessential p (ξ.or (.prop p))
docstring:
For underivable p-free ξ, `p` is essential in `ξ ∨ p`: the instances
`p := ⊤` and `p := ⊥` are separated at any countermodel to ξ.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semEx_and_p
signature:
theorem semEx_and_p (p : String) {ξ : PLLFormula} (hp : p ∉ ξ.atoms) :
    IsSemEx p (ξ.and (.prop p)) ξ
docstring: `∃p.(ξ ∧ p) = ξ` for p-free ξ.

name: PLLND.SemUI.essential_and_p
signature:
theorem essential_and_p (p : String) {ξ : PLLFormula} (hp : p ∉ ξ.atoms)
    (hξ : ¬ Nonempty (LaxND [ξ] .falsePLL)) :
    ¬ Inessential p (ξ.and (.prop p))
docstring: For p-free ξ with `ξ ⊬ ⊥`, `p` is essential in `ξ ∧ p`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.essential_semAll_image
docstring:
**The essential ∀p-image theorem**: a p-free ξ is the ∀p-value of a
formula in which `p` is essential  iff  ξ is not derivable.  On the
closed fragment: the essential ∀p-image is RN(◯,{}) ∖ {⊤}.

name: PLLND.SemUI.essential_semEx_image
signature:
theorem essential_semEx_image {p : String} {ξ : PLLFormula}
    (hp : p ∉ ξ.atoms) :
    (∃ M, IsSemEx p M ξ ∧ ¬ Inessential p M) ↔
      ¬ Nonempty (LaxND [ξ] .falsePLL)
docstring:
**The essential ∃p-image theorem**: a p-free ξ is the ∃p-value of a
formula in which `p` is essential  iff  `ξ ⊬ ⊥`.  On the closed
fragment: the essential ∃p-image is RN(◯,{}) ∖ {⊥}.

name: PLLND.SemUI.double
signature:
def double (C : ConstraintModel) : ConstraintModel where
  W
docstring:
The doubled model: worlds `W × Bool`, both relations required to be
monotone into the upper copy, fallibility and valuation inherited from
the first coordinate.

name: PLLND.SemUI.emSet
signature: def emSet (C : ConstraintModel) (w₀ : C.W) : Set (C.W × Bool)
docstring:
The upper-copy decoration over `w₀`: the upper copy of the cone over
`w₀`, plus the fallible worlds.

name: PLLND.SemUI.emVariant
signature:
def emVariant (C : ConstraintModel) (p : String) (w₀ : C.W) :
    ConstraintModel
docstring: The doubled model with `p` decorated on the upper copy over `w₀`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.emVariant_pbisim
docstring:
Projection to the first coordinate is a p-bisimulation onto the
decorated double: each `(x, i)` is a p-variant of `x`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_em_p
signature:
theorem semAll_em_p (p : String) :
    IsSemAll p ((PLLFormula.prop p).or ((PLLFormula.prop p).ifThen .falsePLL))
      .falsePLL
docstring:
**`∀p.(p ∨ ¬p) = ⊥`** — the first quantifier value requiring a
frame-changing p-variant.  A non-fallible world of the lower copy
forces neither `p` (it is not in the decoration) nor `¬p` (its upper
twin is), so only fallible worlds survive the spec.

name: PLLND.SemUI.oneW_em
signature:
theorem oneW_em (A : PLLFormula) :
    oneW.force () (A.or (A.ifThen .falsePLL))
docstring:
At the one-world irrefutable model, excluded middle holds for every
formula (classically).

name: PLLND.SemUI.em_p_no_certificate
signature:
theorem em_p_no_certificate (p : String) (χs : List PLLFormula) :
    ¬ Nonempty (LaxND (χs.map (fun χ =>
        substP p χ
          ((PLLFormula.prop p).or ((PLLFormula.prop p).ifThen .falsePLL))))
      .falsePLL)
docstring:
**No substitution certificate reaches `∀p.(p ∨ ¬p)`**: every
substitution instance of `p ∨ ¬p` is an excluded-middle instance, forced
at the one-world model, so no finite family of instances derives ⊥.
The ∀-criterion provably cannot establish `semAll_em_p`: the doubling
is necessary.

name: PLLND.SemUI.lowT
signature:
def lowT (p : String) : PLLFormula → PLLFormula
  | .prop a     => if a = p then .falsePLL else .prop a
  | .falsePLL   => .falsePLL
  | .and A B    => (lowT p A).and (lowT p B)
  | .or A B     => (lowT p A).or (lowT p B)
  | .ifThen A B => ((lowT p A).ifThen (lowT p B)).and
      ((substP p truePLL A).ifThen (substP p truePLL B))
  | .somehow A  => (substP p truePLL A).somehow
docstring:
The lower transform: forcing of `M` at the generic lower point of
the decorated double.

name: PLLND.SemUI.emVariant_force_true
signature:
theorem emVariant_force_true (C : ConstraintModel) (p : String) (w₀ : C.W) :
    ∀ (M : PLLFormula) {x : C.W}, C.Ri w₀ x →
      ((emVariant C p w₀).force (x, true) M ↔
        C.force x (substP p truePLL M))
docstring:
Upper-copy evaluation: within the cone over `w₀`, the upper copy
forces `M` iff the base world forces `M[p:=⊤]`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.emVariant_force_false
signature:
theorem emVariant_force_false (C : ConstraintModel) (p : String) (w₀ : C.W) :
    ∀ (M : PLLFormula) {x : C.W}, C.Ri w₀ x →
      ((emVariant C p w₀).force (x, false) M ↔ C.force x (lowT p M))
docstring:
**Lower-copy evaluation**: within the cone over `w₀`, the lower copy
forces `M` iff the base world forces the lower transform `lowT p M`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.isSemAll_of_certificates_low
signature:
theorem isSemAll_of_certificates_low {p : String} {M ψ : PLLFormula}
    {χs : List PLLFormula} (hp : p ∉ ψ.atoms) (d₁ : LaxND [ψ] M)
    (d₂ : LaxND (lowT p M :: χs.map (fun χ => substP p χ M)) ψ) :
    IsSemAll p M ψ
docstring:
**∀-side extended criterion**: the lower transform joins the
substitution instances as one more certificate premise:
`lowT p M, M[p:=χ₁], …, M[p:=χₖ] ⊢ ψ` (with `ψ ⊢ M`, `ψ` p-free)
establishes the ∀p-spec.

name: PLLND.SemUI.isSemEx_of_certificates_low
docstring:
**∃-side extended criterion**: if `ψ ⊢ lowT p M`, the decorated
double is the required p-variant.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_boxp_imp_p
signature:
theorem semAll_boxp_imp_p (p : String) :
    IsSemAll p ((PLLFormula.prop p).somehow.ifThen (.prop p)) .falsePLL
docstring:
**`∀p.(◯p ⊃ p) = ⊥`** — the probe's first substitution-uncertifiable
∀p-value, reached by the lower transform:
`lowT p (◯p ⊃ p) = (◯⊤ ⊃ ⊥) ∧ (◯⊤ ⊃ ⊤) ⊢ ⊥`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_nnp_imp_p
signature:
theorem semAll_nnp_imp_p (p : String) :
    IsSemAll p ((((PLLFormula.prop p).ifThen .falsePLL).ifThen
        .falsePLL).ifThen (.prop p)) .falsePLL
docstring:
**`∀p.(¬¬p ⊃ p) = ⊥`** — classicality of `p` also has ∀p-value ⊥,
again through the lower transform.

name: PLLND.SemUI.lobModel
signature:
def lobModel (C : ConstraintModel) : ConstraintModel where
  W
docstring:
ℕ-levelled copies: `Rᵢ` level-monotone, `Rₘ` level-rigid except the
single step 1 → 2; fallibility and valuation inherited.

name: PLLND.SemUI.lobVariant
signature: def lobVariant (C : ConstraintModel) (p : String) : ConstraintModel
docstring: The Löb variant: `p` decorated on levels ≥ 2 plus fallible worlds.

name: PLLND.SemUI.lobVariant_pbisim
docstring:
Projection to the first coordinate is a p-bisimulation onto the Löb
variant.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_box_lob
signature:
theorem semAll_box_lob (p : String) :
    IsSemAll p (((PLLFormula.prop p).somehow.ifThen (.prop p)).somehow)
      PLLFormula.falsePLL.somehow
docstring:

name: PLLND.SemUI.sideT
signature:
def sideT (p : String) : PLLFormula → PLLFormula
  | .prop a     => if a = p then .falsePLL else .prop a
  | .falsePLL   => .falsePLL
  | .and A B    => (sideT p A).and (sideT p B)
  | .or A B     => (sideT p A).or (sideT p B)
  | .ifThen A B => ((sideT p A).ifThen (sideT p B)).and (lowT p (A.ifThen B))
  | .somehow A  => ((sideT p A).somehow).and ((substP p truePLL A).somehow)
docstring: The level-0 transform of the Löb variant.

docstring:

`M[p:=⊤]`.

weight-cap artifact — the substitution `p := ⊤` also certifies, since
`¬◯⊤ ∨ ◯⊤` is derivable (right disjunct).  No ∃-side value is
currently known to REQUIRE a frame-changing generator; the ∀-side
necessity is `em_p_no_certificate`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.adjoin
signature:
def adjoin (N : ConstraintModel) (n₀ : N.W) (U R : Set N.W)
    (uUp : ∀ {y y'}, y ∈ U → N.Ri y y' → y' ∈ U)
    (uAbove : ∀ {y}, y ∈ U → N.Ri n₀ y)
    (rU : ∀ {u}, u ∈ R → u ∈ U)
    (rClosed : ∀ {u v}, u ∈ R → N.Rm u v → v ∈ R) : ConstraintModel where
  W
docstring:
Adjoin one point ⋆ to N, anchored at `n₀`: below-⋆ = below-n₀,
above-⋆ = the up-closed `U` over n₀, constraint row `{⋆} ∪ R` with
`R ⊆ U` closed under `N.Rm`; fallibility and valuations copied from
n₀.

name: PLLND.SemUI.adjoin_pbisim
signature:
def adjoin_pbisim {p : String} {C N : ConstraintModel}
    (B : PBisim p C N) {z : C.W} {n₀ : N.W} (hzn : B.Z z n₀)
    (U R : Set N.W)
    (uUp : ∀ {y y'}, y ∈ U → N.Ri y y' → y' ∈ U)
    (uAbove : ∀ {y}, y ∈ U → N.Ri n₀ y)
    (rU : ∀ {u}, u ∈ R → u ∈ U)
    (rClosed : ∀ {u v}, u ∈ R → N.Rm u v → v ∈ R)
    (anchor_down : ∀ {c n}, B.Z c n → N.Ri n n₀ → C.Ri c z)
    (iforth_cover : ∀ {v}, C.Ri z v → v = z ∨ ∃ n' ∈ U, B.Z v n')
    (iback_cover : ∀ {n'}, n' ∈ U → ∃ v, C.Ri z v ∧ B.Z v n')
    (mforth_cover : ∀ {u}, C.Rm z u → u = z ∨ ∃ n' ∈ R, B.Z u n')
    (mback_cover : ∀ {n'}, n' ∈ R → ∃ u, C.Rm z u ∧ B.Z u n') :
    PBisim p C (adjoin N n₀ U R uUp uAbove rU rClosed) where
  Z
docstring:
**Point-adjunction extends a p-bisimulation**: given a p-variant N
of C, an anchored pair `(z, n₀) ∈ B.Z`, and five cover conditions
routing z's relational data through the accumulated Z, the adjoined
model is again a p-variant, with ⋆ a p-variant of z.  `mback_cover`
is the promise mechanism: ⋆ may constraint-reach any world
Z-equivalent to a constraint successor of its anchor.

theorem adjoinAtP_not_em (C : ConstraintModel) (p : String) (z : C.W)
    (hzF : z ∉ C.F) :
    ¬ (adjoinAtP C p z).force (.inl z)
      ((PLLFormula.prop p).or ((PLLFormula.prop p).ifThen .falsePLL))
docstring:
**The doubling's job by one point**: at a non-fallible anchor, the
decorated instance refutes `p ∨ ¬p` — z is not in the decoration, its
point ⋆ is.  (No cluster or row hypothesis: the refutation is
frame-legal always; triviality is needed only for the BISIMULATION.)

name: PLLND.SemUI.adjoinAtP_not_frontier
signature:
theorem adjoinAtP_not_frontier (C : ConstraintModel) (p : String)
    (z : C.W) (hz : ∀ u, C.Rm z u → u ∉ C.F) :
    ¬ (adjoinAtP C p z).force (.inl z)
      ((((PLLFormula.prop p).ifThen PLLFormula.falsePLL.somehow).ifThen
        (.prop p)).ifThen (.prop p))
docstring:
**The split's job by one point**: with a fallibility-free
constraint row at the anchor, the decorated instance refutes
`((p ⊃ ◯⊥) ⊃ p) ⊃ p` — ⋆ forces `p` but not `◯⊥` (its row is z's
strict row), so no world below ⋆ can force `p ⊃ ◯⊥`, and every other
future of z is decorated.

name: PLLND.SemUI.substND
signature:
def substND (p : String) (χ : PLLFormula) :
    {Γ : List PLLFormula} → {φ : PLLFormula} →
    LaxND Γ φ → LaxND (Γ.map (substP p χ)) (substP p χ φ)
  | _, _, .iden h          => .iden (List.mem_map_of_mem h)
  | _, _, .falsoElim φ d   => .falsoElim (substP p χ φ) (substND p χ d)
  | _, _, .impIntro d      => .impIntro (substND p χ d)
  | _, _, .impElim d₁ d₂   => .impElim (substND p χ d₁) (substND p χ d₂)
  | _, _, .andIntro d₁ d₂  => .andIntro (substND p χ d₁) (substND p χ d₂)
  | _, _, .andElim1 d      => .andElim1 (substND p χ d)
  | _, _, .andElim2 d      => .andElim2 (substND p χ d)
  | _, _, .orIntro1 d      => .orIntro1 (substND p χ d)
  | _, _, .orIntro2 d      => .orIntro2 (substND p χ d)
  | _, _, .orElim d₀ d₁ d₂ => .orElim (substND p χ d₀) (substND p χ d₁) (substND p χ d₂)
  | _, _, .laxIntro d      => .laxIntro (substND p χ d)
  | _, _, .laxElim d₁ d₂   => .laxElim (substND p χ d₁) (substND p χ d₂)
docstring:
Natural deduction is closed under substitution of a formula for an
atom: every rule is homomorphic because `substP` commutes with every
connective (including `◯`).

name: PLLND.SemUI.CtxPFree
signature: def CtxPFree (p : String) (C : StdCtx) : Prop
docstring: The atom `p` occurs nowhere in the constraint's `K,L` formulas.

name: PLLND.SemUI.substP_applyC
docstring: Substitution passes through a `p`-free constraint application.

name: PLLND.SemUI.subC_substP
signature:
theorem subC_substP {p : String} {χ : PLLFormula} {C : StdCtx}
    (hC : CtxPFree p C) :
    ∀ M, subC C (substP p χ M) = substP p (subC C χ) (subC C M)
  | .prop a => by
      by_cases h : a = p <;> simp [substP, subC, h]
  | .falsePLL => rfl
  | .and A B => by
      simp only [substP, subC, subC_substP hC A, subC_substP hC B]
  | .or A B => by
      simp only [substP, subC, subC_substP hC A, subC_substP hC B]
  | .ifThen A B => by
      simp only [substP, subC, subC_substP hC A, subC_substP hC B]
  | .somehow A => by
      simp only [substP, subC, subC_substP hC A, substP_applyC hC]
docstring:
**The bridge**: constraint translation commutes with substitution,
`(M[p := χ])^C = (M^C)[p := χ^C]`, when `C` is `p`-free.  This is what
identifies the ladder route's substitution instances with IPC
instances of the translation.

name: PLLND.SemUI.applyC_pfree
signature:
theorem applyC_pfree {p : String} {C : StdCtx} (hC : CtxPFree p C)
    {x : PLLFormula} (hx : p ∉ x.atoms) : p ∉ (applyC C x).atoms
docstring: Applying a `p`-free constraint to a `p`-free formula is `p`-free.

name: PLLND.SemUI.subC_pfree
signature:
theorem subC_pfree {p : String} {C : StdCtx} (hC : CtxPFree p C) :
    ∀ {ξ : PLLFormula}, p ∉ ξ.atoms → p ∉ (subC C ξ).atoms
  | .prop a, h => by simpa [subC] using h
  | .falsePLL, h => by simp [subC]
  | .and A B, h => by
      have hA : p ∉ A.atoms
docstring: Translating a `p`-free formula by a `p`-free constraint is `p`-free.

name: PLLND.SemUI.IsIPCAll
signature:
structure IsIPCAll (p : String) (P : PLLFormula → Prop) (X A : PLLFormula) : Prop where
  pfree : p ∉ A.atoms
  lower : Nonempty (LaxND [A] X)
  greatest : ∀ ψ, P ψ → p ∉ ψ.atoms → Nonempty (LaxND [ψ] X) →
    Nonempty (LaxND [ψ] A)
docstring:
`A` behaves as `∀ᴵᴾᶜp.X` against comparisons in `P`: it is a
`p`-free lower bound of `X`, and the greatest among `P`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.IsIPCEx
signature:
structure IsIPCEx (p : String) (P : PLLFormula → Prop) (X E : PLLFormula) : Prop where
  pfree : p ∉ E.atoms
  upper : Nonempty (LaxND [X] E)
  least : ∀ ψ, P ψ → p ∉ ψ.atoms → Nonempty (LaxND [X] ψ) →
    Nonempty (LaxND [E] ψ)
docstring:
`E` behaves as `∃ᴵᴾᶜp.X` against comparisons in `P`: it is a
`p`-free upper bound of `X`, and the least among `P`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.ctxAll_ge_value
signature:
theorem ctxAll_ge_value {p : String} {C : StdCtx} {M ξ A : PLLFormula}
    (hCipl : CtxIsIPL C) (hCp : CtxPFree p C)
    (hξp : p ∉ ξ.atoms) (hlow : Nonempty (LaxND [ξ] M))
    (hA : IsIPCAll p isIPL (subC C M) A) :
    Nonempty (LaxND [subC C ξ] A)
docstring:
**∀-side lower bound (the constraint route over-approximates)**:
for any IPL, `p`-free constraint `C`, the translation of ANY `p`-free
PLL lower bound `ξ` of `M` derives the IPC ∀p-value of the translation
`M^C`.  With `ξ` the semantic value (via `semAll_lower`) this says the
constraint route can only ever land ON or ABOVE the translated true
value — never below.

name: PLLND.SemUI.ctxEx_le_value
signature:
theorem ctxEx_le_value {p : String} {C : StdCtx} {M ξ E : PLLFormula}
    (hCipl : CtxIsIPL C) (hCp : CtxPFree p C)
    (hξp : p ∉ ξ.atoms) (hup : Nonempty (LaxND [M] ξ))
    (hE : IsIPCEx p isIPL (subC C M) E) :
    Nonempty (LaxND [E] (subC C ξ))
docstring:
**∃-side upper bound (dual)**: the IPC ∃p-value of `M^C` derives
the translation of any `p`-free PLL upper bound of `M`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.ctxAll_le_instance
signature:
theorem ctxAll_le_instance {p : String} {C : StdCtx} {M A : PLLFormula}
    (hCp : CtxPFree p C) (hA : IsIPCAll p isIPL (subC C M) A)
    (χ : PLLFormula) :
    Nonempty (LaxND [A] (subC C (substP p χ M)))
docstring:
**∀-side upper bound (the constraint route reaches the whole
substitution fragment)**: the IPC ∀p-value of `M^C` derives the
translation of EVERY substitution instance `M[p := χ]` — via the
bridge `(M[p := χ])^C = (M^C)[p := χ^C]` and substitution through the
derivation `A ⊢ M^C`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.derives
signature: instance derives the IPC ∃p-value of `M^C`. -/
docstring: **∃-side instance bound (dual)**: every translated substitution

name: PLLND.SemUI.ctxEx_ge_instance
signature:
theorem ctxEx_ge_instance {p : String} {C : StdCtx} {M E : PLLFormula}
    (hCp : CtxPFree p C) (hE : IsIPCEx p isIPL (subC C M) E)
    (χ : PLLFormula) :
    Nonempty (LaxND [subC C (substP p χ M)] E)

name: PLLND.SemUI.ctx_sandwich_all
signature:
theorem ctx_sandwich_all {p : String} {C : StdCtx} {M ξ A : PLLFormula}
    (hCipl : CtxIsIPL C) (hCp : CtxPFree p C)
    (hval : IsSemAll p M ξ)
    (hA : IsIPCAll p isIPL (subC C M) A) :
    Nonempty (LaxND [subC C ξ] A) ∧
    ∀ χ, Nonempty (LaxND [A] (subC C (substP p χ M)))
docstring:
**The ∀-sandwich**: if `ξ` is the semantic ∀p-value of `M`
(`IsSemAll`) and `A` is the IPC ∀p-value of the translation `M^C`,
then

    ξ^C ⊢ A   and   A ⊢ (M[p := χ])^C for every χ.

So the constraint route computes a value squeezed between the
translated semantic value and the translated substitution instances —
it agrees with the ladder route EXACTLY on the substitution fragment,
and the residual gap `A ⊬ ξ^C` (oracle-witnessed at `M = ◯p ⊃ p`) is
precisely the frame-changing content (`lowT`/`sideT`).

name: PLLND.SemUI.ctx_sandwich_ex
signature:
theorem ctx_sandwich_ex {p : String} {C : StdCtx} {M ξ E : PLLFormula}
    (hCipl : CtxIsIPL C) (hCp : CtxPFree p C)
    (hval : IsSemEx p M ξ)
    (hE : IsIPCEx p isIPL (subC C M) E) :
    (∀ χ, Nonempty (LaxND [subC C (substP p χ M)] E)) ∧
    Nonempty (LaxND [E] (subC C ξ))
docstring:
**The ∃-sandwich** (dual): with `ξ` the semantic ∃p-value and `E`
the IPC ∃p-value of `M^C`,

    (M[p := χ])^C ⊢ E for every χ,   and   E ⊢ ξ^C.

name: PLLND.SemUI.DescPack
signature:
structure DescPack (C K : ConstraintModel) (p : String)
    (dom : String → Prop) where
  R : C.W → K.W → Prop
  atoms : ∀ {c k}, R c k → ∀ q, q ≠ p → dom q →
    (c ∈ C.V q ↔ k ∈ K.V q)
  fall : ∀ {c k}, R c k → (c ∈ C.F ↔ k ∈ K.F)
  iforth : ∀ {c k}, R c k → ∀ {v}, C.Ri c v →
    (∃ k', K.Ri k k' ∧ R v k') ∨ v ∈ C.F
  kback : ∀ {c k}, R c k → ∀ {k'}, K.Ri k k' →
    ∃ v, C.Ri c v ∧ R v k'
  mforth : ∀ {c k}, R c k → ∀ {u}, C.Rm c u →
    ∃ s, K.Rm k s ∧ (R u s ∨ (u ∈ C.F ∧ s ∈ K.F))
  mback : ∀ {c k}, R c k → ∀ {s}, K.Rm k s →
    ∃ u, C.Rm c u ∧ (R u s ∨ u ∈ C.F)

name: PLLND.SemUI.descGraftBase
signature:
def descGraftBase (P : DescPack C K p dom) : ConstraintModel where
  W
docstring:
The graft frame: base ⊎ R-related fibres.  Fibres climb both
coordinates, with the K-side edge relaxed into fallible K-worlds;
fibres re-enter the base only at fallible worlds; all valuations and
fallibility from the base coordinate.

name: PLLND.SemUI.descSet
signature: def descSet (P : DescPack C K p dom) : Set (descGraftBase P).W
docstring:
The graft decoration: `p` from the K-coordinate on the fibres, the
fallible worlds on the base.

name: PLLND.SemUI.descSet_hered
signature:
theorem descSet_hered (P : DescPack C K p dom) :
    ∀ {a b}, (descGraftBase P).Ri a b → a ∈ descSet P → b ∈ descSet P

name: PLLND.SemUI.descSet_full
signature:
theorem descSet_full (P : DescPack C K p dom) :
    ∀ {a}, a ∈ (descGraftBase P).F → a ∈ descSet P

name: PLLND.SemUI.descGraft
signature: def descGraft (P : DescPack C K p dom) : ConstraintModel
docstring:
The description graft: the frame with `p` redecorated from the
K-coordinate.

name: PLLND.SemUI.descGraft_pbisim
docstring:
**The graft is a p-variant of the base**: base-identity ∪
projection to the base coordinate.  No atom or fallibility condition
is consumed — both read the base coordinate by design.

name: PLLND.SemUI.descGraft_force_iff
signature:
theorem descGraft_force_iff (P : DescPack C K p dom) :
    ∀ {θ : PLLFormula}, (∀ q ∈ θ.atoms, q ≠ p → dom q) →
    ∀ (c : C.W) (k : K.W) (hR : P.R c k),
    ((descGraft P).force (.inr ⟨(c, k), hR⟩) θ ↔ K.force k θ)
docstring:
**A fibre forces exactly what its K-coordinate forces** — for
formulas whose atoms other than p are tracked by `dom`, and with ◯
INCLUDED: constraint witnesses transfer through the pack's m-clauses,
fallible escapes are absorbed on both sides (a fallible base witness
pairs with a fallible K-witness by `mforth`; an unpaired fallible
K-future is itself fallible in the graft by `fall`).

name: PLLND.SemUI.boxRowAmalgAll_of_desc
signature:
theorem boxRowAmalgAll_of_desc {p : String} {φ ψ : PLLFormula}
    {dom : String → Prop} (hat : ∀ q ∈ φ.atoms, q ≠ p → dom q)
    (h : ∀ (C : ConstraintModel) (x : C.W),
      (∀ y, C.Rm x y → ¬ C.force y ψ) →
      ∃ (K : ConstraintModel) (P : DescPack C K p dom) (k : K.W),
        P.R x k ∧ ¬ K.force k φ.somehow) :
    BoxRowAmalgAll p φ ψ
docstring:
**The ∀-residue reduces to description-realisation**: per (C, x)
with a ψ-refuting row, exhibit a target model and a pack pairing x
with a ◯φ-refuting K-world; the graft does the rest.  With
K := `canonFin cl` the condition is finite combinatorics: a closure
triple with `◯φ ∈ fal`, realised over x (truth lemma).

name: PLLND.SemUI.boxRowAmalgEx_of_desc
signature:
theorem boxRowAmalgEx_of_desc {p : String} {φ ψ : PLLFormula}
    {dom : String → Prop} (hat : ∀ q ∈ φ.atoms, q ≠ p → dom q)
    (h : ∀ (C : ConstraintModel) (w : C.W),
      (∀ x, C.Ri w x → ∃ y, C.Rm x y ∧ C.force y ψ) →
      ∃ (K : ConstraintModel) (P : DescPack C K p dom) (k : K.W),
        P.R w k ∧ K.force k φ.somehow) :
    BoxRowAmalgEx p φ ψ
docstring:
**The ∃-residue reduces to description-realisation** dually: a
pack pairing w with a ◯φ-forcing K-world (`◯φ ∈ val` canonically).

def bigAnd : List PLLFormula → PLLFormula
  | [] => truePLL
  | [φ] => φ
  | φ :: ψ :: l => φ.and (bigAnd (ψ :: l))
docstring:
Finite conjunction; the singleton case avoids a trailing `⊤`
(`truePLL = ⊥ ⊃ ⊥` has crank 1), so a NONEMPTY conjunction's crank is
the maximum of its members'.

signature: @[simp] theorem bigAnd_nil : bigAnd [] = truePLL

name: PLLND.SemUI.crank_bigAnd_le
signature:
theorem crank_bigAnd_le {r : Nat} :
    ∀ {T : List PLLFormula}, T ≠ [] → (∀ D ∈ T, crank D ≤ r) →
      crank (bigAnd T) ≤ r
  | [], h, _ => absurd rfl h
  | [E], _, h => h E (.head _)
  | E :: F :: l, _, h => by
      have h₁

name: PLLND.SemUI.atoms_bigAnd
signature:
theorem atoms_bigAnd {Q : String → Prop} :
    ∀ {T : List PLLFormula}, (∀ D ∈ T, ∀ a ∈ D.atoms, Q a) →
      ∀ a ∈ (bigAnd T).atoms, Q a
  | [], _, a, ha => by simp [truePLL] at ha
  | [E], h, a, ha => h E (.head _) a ha
  | E :: F :: l, h, a, ha => by
      rcases mem_atoms_and.mp ha with h' | h'
      · exact h E (.head _) a h'
      · exact atoms_bigAnd (fun D hD => h D (.tail _ hD)) a h'

signature:
theorem crank_bigOr_le {r : Nat} :
    ∀ {S : List PLLFormula}, (∀ D ∈ S, crank D ≤ r) → crank (bigOr S) ≤ r
  | [], _ => by simp [crank]
  | E :: l, h => by
      have h₁

      ∀ a ∈ (bigOr S).atoms, Q a
  | [], _, a, ha => by simp at ha
  | E :: l, h, a, ha => by

      · exact h E (.head _) a h'
      · exact atoms_bigOr (fun D hD => h D (.tail _ hD)) a h'

    ∀ {T : List PLLFormula} {D : PLLFormula}, D ∈ T → Deriv [bigAnd T] D
  | [], _, h => nomatch h
  | [E], D, h => by
      obtain rfl : D = E
docstring: A finite conjunction proves each of its members.

name: PLLND.SemUI.Deriv.bigAndIntro
signature:
theorem Deriv.bigAndIntro {Γ : List PLLFormula} :
    ∀ {T : List PLLFormula}, (∀ D ∈ T, Deriv Γ D) → Deriv Γ (bigAnd T)
  | [], _ => Deriv.impIntro (Deriv.iden (.head _))
  | [E], h => h E (.head _)
  | E :: _ :: _, h =>
      Deriv.andIntro (h E (.head _))
        (Deriv.bigAndIntro fun D hD => h D (.tail _ hD))

      rcases List.mem_cons.mp h with rfl | h'
      · exact Deriv.orIntro1 (Deriv.iden (.head _))
      · exact Deriv.orIntro2 (Deriv.bigOrIntroT h')

name: PLLND.SemUI.comps
signature:
def comps (V : List String) : Nat → List PLLFormula
  | 0 => .falsePLL :: V.map .prop
  | 1 => comps V 0 ++ implList (dnfL (comps V 0))
  | (r+2) => comps V (r+1) ++ implList (dnfL (comps V (r+1)))
      ++ boxList (dnfL (comps V r))

name: PLLND.SemUI.comps_zero
signature:
theorem comps_zero (V : List String) :
    comps V 0 = .falsePLL :: V.map .prop

name: PLLND.SemUI.comps_one

signature:

    comps V (r+2) = comps V (r+1) ++ implList (dnfL (comps V (r+1)))
      ++ boxList (dnfL (comps V r))

signature:
theorem comps_succ_append (V : List String) :
    ∀ r : Nat, ∃ rest, comps V (r+1) = comps V r ++ rest
  | 0 => ⟨_, comps_one V⟩
  | r+1 =>
      ⟨implList (dnfL (comps V (r+1))) ++ boxList (dnfL (comps V r)), by
        rw [comps_add_two, List.append_assoc]⟩

    ∀ P ∈ comps V r, P ∈ comps V (r+1)

name: PLLND.SemUI.dnfL_atoms
PLLND.SemUI.comps_crank
signature:
theorem comps_crank (V : List String) : ∀ r : Nat, ∀ P ∈ comps V r, crank P ≤ r
  | 0 => by
      intro P hP
      rw [comps_zero] at hP
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp hP with rfl | hP
      · simp [crank]
      · obtain ⟨b, _, rfl⟩

name: PLLND.SemUI.comps_atoms
signature:
theorem comps_atoms (V : List String) :
    ∀ r : Nat, ∀ P ∈ comps V r, ∀ a ∈ P.atoms, a ∈ V
  | 0 => by
      intro P hP a ha
      rw [comps_zero] at hP
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp hP with rfl | hP
      · simp at ha
      · obtain ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩

name: PLLND.SemUI.implList_dnfL_subset
signature:
theorem implList_dnfL_subset (V : List String) :
    ∀ s : Nat, ∀ P ∈ implList (dnfL (comps V s)), P ∈ comps V (s+1)
  | 0 => by
      intro P hP
      rw [comps_one]
      exact List.mem_append_right _ hP
  | t+1 => by
      intro P hP
      rw [comps_add_two]
      exact List.mem_append_left _ (List.mem_append_right _ hP)

name: PLLND.SemUI.boxList_dnfL_subset
signature:
theorem boxList_dnfL_subset (V : List String) (s : Nat) :
    ∀ P ∈ boxList (dnfL (comps V s)), P ∈ comps V (s+2)

name: PLLND.SemUI.canonicalise
signature:
theorem canonicalise (V : List String) (s : Nat) (ds : List (List PLLFormula))
    (h : ∀ S ∈ ds, S ≠ [] ∧ ∀ P ∈ S, P ∈ comps V s) :
    ∃ D ∈ dnfL (comps V s), Interd (bigOr (ds.map bigAnd)) D
docstring:
**Canonicalisation**: any DNF datum over `comps V s` is
interderivable with a MEMBER of the fixed finite list
`dnfL (comps V s)`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.toDNF
signature:
theorem toDNF (V : List String) :
    ∀ (φ : PLLFormula) (r : Nat), crank φ ≤ r → (∀ a ∈ φ.atoms, a ∈ V) →
    ∃ ds : List (List PLLFormula),
      (∀ S ∈ ds, S ≠ [] ∧ ∀ P ∈ S, P ∈ comps V r) ∧
      Interd φ (bigOr (ds.map bigAnd))
docstring:
**Normal form**: every formula of crank ≤ r over atoms in `V` is
interderivable with a disjunction of nonempty conjunctions of members
of `comps V r`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.frag_reps_exist'
signature:
theorem frag_reps_exist' (V : Finset String) (r : Nat) :
    ∃ L : List PLLFormula,
      (∀ D ∈ L, crank D ≤ r ∧ ∀ a ∈ D.atoms, a ∈ V) ∧
      ∀ φ : PLLFormula, crank φ ≤ r → (∀ a ∈ φ.atoms, a ∈ V) →
        ∃ D ∈ L, Nonempty (LaxND [φ] D) ∧ Nonempty (LaxND [D] φ)
docstring:
**Fragment finiteness up to interderivability** (Litak–Visser
Thm 4.5 analogue for PLL): the finite list `dnfL (comps V.toList r)`
contains, up to interderivability, every formula of crank ≤ r over
atoms in `V`, and all its members satisfy the same bounds.

name: from
signature:
theorem from its two claims, with the root pair admissible and
forcing at the root converted through the descriptions functor.  The
two claims that carry the mathematics are stated as named `sorry`s:

name: PLLND.SemUI.canonDepth
signature: def canonDepth (cl : Finset PLLFormula) (T : (canonFin cl).W) : Nat
docstring:
Depth of a canonical theory: how many closure formulas its `val`
is still missing.  The budget financier: strict extensions strictly
drop it.

name: PLLND.SemUI.canonDepth_le
signature:
theorem canonDepth_le (cl : Finset PLLFormula) (T : (canonFin cl).W) :
    canonDepth cl T ≤ cl.card

name: PLLND.SemUI.canonDepth_lt
docstring:
**Strict extensions strictly drop the depth**: a proper
`val`-inclusion between canonical theories loses at least one unit of
budget.

name: PLLND.SemUI.promise_blocks_row
docstring:
**Promises block the canonical row**: a formula promised by a
canonical world is validated by none of its `Rₘ`-successors — the
forward ◯-case refutes through the promise component alone.

name: PLLND.SemUI.trace_box_refuter
docstring:
**The forward refuter promises**: a world refuting `◯χ` has an
`Rᵢ`-successor whose description promises `χ`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.canon_box_dichotomy
signature:
theorem canon_box_dichotomy {cl : Finset PLLFormula} (hcl : SubClosed cl)
    {χ : PLLFormula} (hbox : χ.somehow ∈ cl) (hχ : χ ∈ cl)
    (T : (canonFin cl).W) (h : χ.somehow ∈ T.1.val) :
    χ ∈ T.1.val ∨
      ∃ S : (canonFin cl).W, (canonFin cl).Rm T S ∧ χ ∈ S.1.val ∧
        canonDepth cl S < canonDepth cl T
docstring:
**The backward dichotomy (reflexivity rescue)**: a validated `◯χ`
has a canonical row-witness that either is the world itself (`χ`
already validated — `Rₘ` is reflexive, so no bisimulation move is
spent) or strictly grows the theory, so the move is financed by the
depth drop exactly as in the Litak–Visser strict case.  This replaces
their <-maximality trick, which needs converse well-foundedness.

name: PLLND.SemUI.imp_val_of_val
docstring:
Validated consequents validate their implications (deductive
closure by the K-combinator): half of the ⊃-case split.

name: PLLND.SemUI.imp_unval_cases
signature:
theorem imp_unval_cases {cl : Finset PLLFormula} (hcl : SubClosed cl)
    {ξ ζ : PLLFormula} (T : (canonFin cl).W) (himp : ξ.ifThen ζ ∈ cl)
    (h : ξ.ifThen ζ ∉ T.1.val) :
    (ξ ∈ T.1.val ∧ ζ ∈ T.1.fal) ∨ ξ ∉ T.1.val
docstring:
**The ⊃-case split, exhaustive with guaranteed strictness**: an
unvalidated implication either fails at the world itself (antecedent
validated, consequent falsified — refute in place, no move) or its
antecedent is unvalidated, and then any refuting witness forces a
formula the theory lacks — the strict-growth trick that ports from
Litak–Visser unchanged.

name: PLLND.SemUI.traceT_val_ssubset
signature:
theorem traceT_val_ssubset {C : ConstraintModel} {cl : Finset PLLFormula}
    {k v : C.W} (hkv : C.Ri k v) {ξ : PLLFormula} (hξcl : ξ ∈ cl)
    (hforce : C.force v ξ) (hnew : ξ ∉ (traceT C cl k).val) :
    (traceT C cl k).val ⊂ (traceT C cl v).val
docstring:
**Strict growth of descriptions**: a witness above `k` forcing a
tracked formula the description of `k` lacks strictly extends the
`val`-trace — the depth financier for all forward strict cases.

name: PLLND.SemUI.traceT_mfal_empty_of_fallible
docstring:
**Fallible row-members erase promises**: descriptions of worlds
whose row hits the fallible set promise nothing (fallible worlds force
everything).

name: PLLND.SemUI.canonTop
signature: def canonTop (cl : Finset PLLFormula) : (canonFin cl).W
docstring:
The canonical top: everything validated, nothing falsified,
nothing promised.  Consistent outright, fallible once `⊥ ∈ cl`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.canonTop_fallible
signature:
theorem canonTop_fallible {cl : Finset PLLFormula} (hcl : SubClosed cl) :
    canonTop cl ∈ (canonFin cl).F

name: PLLND.SemUI.rm_canonTop_iff
signature:
theorem rm_canonTop_iff {cl : Finset PLLFormula} (Δ : (canonFin cl).W) :
    (canonFin cl).Rm Δ (canonTop cl) ↔ Δ.1.mfal = ∅
docstring:
A canonical world reaches the top along `Rₘ` exactly when it
promises nothing — where the fallible escapes of the m-zigzag land.

name: PLLND.SemUI.WitTriple
signature:
structure WitTriple (cl : Finset PLLFormula)
    (B : LayeredBisimE (fun a => a ≠ p) K M)
    (Δ : (canonFin cl).W) (m : M.W) where
  k' : K.W
  k : K.W
  m' : M.W
  hΔk : (traceT K cl k) = Δ.1
  hΔk' : (traceT K cl k') = Δ.1
  hik : K.Ri k' k
  him : M.Ri m' m
  hZ' : B.Z (2 * canonDepth cl Δ + 1) k' m'
  hZ : B.Z (2 * canonDepth cl Δ) k m
docstring:
**Witnessing triple** for a pair ⟨Δ, m⟩ (Litak–Visser Lemma 5.4):
worlds k′ ≼ k of K both describing Δ, a shadow m′ ≼ m, with the
layered links k′ Z_{2d+1} m′ and k Z_{2d} m, d the canonical depth of
Δ.

name: PLLND.SemUI.witAmalgam
signature:
def witAmalgam : ConstraintModel where
  W
docstring:
The amalgam: admissible pairs ⟨Δ, m⟩, relations componentwise
(the canonical side carries the promise-aware `Rₘ`).  Valuation in
the `descGraft` discipline rather than Litak–Visser's union clause:
atoms other than `p` and fallibility read the M-COORDINATE (the
canonical model forces every out-of-closure atom — the filtration
convention — so a union valuation would break the p-variant claim on
untracked atoms); `p` reads the theory coordinate, with the
M-fallibility disjunct restoring fullness on F.

name: PLLND.SemUI.wit_pbisim
signature:
theorem wit_pbisim :
    ∃ C : PBisim p M (witAmalgam cl B),
      ∀ (q : (witAmalgam cl B).W), C.Z q.1.2 q
docstring:
**Claim 1 (their proof of Lemma 5.4; OPEN)**: the projection to
the M-coordinate is an unbounded bisimulation off p — the amalgam is
a p-variant of M.  Proof shape: Z := graph of the projection; zig is
componentwise; zag maintains a witnessing triple for the moved pair
by the two-case budget argument, with the Henkin-side move supplied
by `trace_iforth` (Rᵢ) resp. `trace_mforth` (Rₘ, promises included)
and the depth drop `canonDepth_lt` paying for the fresh triple in the
strictly-up case.  Atoms off p: for a ≠ p tracked in the pair, the
theory coordinate and the M-coordinate agree through the triple's
links (their displayed "Δ ⊩ p ⇔ k ⊩ p ⇔ m ⊩ p"); fallibility: the
links match fallibility at every level.

name: PLLND.SemUI.wit_force
signature:
theorem wit_force (hcl : SubClosed cl) :
    ∀ (q : (witAmalgam cl B).W) (φ : PLLFormula), φ ∈ cl →
      ((witAmalgam cl B).force q φ ↔ φ ∈ q.1.1.1.val)
docstring:
**Claim 2 (their proof of Lemma 5.4; OPEN)**: a pair forces a
closure formula iff its theory coordinate contains it.  Induction on
the adequate set; ⊃ spends one i-zigzag, ◯ an i-zigzag and an
m-zigzag; the truth-lemma infrastructure of `canonFin` bridges
membership and canonical forcing; fallible escapes absorb as in
`descGraft_force_iff`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.amalgamation_assembled
signature:
theorem amalgamation_assembled (hcl : SubClosed cl)
    (k₀ : K.W) (m₀ : M.W)
    (hB : B.Z (2 * cl.card + 1) k₀ m₀) :
    ∃ (N : ConstraintModel) (C : PBisim p M N) (n₀ : N.W),
      C.Z m₀ n₀ ∧ ∀ φ ∈ cl, (N.force n₀ φ ↔ K.force k₀ φ)
docstring:
**The amalgamation theorem, assembled**: from a layered link of
budget `2·cl.card + 1` between k₀ and m₀, a p-variant of M whose
distinguished world agrees with k₀ on the whole closure.  The root
pair is ⟨description of k₀, m₀⟩, admissible by the degenerate
witnessing triple (k₀, k₀, m₀) after stepping the budget down to the
root theory's depth; forcing at the root converts through the
descriptions functor.

name: PLLND.SemUI.subsOf
signature:
def subsOf : PLLFormula → List PLLFormula
  | .prop a     => [.prop a]
  | .falsePLL   => [.falsePLL]
  | .and A B    => (A.and B) :: (subsOf A ++ subsOf B)
  | .or A B     => (A.or B) :: (subsOf A ++ subsOf B)
  | .ifThen A B => (A.ifThen B) :: (subsOf A ++ subsOf B)
  | .somehow A  => A.somehow :: subsOf A
docstring: All subformulas (including the formula itself).

name: PLLND.SemUI.rungsIn
signature: def rungsIn (M : PLLFormula) : List PLLFormula
docstring:
The closed-fragment rungs occurring in `M`: its atom-free
subformulas.

name: PLLND.SemUI.rungsIn_closed

name: PLLND.SemUI.rungsIn_pfree
signature:
theorem rungsIn_pfree {p : String} {M χ : PLLFormula}

name: PLLND.SemUI.poolAll
signature: def poolAll (p : String) (M : PLLFormula) : List PLLFormula
docstring:
The ∀-side pool: the two transforms, then the substitution
instances at the BASE rungs ⊥, ⊤, ◯⊥ and at every rung occurring in
`M`.

CORRECTION (2026-07-19, certified by the law sweep): the
occurring-rungs-only pool is REFUTED — witness `((◯p)⊃p)⊃p`, whose
Peirce pivot ◯p contains p, so it has NO atom-free subformulas and
the occurring-only pool degenerates to the fixed basis, which
provably fails there (`occurring_only_insufficient` below, a
`decide`-checked countermodel).  The base instance ◯⊥ is needed
unconditionally: `M[p:=◯⊥] ≡ ◯⊥` is the value of that witness.

name: PLLND.SemUI.poolEx
signature: def poolEx (p : String) (M : PLLFormula) : List PLLFormula
docstring:
The ∃-side pool: additionally the ◯⊥ instance (the fixed basis's
fifth generator).

name: PLLND.SemUI.allCandP
signature: def allCandP (p : String) (M : PLLFormula) : PLLFormula
docstring: The per-instance ∀-candidate: the conjunction of the pool.

name: PLLND.SemUI.exCandP
signature: def exCandP (p : String) (M : PLLFormula) : PLLFormula
docstring: The per-instance ∃-candidate: the disjunction of the pool.

name: PLLND.SemUI.poolAll_pfree
signature:
theorem poolAll_pfree {p : String} {M : PLLFormula} :

name: PLLND.SemUI.poolEx_pfree

name: PLLND.SemUI.allCandP_pfree

name: PLLND.SemUI.bigOr_pfree
signature:
theorem bigOr_pfree {p : String} :
    ∀ {L : List PLLFormula}, (∀ ξ ∈ L, p ∉ ξ.atoms) →
      p ∉ (Ctx.bigOr L).atoms
  | [], _ => by simp [Ctx.bigOr]
  | ξ :: L, h => by
      intro hm
      rcases (by simpa [Ctx.bigOr] using hm :
          p ∈ ξ.atoms ∨ p ∈ (Ctx.bigOr L).atoms) with hm | hm
      · exact h ξ (List.mem_cons_self ..) hm
      · exact bigOr_pfree (fun χ hχ => h χ (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hχ)) hm
