docstring:
**∀-reduction**: if the per-instance pool reconstructs `M`, its
conjunction is the ∀p-value.  Via the full-basis certificate criterion
with `χs := ⊥ :: ⊤ :: rungsIn M`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.isSemEx_of_poolRec

    (d : LaxND [M] (exCandP p M)) : IsSemEx p M (exCandP p M)
docstring:
**∃-reduction**: if `M` derives the pool disjunction, that
disjunction is the ∃p-value — a world forcing a disjunct has the
corresponding p-variant forcing `M` (truth-set decorations for the
substitution instances, the doubled model for `lowT`, the levelled
model for `sideT`; fallible worlds force the ⊥-instance variant).

name: PLLND.SemUI.ReconLawAll
signature: def ReconLawAll : Prop
docstring:
**The per-instance reconstruction law, ∀-side (OPEN).**  For every
one-variable `M`, the pool conjunction derives `M` back.  Evidence:
every formula of weight ≤ 7 (2758 sequents), the depth-3/4 battery,
and every named witness including the Peirce family; no counterexample
known.

name: PLLND.SemUI.ReconLawEx
signature: def ReconLawEx : Prop
docstring: **The per-instance reconstruction law, ∃-side (OPEN).**

name: PLLND.SemUI.onevar_definable_of_laws
signature:
theorem onevar_definable_of_laws (hA : ReconLawAll) (hE : ReconLawEx) :
    ∀ (p : String) (M : PLLFormula), M.atoms ⊆ {p} →
      (∃ ψ, IsSemAll p M ψ) ∧ (∃ ψ, IsSemEx p M ψ)
docstring: The law yields one-variable definability, both quantifiers.

The sweep's countermodel: 0 < 1 < 2, Rₘ rigid except 1 → 2, top

name: PLLND.SemUI.crank
signature:
def crank : PLLFormula → Nat
  | .prop _ => 0
  | .falsePLL => 0
  | .and φ ψ => max (crank φ) (crank ψ)
  | .or φ ψ => max (crank φ) (crank ψ)
  | .ifThen φ ψ => max (crank φ) (crank ψ) + 1
  | .somehow φ => crank φ + 2
docstring:
Litak–Visser complexity, adapted: atoms and ⊥ cost 0, ∧/∨ take
the maximum, → adds 1, and ◯ adds 2 — its constraint-model clause
spends an Rᵢ-move AND an Rₘ-move.  (Calibration constant; their Lewis
arrow with its one-step clause costs 1.)

name: PLLND.SemUI.isBudget
signature:
def isBudget : PLLFormula → Bool
  | .prop _ => true
  | .ifThen _ _ => true
  | .somehow _ => true
  | _ => false
docstring:
The budget-financing count for an adequate set: its variables,
implications and ◯-formulas (their n_X).

name: PLLND.SemUI.nu
signature: def nu (X : Finset PLLFormula) : Nat

name: PLLND.SemUI.LayeredBisim
signature:
structure LayeredBisim (A : String → Prop) (M N : ConstraintModel) where
  Z : Nat → M.W → N.W → Prop
  mono : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z (n + 1) w w' → Z n w w'
  atoms : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z n w w' → ∀ a, A a → (w ∈ M.V a ↔ w' ∈ N.V a)
  fall : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z n w w' → (w ∈ M.F ↔ w' ∈ N.F)
  iforth : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z (n + 1) w w' → ∀ {v}, M.Ri w v →
    ∃ v', N.Ri w' v' ∧ Z n v v'
  iback : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z (n + 1) w w' → ∀ {v'}, N.Ri w' v' →
    ∃ v, M.Ri w v ∧ Z n v v'
  mforth : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z (n + 1) w w' → ∀ {u}, M.Rm w u →
    ∃ u', N.Rm w' u' ∧ Z n u u'
  mback : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z (n + 1) w w' → ∀ {u'}, N.Rm w' u' →
    ∃ u, M.Rm w u ∧ Z n u u'
docstring:
**Layered (bounded) bisimulation** for the protected alphabet
`A`: a level-indexed relation, downward closed, with atoms and
fallibility matched at every level and the four zigzags each spending
one level (their §4.3, with the fallibility clause PLL adds).

name: PLLND.SemUI.LayeredBisim.mono_le
signature:
theorem LayeredBisim.mono_le (B : LayeredBisim A M N) :
    ∀ {m n : Nat}, m ≤ n → ∀ {w w'}, B.Z n w w' → B.Z m w w'
docstring: Levels drop along `≤`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.LayeredBisim.ofABisim
signature:
def LayeredBisim.ofABisim (B : ABisim A M N) : LayeredBisim A M N where
  Z
docstring:
An unbounded bisimulation is a layered one at every level (the
constant family).

name: PLLND.SemUI.force_iff_of_layered
signature:
theorem force_iff_of_layered (B : LayeredBisim A M N) :
    ∀ {φ : PLLFormula} {n : Nat}, crank φ ≤ n →
    (∀ a ∈ φ.atoms, A a) →
    ∀ {w : M.W} {w' : N.W}, B.Z n w w' → (M.force w φ ↔ N.force w' φ)
docstring:
**A level-n link transfers formulas of complexity ≤ n** whose
atoms are protected.  The ⊃-case spends one level (one i-zigzag); the
◯-case spends two (an i-zigzag then an m-zigzag) — the reason ◯ costs
2 in `crank`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.force_iff_of_bisim_via_layered
signature:
theorem force_iff_of_bisim_via_layered (B : ABisim A M N)
    {φ : PLLFormula} (hA : ∀ a ∈ φ.atoms, A a)
    {w : M.W} {w' : N.W} (hZ : B.Z w w') :
    (M.force w φ ↔ N.force w' φ)
docstring:
Consistency test: the constant family recovers the unbounded
invariance theorem exactly.

name: PLLND.SemUI.LayeredBisimE
signature:
structure LayeredBisimE (A : String → Prop) (M N : ConstraintModel) where
  Z : Nat → M.W → N.W → Prop
  mono : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z (n + 1) w w' → Z n w w'
  atoms : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z n w w' → ∀ a, A a → (w ∈ M.V a ↔ w' ∈ N.V a)
  fall : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z n w w' → (w ∈ M.F ↔ w' ∈ N.F)
  iforth : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z (n + 1) w w' → ∀ {v}, M.Ri w v →
    (∃ v', N.Ri w' v' ∧ Z n v v') ∨ v ∈ M.F
  iback : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z (n + 1) w w' → ∀ {v'}, N.Ri w' v' →

  mforth : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z (n + 1) w w' → ∀ {u}, M.Rm w u →
    ∃ u', N.Rm w' u' ∧ (Z n u u' ∨ (u ∈ M.F ∧ u' ∈ N.F))
  mback : ∀ {n : Nat} {w w'}, Z (n + 1) w w' → ∀ {u'}, N.Rm w' u' →

Layered bisimulation with the WEAK m-escape: no obligation at a
fallible row-member.  This is the form fragment-agreement can
deliver; `force_iff` FAILS for it (`weak_escape_breaks_force_iff`).

name: PLLND.SemUI.chainFM

Two-point chain with a fallible top on the FULL constraint
relation (`Rₘ = Rᵢ`): the bottom forces ◯⊥ through the fallible

name: PLLND.SemUI.weak_escape_breaks_force_iff
signature:
theorem weak_escape_breaks_force_iff :
    ∃ (B : LayeredBisimW (fun _ => True) chainFM oneW),
      B.Z 2 false () ∧
      chainFM.force false (PLLFormula.falsePLL.somehow) ∧
      ¬ oneW.force () (PLLFormula.falsePLL.somehow)
docstring:
**The weak m-escape breaks rank preservation**: the constant
relation linking the bottom of `chainFM` with the world of `oneW`
satisfies every `LayeredBisimW` clause, yet ◯⊥ (complexity 2) holds
at the bottom — the fallible row-member supplies every witness — and
fails at the lone point.

non-fallible top `some false`, a fallible top `some true` reached by

docstring:
**Full agreement of the fork's bottom with the lone point**: the
fallible m-branch is invisible to every formula — its witnesses come
free at the bottom's own row, and every other future self-witnesses.

docstring:
**The pair escape is not derivable from agreement**: the fork's
bottom agrees with the lone point on EVERY formula, yet any
`LayeredBisimE` linking them at level 1 dies on `mforth` at the
fallible m-branch — the lone point's row has no fallible member.
(With `forkF_agree` this also separates logical indistinguishability
from escape-bisimilarity in PLL outright.)

name: PLLND.SemUI.chainF

Two-point chain with a fallible top and trivial rows: the
conservative extension that defeats the `fall` zigzag.

name: PLLND.SemUI.chainF_oneW_agree

**Conservativity of the fallible top** at rank ≤ 1: the bottom of
`chainF` agrees with the world of `oneW` on every variable-free
formula of complexity ≤ 1 (the fallible top forces everything, so it
never blocks an implication; ◯ needs complexity 2).

name: PLLND.SemUI.layered_of_frag_agree_refuted
signature:
theorem layered_of_frag_agree_refuted :
    ¬ (∀ (V : Finset String) (n : Nat) (M N : ConstraintModel)
        (w : M.W) (w' : N.W),
      (∀ χ : PLLFormula, crank χ ≤ n → (∀ a ∈ χ.atoms, a ∈ V) →
        (M.force w χ ↔ N.force w' χ)) →
      ∃ B : LayeredBisim (fun a => a ∈ V) M N, B.Z n w w')

**The refutation** (machine-checked): fragment-agreement does NOT
yield a layered bisimulation for PLL — the pillar-2 statement in the

name: PLLND.SemUI.amalgamation
signature:
theorem amalgamation (X : Finset PLLFormula) (hX : SubClosed X)
    (p : String) (K M : ConstraintModel) (k₀ : K.W) (m₀ : M.W)
    (B : LayeredBisim (fun a => a ≠ p) K M)
    (hB : B.Z (2 * nu X + 1) k₀ m₀) :
    ∃ (N : ConstraintModel) (C : PBisim p M N) (n₀ : N.W),
      C.Z m₀ n₀ ∧ ∀ φ ∈ X, (N.force n₀ φ ↔ K.force k₀ φ)
docstring:
**THE PLL AMALGAMATION LEMMA** (their Lemma 5.4 / Visser's Lemma
5.1; OPEN — the central open problem of the route, equivalent in
strength to the residues of the box-commutation law).

Given an adequate set X, a model K whose root k₀ is layered-bisimilar
to m₀ ∈ M at level 2·(nu X)+1 protecting everything but p, there is a
p-VARIANT of M (unbounded bisimulation!) whose root agrees with k₀ on
all of X.

Their proof shape to adapt: amalgam worlds = pairs ⟨Δ, m⟩ with Δ an
X-prime theory of the finite pre-Henkin model and m ∈ M, admissible
when a witnessing triple k′ ≼ k, k′ Z_{2d(k′)+1} m′, k Z_{2d(k′)} m
exists (d = Henkin depth of Δ); relations componentwise; atoms from
the union of the coordinates.  PLL additions needed: the fallibility
clauses (F-absorption as in `descGraft_force_iff`), the frame
conditions Rₘ ⊆ Rᵢ and reflexivity of Rₘ on the amalgam, and the
promise components of the canonical theories in the ◯-case (where
their ⊏-maximality trick, which uses irreflexivity/Löb, must be
replaced by idempotence-and-promise reasoning).

  | .falsePLL => true
  | .and φ ψ => boxFree φ && boxFree ψ
  | .or φ ψ => boxFree φ && boxFree ψ
  | .ifThen φ ψ => boxFree φ && boxFree ψ
  | .somehow _ => false
docstring: ◯-freeness, computably.

the fallible top: the new world forces everything, so it never
constrains an implication.  (False for `¬◯⊥`, which the top

◯⊥-cone**: if some world of some model refutes M (◯-free), then no ξ
derivable from `◯⊥` derives M — adjoin the fallible top: the refuting
world keeps refuting M but now forces `◯⊥`, hence ξ.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_value_of_derivable
docstring:
If `⊢ M` then any ∀p-value of M is derivable — the value is ⊤, in

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_value_bot_of_cones
signature:
theorem semAll_value_bot_of_cones {p : String} {M ψ : PLLFormula}
    (hM : boxFree M = true) (h : IsSemAll p M ψ)
    {D₁ : ConstraintModel} {d₁ : D₁.W} (hd₁ : ¬ D₁.force d₁ M)
    {D₂ : ConstraintModel} (hDF : D₂.F = ∅) {d₂ : D₂.W}
    (hd₂ : ¬ D₂.force d₂ M)
    (hcov : Nonempty (LaxND [PLLFormula.falsePLL.somehow] ψ) ∨
      Nonempty (LaxND [PLLFormula.falsePLL.somehow.ifThen .falsePLL] ψ) ∨
      Nonempty (LaxND [ψ] .falsePLL)) :
    Nonempty (LaxND [ψ] .falsePLL)
docstring:
**Agreement with IPC on ◯-free rows, modulo cone coverage**: an
underivable ◯-free M (refuted at a general world and at a
fallibility-free world) has its ∀p-value excluded from both cones; so
a value lying in either cone — or `≡ ⊥` — is `⊥`, Pitts's value.  The
coverage of RN(◯,{}) ∖ {⊥} by the two cones (every nonzero closed
formula derivable from `◯⊥` or from `¬◯⊥`) is the remaining OPEN step
to the unconditional collapse; it holds for every rung tested.

non-fallible Rₘ-stable world named `n₀`: that world's pair is present

covers are `bad`-named, so forcing one makes the world fallible, and
fallible worlds force `p` anyway.

theorem residue_obstruction {p n₀ : String} {X A ξ θ : PLLFormula}

    (hθR : (residue n₀).force PUnit.unit θ)
    (hΘR : ∀ ψ ∈ Θ, (residue n₀).force PUnit.unit ψ)
    (hξR : ¬ (residue n₀).force PUnit.unit ξ) :
    ¬ Nonempty (LaxND (A :: Θ) ξ)
docstring:
**Engine**: a p-free IPL premise θ that derives `X` and holds at
the residue point transports any `IsIPCAll`-value of `X` to the point
(spec + soundness); the point then blocks every derivation from
`A :: Θ` of anything it refutes.

name: PLLND.SemUI.residue_theta

name: PLLND.SemUI.fails_half_boxp_imp_p
signature:
theorem fails_half_boxp_imp_p {p n₀ : String} {bad : List String}
    {C : StdCtx} {A : PLLFormula} {Θ : List PLLFormula}
    (h : ResiduePair n₀ bad C) (hpn : p ≠ n₀) (hpb : p ∉ bad)
    (hA : IsIPCAll p isIPL
      (subC C ((PLLFormula.prop p).somehow.ifThen (.prop p))) A)
    (hΘ : ∀ ψ ∈ Θ, ∃ a, a ≠ n₀ ∧ ψ = negA a) :
    ¬ Nonempty (LaxND (A :: Θ) .falsePLL)
docstring:
**General fails-half, row `∀p.(◯p⊃p) = ⊥`.**  For ANY constraint
`C` carrying a residue pair at `n₀` (the Lemma-7 shape at a
non-fallible Rₘ-stable world), ANY `IsIPCAll`-value `A` of the
translation `(◯p⊃p)^C`, and ANY frame theory `Θ` of `n₀`-avoiding
negated atoms (in particular the fallibility axioms):
`A :: Θ` is CONSISTENT.  The translated PLL value is
`(∀p.(◯p⊃p))^C = ⊥^C = ⊥`, so `A` is not `Θ`-equivalent to it —
frame-relative constraint-commutation FAILS, provably, at every such
constraint.

name: PLLND.SemUI.SplitW
signature: abbrev SplitW (C : ConstraintModel) (z : C.W) : Type
docstring:
Worlds of the split: the original worlds, plus one copy of each
world in the Rᵢ-cluster of `z`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.splitRi
signature:
def splitRi (C : ConstraintModel) (z : C.W) : SplitW C z → SplitW C z → Prop
  | .inl x, .inl y => C.Ri x y
  | .inl x, .inr _ => C.Ri x z
  | .inr _, .inl y => C.Ri z y ∧ ¬ C.Ri y z
  | .inr _, .inr _ => True
docstring:
The split order: copies sit above everything below the cluster
(including the cluster itself), below the strict cone over it, and are
mutually related (as the cluster is).

name: PLLND.SemUI.splitRm
signature:
def splitRm (C : ConstraintModel) (z : C.W) : SplitW C z → SplitW C z → Prop
  | .inl x, .inl y => C.Rm x y
  | .inl _, .inr _ => False
  | .inr u, .inl y => C.Rm u.1 y ∧ ¬ C.Ri y z
  | .inr u, .inr t => C.Rm u.1 t.1
docstring:
The split constraint relation: the original one on originals, the
cluster's own `Rₘ`-structure between copies, and from a copy to an
original only along the duplicated world's *strict* `Rₘ`-successors.
No original world reaches a copy.

docstring:
Projection of the split onto the base model: each copy goes to the
world it duplicates.

name: PLLND.SemUI.splitVariant_pbisim
docstring:
**The projection is a p-bisimulation**: every world of the split
variant is a p-variant of its projection.  The m-zigzag at a copy is
exact because the copies carry the cluster's internal `Rₘ`-structure;
the two `by_cases` route an original-side successor to its copy when it
stays in the cluster and to itself when it escapes.

name: PLLND.SemUI.splitVariant_not_frontier
signature:
theorem splitVariant_not_frontier (C : ConstraintModel) (p : String)
    (z : C.W) (hz : ∀ u, C.Rm z u → u ∉ C.F) :
    ¬ (splitVariant C p z).force (.inl z)
      ((((PLLFormula.prop p).ifThen PLLFormula.falsePLL.somehow).ifThen
        (.prop p)).ifThen (.prop p))
docstring:
**The split refutes the frontier row** at any world whose
`Rₘ`-row is fallibility-free.  `z`'s copy `⋆` forces `p` but not `◯⊥`
(its constraint row is `z`'s own), so no cluster world can force
`p ⊃ ◯⊥`; every world above `z` outside the cluster forces `p`
outright.  Hence `z` forces `(p ⊃ ◯⊥) ⊃ p` — but `z` itself is
neither in the decoration nor fallible, so it does not force `p`.

name: PLLND.SemUI.semAll_frontier
signature:
theorem semAll_frontier (p : String) :
    IsSemAll p
      ((((PLLFormula.prop p).ifThen PLLFormula.falsePLL.somehow).ifThen
        (.prop p)).ifThen (.prop p))
      PLLFormula.falsePLL.somehow
docstring:
**`∀p.(((p ⊃ ◯⊥) ⊃ p) ⊃ p) = ◯⊥`** — the frontier-row value, by
the split.  Below `◯⊥` every future forces `p ⊃ ◯⊥` outright, so a
`(p⊃◯⊥)⊃p`-world forces `p`; conversely a world without `◯⊥` has a
future whose `Rₘ`-row is fallibility-free, and the split there is a
p-variant refuting the row.

provably cannot.

    ∃ (C : ConstraintModel) (cl : Finset PLLFormula) (c : C.W)
      (S : (canonFin cl).W),
      (canonFin cl).Rm (trace C cl c) S ∧
      ∀ u, C.Rm c u → ¬ (trace C cl u = S ∨ u ∈ C.F)
docstring:
**The m-back clause FAILS for the functor** (fallible escape
included): the description of the bottom of `chainQ` has a canonical
m-extension promising `q`, but neither world of the chain honours that
promise (the top forces `q`; the bottom's row reaches the top).

name: PLLND.SemUI.boxRowAmalgAll_of_realises
signature:
theorem boxRowAmalgAll_of_realises {p : String} {φ ψ : PLLFormula}
    {cl : Finset PLLFormula} (hcl : SubClosed cl)
    (hat : ∀ q ∈ φ.atoms, q ≠ p → PLLFormula.prop q ∈ cl)
    (hbox : φ.somehow ∈ cl)
    (h : ∀ (C : ConstraintModel) (x : C.W),
      (∀ y, C.Rm x y → ¬ C.force y ψ) →
      ∃ k : (canonFin cl).W,

        φ.somehow ∈ k.1.fal) :
    BoxRowAmalgAll p φ ψ
docstring:

`ψ`-refuting row, a closure triple with `◯φ ∈ fal` realised over `x`
discharges `BoxRowAmalgAll` (truth lemma + the realisability pack).

    (hbox : φ.somehow ∈ cl)

      (∀ x, C.Ri w x → ∃ y, C.Rm x y ∧ C.force y ψ) →
      ∃ k : (canonFin cl).W,

        φ.somehow ∈ k.1.val) :

docstring:

triple with `◯φ ∈ val` realised over `w`.

    (canonFin cl).force T χ ↔ χ ∈ T.1.val
docstring:
On the finite canonical model, forcing of closure formulas is
membership in `val` (both truth-lemma halves plus totality).

name: PLLND.SemUI.realises_force_iff
docstring:
**Realised descriptions agree with their base world on p-free
tracked formulas**: through the graft, `c` and `k` force exactly the
same `θ` whenever `p ∉ θ.atoms` and `θ`'s atoms are tracked
(bisimulation invariance on the base side, the forcing lemma on the
fibre side).

name: PLLND.SemUI.realises_val_iff
signature:
theorem realises_val_iff {cl : Finset PLLFormula} (hcl : SubClosed cl)
    {c : C.W} {k : (canonFin cl).W}
    (hR : Realises C (canonFin cl) p (fun q => PLLFormula.prop q ∈ cl) c k)
    {χ : PLLFormula} (hχcl : χ ∈ cl) (hpf : p ∉ χ.atoms)
    (hatoms : ∀ q ∈ χ.atoms, PLLFormula.prop q ∈ cl) :
    (χ ∈ k.1.val ↔ C.force c χ)
docstring:
Over the finite canonical model this pins the whole p-free part of
any realisable triple: `χ ∈ val` iff the base world forces `χ` — the
p-free part of a realisable description IS the p-free trace.  All
realisation freedom is p-relevant.

name: PLLND.SemUI.preTripleAll_cons_of_residue

theorem preTripleAll_cons_of_residue {p : String} {φ ψ : PLLFormula}

killing `◯φ` over `x` is a countermodel witnessing consistency of the

name: PLLND.SemUI.preTripleAll_extend

      T.1.mfal = (preTripleAll C cl p x φ).mfal
docstring:

the consistent ∀-side pre-triple to a closure-maximal triple with
`◯φ ∈ fal`, the pre-triple below it, and the promises exactly
preserved.

signature:
inductive SCh : Nat → List PLLFormula → PLLFormula → Prop
  | init {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {a : String}

  | botL {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula}
      (h : PLLFormula.falsePLL ∈ Γ) : SCh n Γ C
  | andR {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {A B : PLLFormula} :
      SCh n Γ A → SCh n Γ B → SCh (n + 1) Γ (A.and B)
  | andL {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {A B C : PLLFormula}
      (h : A.and B ∈ Γ) : SCh n (A :: B :: Γ) C → SCh (n + 1) Γ C
  | orR1 {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {A B : PLLFormula} :
      SCh n Γ A → SCh (n + 1) Γ (A.or B)
  | orR2 {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {A B : PLLFormula} :
      SCh n Γ B → SCh (n + 1) Γ (A.or B)
  | orL {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {A B C : PLLFormula}
      (h : A.or B ∈ Γ) :

  | impR {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {A B : PLLFormula} :
      SCh n (A :: Γ) B → SCh (n + 1) Γ (A.ifThen B)
  | impL {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {A B C : PLLFormula}
      (h : A.ifThen B ∈ Γ) :
      SCh n Γ A → SCh n (B :: Γ) C → SCh (n + 1) Γ C
  | laxR {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {A : PLLFormula} :
      SCh n Γ A → SCh (n + 1) Γ (A.somehow)
  | laxL {n : Nat} {Γ : List PLLFormula} {A B : PLLFormula}
      (h : A.somehow ∈ Γ) :

name: PLLND.SC.iden
signature:
theorem iden : ∀ (φ : PLLFormula) {Γ : List PLLFormula}, φ ∈ Γ → SC Γ φ
  | .prop a, _, h => init h
  | .falsePLL, _, h => botL h
  | .and A B, _, h =>
      andL h (andR (iden A (.head _)) (iden B (.tail _ (.head _))))
  | .or A B, _, h =>
      orL h (orR1 (iden A (.head _))) (orR2 (iden B (.head _)))
  | .ifThen A B, _, h =>
      impR (impL (.tail _ h) (iden A (.head _)) (iden B (.head _)))
  | .somehow A, _, h =>
      laxL h (laxR (iden A (.head _)))
docstring: General identity is admissible.

name: PLLND.cut_aux
signature:
theorem cut_aux : ∀ (k : Nat), ∀ {A : PLLFormula}, sizeOf A ≤ k →
    ∀ (nm : Nat), ∀ {n m : Nat} {Γ Δ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula},
    n + m ≤ nm → SCh n Γ A → SCh m Δ C →
    (∀ ψ ∈ Δ, ψ = A ∨ ψ ∈ Γ) → SC Γ C
docstring:

generalised: from `Γ ⊢ A` and `Δ ⊢ C` where every hypothesis of `Δ` is
either the cut formula `A` or in `Γ`, conclude `Γ ⊢ C`.  Lexicographic
induction on (size of the cut formula, sum of the two heights); the
principal `laxR`/`laxL` case is the extra reduction of F&M Figure 2.

name: PLLND.Tm.weight
signature:
def Tm.weight : ∀ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula}, Tm Γ φ → Nat
  | _, _, .var _ => 1
  | _, _, .abort _ t => t.weight + 1
  | _, _, .lam t => t.weight + 1
  | _, _, .app t s => t.weight + s.weight + 1
  | _, _, .pair t s => t.weight + s.weight + 1
  | _, _, .fst t => t.weight + 1
  | _, _, .snd t => t.weight + 1
  | _, _, .inl t => t.weight + 1
  | _, _, .inr t => t.weight + 1
  | _, _, .case t u₁ u₂ => t.weight + u₁.weight + u₂.weight + 1
  | _, _, .val t => t.weight + 1
  | _, _, .bind t u => 2 * t.weight + u.weight + 1
docstring: Weight: `bind` counts its scrutinee twice.

name: PLLND.Tm.weight_rename
signature:
theorem Tm.weight_rename : ∀ {Γ Δ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula}
    (t : Tm Γ φ) (ρ : Ren Γ Δ), (t.rename ρ).weight = t.weight
  | _, _, _, .var _, ρ => rfl
  | _, _, _, .abort _ t, ρ => by simp [Tm.rename, Tm.weight, t.weight_rename]
  | _, _, _, .lam t, ρ => by simp [Tm.rename, Tm.weight, t.weight_rename]
  | _, _, _, .app t s, ρ => by
      simp [Tm.rename, Tm.weight, t.weight_rename, s.weight_rename]
  | _, _, _, .pair t s, ρ => by
      simp [Tm.rename, Tm.weight, t.weight_rename, s.weight_rename]
  | _, _, _, .fst t, ρ => by simp [Tm.rename, Tm.weight, t.weight_rename]
  | _, _, _, .snd t, ρ => by simp [Tm.rename, Tm.weight, t.weight_rename]
  | _, _, _, .inl t, ρ => by simp [Tm.rename, Tm.weight, t.weight_rename]
  | _, _, _, .inr t, ρ => by simp [Tm.rename, Tm.weight, t.weight_rename]
  | _, _, _, .case t u₁ u₂, ρ => by
      simp [Tm.rename, Tm.weight, t.weight_rename, u₁.weight_rename,
        u₂.weight_rename]
  | _, _, _, .val t, ρ => by simp [Tm.rename, Tm.weight, t.weight_rename]
  | _, _, _, .bind t u, ρ => by
      simp [Tm.rename, Tm.weight, t.weight_rename, u.weight_rename]
docstring: Weight is invariant under renaming.

  | bindAssoc {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ χ : PLLFormula}
      (s : Tm Γ (somehow φ)) (t : Tm (φ :: Γ) (somehow ψ))

      AStep (.bind (.bind s t) u) (.bind s (.bind t (u.rename Ren.skip1)))
  | abortCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ .falsePLL} :
      AStep t t' → AStep (.abort φ t) (.abort φ t')
  | lamCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm (φ :: Γ) ψ} :

  | pairCong₁ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula}

  | pairCong₂ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula}

      AStep s s' → AStep (.pair t s) (.pair t s')
  | fstCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ (φ.and ψ)} :

  | sndCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ (φ.and ψ)} :

  | inrCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ ψ} :
      AStep t t' → AStep (.inr (φ := φ) t) (.inr t')
  | caseCong₀ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ χ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ (φ.or ψ)}
      {u₁ : Tm (φ :: Γ) χ} {u₂ : Tm (ψ :: Γ) χ} :

      {u₁ u₁' : Tm (φ :: Γ) χ} {u₂ : Tm (ψ :: Γ) χ} :

      {u₁ : Tm (φ :: Γ) χ} {u₂ u₂' : Tm (ψ :: Γ) χ} :
      AStep u₂ u₂' → AStep (.case t u₁ u₂) (.case t u₁ u₂')
  | valCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ φ} :

  | bindCong₂ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula}

The assoc fragment of `Step`: the reassociation redex and its

name: PLLND.AStep.toStep
signature:

name: PLLND.Tm.step?
signature:
def Tm.step? : ∀ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula} (t : Tm Γ φ),
    Option {t' : Tm Γ φ // Step t t'}
  | _, _, .var _ => none
  | _, _, .abort φ t =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', h⟩ => some ⟨.abort φ t', .abortCong h⟩
      | none => none
  | _, _, .lam t =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', h⟩ => some ⟨.lam t', .lamCong h⟩
      | none => none
  | _, _, .app t s =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', h⟩ => some ⟨.app t' s, .appCong₁ h⟩
      | none =>
          match s.step? with
          | some ⟨s', h⟩ => some ⟨.app t s', .appCong₂ h⟩
          | none => t.appRedex? s
  | _, _, .pair t s =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', h⟩ => some ⟨.pair t' s, .pairCong₁ h⟩
      | none =>
          match s.step? with
          | some ⟨s', h⟩ => some ⟨.pair t s', .pairCong₂ h⟩
          | none => none
  | _, _, .fst t =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', h⟩ => some ⟨.fst t', .fstCong h⟩
      | none => t.fstRedex?
  | _, _, .snd t =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', h⟩ => some ⟨.snd t', .sndCong h⟩
      | none => t.sndRedex?
  | _, _, .inl t =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', h⟩ => some ⟨.inl t', .inlCong h⟩
      | none => none
  | _, _, .inr t =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', h⟩ => some ⟨.inr t', .inrCong h⟩
      | none => none
  | _, _, .case t u₁ u₂ =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', h⟩ => some ⟨.case t' u₁ u₂, .caseCong₀ h⟩
      | none =>
          match u₁.step? with
          | some ⟨u₁', h⟩ => some ⟨.case t u₁' u₂, .caseCong₁ h⟩
          | none =>
              match u₂.step? with
              | some ⟨u₂', h⟩ => some ⟨.case t u₁ u₂', .caseCong₂ h⟩
              | none => t.caseRedex? u₁ u₂
  | _, _, .val t =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', h⟩ => some ⟨.val t', .valCong h⟩
      | none => none
  | _, _, .bind t u =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', h⟩ => some ⟨.bind t' u, .bindCong₁ h⟩
      | none =>
          match u.step? with
          | some ⟨u', h⟩ => some ⟨.bind t u', .bindCong₂ h⟩
          | none => t.bindRedex? u
docstring:
Certified one-step reduction: congruences (innermost subterms first),
then head-redex dispatch.  Returns a proof-carrying step or `none`.

name: PLLND.Tm.reduceFuel

def Tm.reduceFuel : ∀ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula},
    Nat → Tm Γ φ → Tm Γ φ × Bool
  | _, _, 0, t => (t, false)
  | _, _, fuel + 1, t =>
      match t.step? with
      | some ⟨t', _⟩ => t'.reduceFuel fuel
      | none => (t, true)
docstring:
The fueled normaliser: iterate `step?`.  Returns the final term and
whether it certified normality (`true` = ran to a stuck term).

name: PLLND.Steps
signature:
inductive Steps {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula} :
    Tm Γ φ → Tm Γ φ → Prop
  | refl (t : Tm Γ φ) : Steps t t
  | head {t t' t'' : Tm Γ φ} : Step t t' → Steps t' t'' → Steps t t''
docstring: Reflexive-transitive closure of `Step`.

name: PLLND.Tm.reduceFuel_sound
signature:
theorem Tm.reduceFuel_sound : ∀ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula}
    (fuel : Nat) (t : Tm Γ φ),
    Steps t (t.reduceFuel fuel).1 ∧
      ((t.reduceFuel fuel).2 = true → Nf (t.reduceFuel fuel).1)
  | _, _, 0, t => ⟨.refl t, by simp [Tm.reduceFuel]⟩
  | Γ, φ, fuel + 1, t => by
      simp only [Tm.reduceFuel]
      cases hs : t.step? with
      | some p =>
          obtain ⟨hsteps, hnf⟩
docstring:
**Soundness of the fueled normaliser**: the result is reachable by
reduction, and when it reports `true` the result is normal.

name: PLLND.Tm.rename_congr
signature:
theorem Tm.rename_congr : ∀ {Γ Δ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula}
    (t : Tm Γ φ) {ρ ρ' : Ren Γ Δ},
    (∀ {ψ : PLLFormula} (v : Var Γ ψ), ρ v = ρ' v) →
    t.rename ρ = t.rename ρ'
  | _, _, _, .var v, _, _, h => by simp [Tm.rename, h v]
  | _, _, _, .abort φ t, _, _, h => by
      simp [Tm.rename, t.rename_congr h]
  | _, _, _, .lam t, ρ, ρ', h => by
      simp only [Tm.rename]
      congr 1
      refine t.rename_congr ?_
      intro ψ v
      cases v with
      | here => rfl
      | there w => simp [Ren.lift, h w]
  | _, _, _, .app t s, _, _, h => by
      simp [Tm.rename, t.rename_congr h, s.rename_congr h]
  | _, _, _, .pair t s, _, _, h => by
      simp [Tm.rename, t.rename_congr h, s.rename_congr h]
  | _, _, _, .fst t, _, _, h => by simp [Tm.rename, t.rename_congr h]
  | _, _, _, .snd t, _, _, h => by simp [Tm.rename, t.rename_congr h]
  | _, _, _, .inl t, _, _, h => by simp [Tm.rename, t.rename_congr h]
  | _, _, _, .inr t, _, _, h => by simp [Tm.rename, t.rename_congr h]
  | _, _, _, .case t u₁ u₂, ρ, ρ', h => by
      simp only [Tm.rename]
      rw [t.rename_congr h]
      congr 1
      · exact u₁.rename_congr (fun {ψ} v => by
          cases v with
          | here => rfl
          | there w => simp [Ren.lift, h w])
      · exact u₂.rename_congr (fun {ψ} v => by
          cases v with
          | here => rfl
          | there w => simp [Ren.lift, h w])
  | _, _, _, .val t, _, _, h => by simp [Tm.rename, t.rename_congr h]
  | _, _, _, .bind t u, ρ, ρ', h => by
      simp only [Tm.rename]
      rw [t.rename_congr h]
      congr 1
      refine u.rename_congr ?_
      intro ψ v
      cases v with
      | here => rfl
      | there w => simp [Ren.lift, h w]

          | there w => rfl), t.subst_ids]
  | _, _, .app t s => by simp [Tm.subst, t.subst_ids, s.subst_ids]
  | _, _, .pair t s => by simp [Tm.subst, t.subst_ids, s.subst_ids]
  | _, _, .fst t => by simp [Tm.subst, t.subst_ids]
  | _, _, .snd t => by simp [Tm.subst, t.subst_ids]
  | _, _, .inl t => by simp [Tm.subst, t.subst_ids]
  | _, _, .inr t => by simp [Tm.subst, t.subst_ids]
  | _, _, .case t u₁ u₂ => by
      simp only [Tm.subst]
      rw [t.subst_ids]
      congr 1
      · rw [show u₁.subst Sub.ids.lift = u₁.subst Sub.ids from
          u₁.subst_congr (fun {ψ} v => by
            cases v with
            | here => rfl
            | there w => rfl), u₁.subst_ids]
      · rw [show u₂.subst Sub.ids.lift = u₂.subst Sub.ids from
          u₂.subst_congr (fun {ψ} v => by
            cases v with
            | here => rfl
            | there w => rfl), u₂.subst_ids]
  | _, _, .val t => by simp [Tm.subst, t.subst_ids]
  | _, _, .bind t u => by
      simp only [Tm.subst]
      rw [t.subst_ids]
      congr 1
      rw [show u.subst Sub.ids.lift = u.subst Sub.ids from
        u.subst_congr (fun {ψ} v => by
          cases v with
          | here => rfl
          | there w => rfl), u.subst_ids]

that `P` may assume itself at any `r`-predecessor of `a` (same `b`) and at

`f a` is the image of an `r`-predecessor of `a`, then accessibility of `a`
gives accessibility of `f a`.  This is the shape of every "SN is preserved
by a unary constructor / by renaming" lemma: `inv` is the step-inversion
fact for `f`.

  | abort {Γ : List PLLFormula} (φ : PLLFormula) :
      Tm Γ .falsePLL → Tm Γ φ
  | lam {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} :
      Tm (φ :: Γ) ψ → Tm Γ (φ.ifThen ψ)
  | app {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} :
      Tm Γ (φ.ifThen ψ) → Tm Γ φ → Tm Γ ψ
  | pair {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} :
      Tm Γ φ → Tm Γ ψ → Tm Γ (φ.and ψ)
  | fst {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} :
      Tm Γ (φ.and ψ) → Tm Γ φ
  | snd {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} :

  | inl {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} :

  | inr {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} :

      Tm Γ (φ.or ψ) → Tm (φ :: Γ) χ → Tm (ψ :: Γ) χ → Tm Γ χ
  | val {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula} :
      Tm Γ φ → Tm Γ (somehow φ)

      Tm Γ (somehow φ) → Tm (φ :: Γ) (somehow ψ) → Tm Γ (somehow ψ)

name: PLLND.Step
signature:
inductive Step : ∀ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula},
    Tm Γ φ → Tm Γ φ → Prop
  | beta {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} (t : Tm (φ :: Γ) ψ) (s : Tm Γ φ) :
      Step (.app (.lam t) s) (t.subst1 s)
  | fstPair {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} (t : Tm Γ φ) (s : Tm Γ ψ) :
      Step (.fst (.pair t s)) t
  | sndPair {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} (t : Tm Γ φ) (s : Tm Γ ψ) :
      Step (.snd (.pair t s)) s
  | caseInl {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ χ : PLLFormula} (s : Tm Γ φ) (u₁ : Tm (φ :: Γ) χ) (u₂ : Tm (ψ :: Γ) χ) :
      Step (.case (.inl s) u₁ u₂) (u₁.subst1 s)
  | caseInr {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ χ : PLLFormula} (s : Tm Γ ψ) (u₁ : Tm (φ :: Γ) χ) (u₂ : Tm (ψ :: Γ) χ) :
      Step (.case (.inr s) u₁ u₂) (u₂.subst1 s)
  | bindVal {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} (s : Tm Γ φ) (t : Tm (φ :: Γ) (somehow ψ)) :
      Step (.bind (.val s) t) (t.subst1 s)
  | bindAssoc {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ χ : PLLFormula} (s : Tm Γ (somehow φ))
      (t : Tm (φ :: Γ) (somehow ψ)) (u : Tm (ψ :: Γ) (somehow χ)) :
      Step (.bind (.bind s t) u)
        (.bind s (.bind t (u.rename Ren.skip1)))
  | abortCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ .falsePLL} :
      Step t t' → Step (.abort φ t) (.abort φ t')
  | lamCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm (φ :: Γ) ψ} :
      Step t t' → Step (.lam t) (.lam t')
  | appCong₁ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ (φ.ifThen ψ)} {s : Tm Γ φ} :
      Step t t' → Step (.app t s) (.app t' s)
  | appCong₂ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t : Tm Γ (φ.ifThen ψ)} {s s' : Tm Γ φ} :
      Step s s' → Step (.app t s) (.app t s')
  | pairCong₁ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ φ} {s : Tm Γ ψ} :
      Step t t' → Step (.pair t s) (.pair t' s)
  | pairCong₂ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t : Tm Γ φ} {s s' : Tm Γ ψ} :
      Step s s' → Step (.pair t s) (.pair t s')
  | fstCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ (φ.and ψ)} :
      Step t t' → Step (.fst t) (.fst t')
  | sndCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ (φ.and ψ)} :
      Step t t' → Step (.snd t) (.snd t')
  | inlCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ φ} :
      Step t t' → Step (.inl (ψ := ψ) t) (.inl t')
  | inrCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ ψ} :
      Step t t' → Step (.inr (φ := φ) t) (.inr t')
  | caseCong₀ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ χ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ (φ.or ψ)}
      {u₁ : Tm (φ :: Γ) χ} {u₂ : Tm (ψ :: Γ) χ} :
      Step t t' → Step (.case t u₁ u₂) (.case t' u₁ u₂)
  | caseCong₁ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ χ : PLLFormula} {t : Tm Γ (φ.or ψ)}
      {u₁ u₁' : Tm (φ :: Γ) χ} {u₂ : Tm (ψ :: Γ) χ} :
      Step u₁ u₁' → Step (.case t u₁ u₂) (.case t u₁' u₂)
  | caseCong₂ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ χ : PLLFormula} {t : Tm Γ (φ.or ψ)}
      {u₁ : Tm (φ :: Γ) χ} {u₂ u₂' : Tm (ψ :: Γ) χ} :
      Step u₂ u₂' → Step (.case t u₁ u₂) (.case t u₁ u₂')
  | valCong {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ φ} :
      Step t t' → Step (.val t) (.val t')
  | bindCong₁ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ (somehow φ)} {u : Tm (φ :: Γ) (somehow ψ)} :
      Step t t' → Step (.bind t u) (.bind t' u)
  | bindCong₂ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {t : Tm Γ (somehow φ)} {u u' : Tm (φ :: Γ) (somehow ψ)} :
      Step u u' → Step (.bind t u) (.bind t u')
docstring:
One-step reduction: β for every connective, the two monadic laws, and
congruence closure.  Intrinsic typing makes subject reduction definitional:
`Step` only relates terms of one sequent.

theorem iff_congr₂ {P P' Q Q' : PLLFormula}

      Δ ⊩ iffPLL X X' → Δ ⊩ iffPLL Y Y' → Δ ⊩ (conn X Y).ifThen (conn X' Y'))

PLLND.SetDeriv.iff_congr_or

name: PLLND.extensionality_setDeriv
signature:
theorem extensionality_setDeriv (a : String) (M N : PLLFormula) :
    ∀ C : PLLFormula,
      ({iffPLL M N} : Set PLLFormula) ⊩ iffPLL (substProp a M C) (substProp a N C)
  | .prop b => by
      by_cases h : b = a
      · simp only [substProp, if_pos h]
        exact of_mem rfl
      · simp only [substProp, if_neg h]
        exact iff_refl (.prop b)
  | .falsePLL => iff_refl _
  | .and φ ψ =>
      iff_congr_and (extensionality_setDeriv a M N φ) (extensionality_setDeriv a M N ψ)
  | .or φ ψ =>
      iff_congr_or (extensionality_setDeriv a M N φ) (extensionality_setDeriv a M N ψ)
  | .ifThen φ ψ =>
      iff_congr_imp (extensionality_setDeriv a M N φ) (extensionality_setDeriv a M N ψ)
  | .somehow φ =>
      iff_congr_somehow (extensionality_setDeriv a M N φ)
docstring:
**Strong extensionality** (F&M Theorem 2.5), set-level core:
from `M ≡ N` conclude `C[M] ≡ C[N]` for any context `C`.

signature: abbrev Ob

name: PLLND.Oc
signature: abbrev Oc

name: PLLND.Od
signature: abbrev Od

name: PLLND.Oe
signature: abbrev Oe

name: PLLND.ΓCIRC
signature: abbrev ΓCIRC : List PLLFormula
docstring: The gate netlist as a context `Γ = [gOR, gINV, gAND]`.

name: PLLND.circUp
signature: def circUp : Tm ΓCIRC (Oa.ifThen (Ob.ifThen Oc))
docstring:
**`CIRC↑` as a `Tm` proof term**: `Γ ⊢ ◯a ⊃ ◯b ⊃ ◯c`, i.e.
`gAND (gOR a b) (gINV b)`.  `b` fans out to `gOR` and `gINV` and reconverges
at `gAND`.

name: PLLND.envCIRC
signature: def envCIRC (δOR δINV δAND : ℕ) : Env (M := ℕ) B ΓCIRC
docstring: The gate environment for `CIRC`, parametric in the three gate delays.

name: PLLND.circUp_extract
signature:
theorem circUp_extract (δOR δINV δAND δa δb : ℕ) :
    (circUp.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envCIRC δOR δINV δAND) (δa, ()) (δb, ())).1
      = max (max δa δb + δOR) (δb + δINV) + δAND
docstring:
**Raw symbolic extraction, by `rfl`.**  With inputs `a, b` ready at times
`δa, δb`, `CIRC↑` extracts the composite delay
`max (max δa δb + δ_OR) (δb + δ_INV) + δ_AND` — Mendler's symbolic delay
*table* `T_OR, T_INV, T_AND` composed, computed by the kernel from the proof
term.

name: PLLND.circUp_rising
signature:
theorem circUp_rising (δOR δINV δAND : ℕ) :
    (circUp.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envCIRC δOR δINV δAND) (0, ()) (0, ())).1
      = max δOR δINV + δAND
docstring:
**The rising bound.**  With inputs available at time `0`, the extracted
bound is exactly Mendler's `δ_CIRC↑ = max(δ_OR, δ_INV) + δ_AND` — genuinely a
`max` over the two reconvergent branches.

name: PLLND.Ow
signature: abbrev Ow

name: PLLND.gateThenBuf
signature:
def gateThenBuf : Tm [Od.ifThen (Oe.ifThen Oc), (prop "c").ifThen Ow]
    (Od.ifThen (Oe.ifThen Ow))
docstring:
`Γ = [g : ◯x ⊃ ◯y ⊃ ◯z, buf : z ⊃ ◯w] ⊢ ◯x ⊃ ◯y ⊃ ◯w`, i.e.
`λ x y. bind (g x y) (λ z. buf z)`.  The `bind` is Mendler's `μ`.

name: PLLND.gateThenBuf_extract
signature:
theorem gateThenBuf_extract (δG δBUF δd δe : ℕ) :
    (gateThenBuf.eval (· + ·) 0 B
        (gate2 δG, (gate δBUF (fun _ => ()), PUnit.unit)) (δd, ()) (δe, ())).1
      = max δd δe + δG + δBUF
docstring:
**`μ = +` on `bind`, `σ = max` in the gate, one evaluation.**  The gate
emits `max δd δe + δ_G` (its `σ` then its own delay); the `bind` then adds the
buffer's `δ_BUF` — the outer `+` is the object-level monad multiplication.

name: PLLND.Γa1
signature: abbrev Γa1 : List PLLFormula
docstring:
The `a = 1` netlist: `◯d` is *given* (stable, since `a = 1`), so `gOR` is
gone.  `Γ = [gINV, gAND, ◯d, ◯b]`.

name: PLLND.circUp_a1
signature: def circUp_a1 : Tm Γa1 Oc
docstring:
**`CIRC↑` on the `a = 1` class**: `Γ ⊢ ◯c`, i.e. `gAND d (gINV b)`.
Note the total absence of `gOR` — the false path is not in the term.

name: PLLND.envA1
signature: def envA1 (δINV δAND δd δb : ℕ) : Env (M := ℕ) B Γa1
docstring: The `a = 1` environment (no `gOR`).

name: PLLND.circUp_a1_extract
signature:
theorem circUp_a1_extract (δINV δAND δd δb : ℕ) :
    (circUp_a1.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envA1 δINV δAND δd δb)).1
      = max δd (δb + δINV) + δAND
docstring:
**Raw extraction on the `a = 1` class, by `rfl`**: `max δd (δb + δ_INV) +
δ_AND`.  Only the `INV → AND` branch contributes a fresh delay; `δd` enters
merely as an already-stable input.

name: PLLND.circUp_a1_bound
signature:
theorem circUp_a1_bound (δINV δAND : ℕ) :
    (circUp_a1.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envA1 δINV δAND 0 0)).1 = δINV + δAND
docstring:
With `d` already stable (ready `0`) and `b` ready `0`, the `a = 1` bound is
`δ_INV + δ_AND` — a single reconvergent branch.

name: PLLND.dINV
signature: def dINV : ℕ
docstring: `sky130_fd_sc_hd__inv_1` nominal rising delay (ps).

name: PLLND.dOR
signature: def dOR : ℕ
docstring: `sky130_fd_sc_hd__or2_1` nominal rising delay (ps).

name: PLLND.dAND
signature: def dAND : ℕ
docstring: `sky130_fd_sc_hd__and2_1` nominal rising delay (ps).

name: PLLND.dTopo
signature: def dTopo : ℕ
docstring:
**The topological longest path** (structural, sensitisation-blind): the
longest input→`c` path is through `OR` or `INV`, both terminating at `AND`, so
`δ_topo = max(δ_OR, δ_INV) + δ_AND`.  This is what naive STA reports; it equals
the *full* `CIRC↑` bound (`circUp_rising`).

name: PLLND.falsePath_beats_topological
signature:
theorem falsePath_beats_topological :
    (circUp_a1.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envA1 dINV dAND 0 0)).1 < dTopo
docstring:
**The false-path punchline, kernel-checked.**  The delay extracted from
the `a = 1` proof (`130 ps`, `= δ_INV + δ_AND`) is **strictly below** the
topological longest path (`210 ps`, `= max(δ_OR, δ_INV) + δ_AND`): the
non-sensitisable `OR → AND` path is absent from the proof's constraint set, so
extraction beats topological STA by recognising the false path — *for free*.

signature: abbrev Oc4

signature: abbrev Ocout

name: PLLND.Γripple
signature: abbrev Γripple : List PLLFormula

name: PLLND.rippleTm
signature: def rippleTm : Tm Γripple Oc4
docstring: `cin` rippled through the 4-stage carry chain: `Γ ⊢ ◯c₄`.

name: PLLND.envRipple
signature: def envRipple (δc : ℕ) (tcin tp0 tp1 tp2 tp3 : ℕ) : Env (M := ℕ) B Γripple
docstring:
The ripple environment: four carry gates (delay `δc`) and the inputs
(`cin` and the `pᵢ`) ready at their given times.

name: PLLND.ripple_extract
signature:
theorem ripple_extract (δc tcin tp0 tp1 tp2 tp3 : ℕ) :
    (rippleTm.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envRipple δc tcin tp0 tp1 tp2 tp3)).1
      = max (max (max (max tcin tp0 + δc) tp1 + δc) tp2 + δc) tp3 + δc
docstring: **Raw ripple extraction, by `rfl`**: the fully-associated `max`/`+` chain.

name: PLLND.ripple_bound
signature:
theorem ripple_bound (δc : ℕ) :
    (rippleTm.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envRipple δc 0 0 0 0 0)).1 = 4 * δc
docstring:
**The ripple bound.**  With `cin` and every `pᵢ` ready at `0`, the block
ripple output `c₄` is ready at `4·δ_carry` — the long sub-path the false path
rides on.

name: PLLND.Γskip
signature: abbrev Γskip : List PLLFormula

name: PLLND.coutSkip
signature: def coutSkip : Tm Γskip Ocout
docstring:
The skip carry-out `Γ ⊢ ◯cout`: `muxSkip cin (aP (a01 p0 p1) (a23 p2 p3))`.
The ripple carries `c₁ … c₄` are absent — the bypass path only.

name: PLLND.envSkip
signature: def envSkip (δa δm : ℕ) (tcin tp0 tp1 tp2 tp3 : ℕ) : Env (M := ℕ) B Γskip
docstring:
The skip environment: three AND gates (delay `δa`), the mux (delay `δm`),
and inputs ready at their given times.

name: PLLND.coutSkip_extract
signature:
theorem coutSkip_extract (δa δm tcin tp0 tp1 tp2 tp3 : ℕ) :
    (coutSkip.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envSkip δa δm tcin tp0 tp1 tp2 tp3)).1
      = max tcin (max (max tp0 tp1 + δa) (max tp2 tp3 + δa) + δa) + δm
docstring:
**Raw skip extraction, by `rfl`**: the mux merges `cin` with the
`P`-tree's output.

name: PLLND.coutSkip_bound
signature:
theorem coutSkip_bound (δa δm : ℕ) :
    (coutSkip.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envSkip δa δm 0 0 0 0 0)).1 = 2 * δa + δm
docstring:
**The skip bound.**  With `cin` and every `pᵢ` ready at `0`, the
all-propagate carry-out is ready at `2·δ_and + δ_mux` — the balanced `P`-tree
(`2·δ_and`) followed by the mux.  No ripple term.

name: PLLND.dCARRY
signature: def dCARRY : ℕ
docstring: Full-adder carry-stage nominal delay (ps).

name: PLLND.dMUX
signature: def dMUX : ℕ
docstring: `sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_1` nominal delay (ps).

name: PLLND.dTopoAdder
signature: def dTopoAdder : ℕ
docstring:
**The topological longest path** to `cout` (structural,
sensitisation-blind): `cin → ripple(4 stages) → cripple → mux`, i.e.
`4·δ_carry + δ_mux`.  This is the classic false path (ripple **and** skip),
and it is what naive topological STA reports.

name: PLLND.skip_beats_topological
signature:
theorem skip_beats_topological :
    (coutSkip.eval (· + ·) 0 B (envSkip dAND dMUX 0 0 0 0 0)).1 < dTopoAdder
docstring:
**The false-path punchline at scale, kernel-checked.**  The data-dependent
carry-out extracted from the `P = 1` skip proof (`280 ps`) is **strictly below**
the topological longest path (`580 ps`): the ripple-and-skip path is
non-sensitisable, so it never enters a correct proof's constraint set.
Extraction beats topological STA by `300 ps` (over 2×) — for free.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.Ogp
signature: abbrev Ogp
docstring:
A `(generate, propagate)` group pair, abstracted as one lax signal:
`◯gp` is ready when the pair is stable.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.Γ
signature: abbrev Γ : List PLLFormula
docstring:
The netlist: one reusable prefix-merge cell `∘ : ◯gp ⊃ ◯gp ⊃ ◯gp` and a
leaf pair `◯gp`.  Independent of how deep we fold.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.linFold
signature:
def linFold : ℕ → Tm Γ Ogp
  | 0     => .var (.there .here)                                 -- leaf
  | n + 1 => .app (.app (.var .here) (linFold n)) (.var (.there .here))  -- ∘ (linFold n) leaf
docstring:
**The ripple-shaped (linear) fold**: `∘` nested `n` deep to the left.  Same
shape as `RippleN.ripple`; `linFold n : Γ ⊢ ◯gp`.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.balFold
signature:
def balFold : ℕ → Tm Γ Ogp
  | 0     => .var (.there .here)                                 -- leaf
  | k + 1 => .app (.app (.var .here) (balFold k)) (balFold k)    -- ∘ (balFold k) (balFold k)
docstring:
**The balanced (lookahead) fold** over `2ᵏ` leaves: `∘` in a perfect binary
tree of depth `k`.  `balFold k : Γ ⊢ ◯gp` — the *same sequent* as `linFold`.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.env
signature: def env (δ : ℕ) : Env (M := ℕ) B Γ
docstring:
The environment: merge cell delay `δ` (a 2-input gate, `σ = max`), leaf pair
ready at `0`.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.linReady
signature: abbrev linReady (δ n : ℕ) : ℕ
docstring: Extracted ready-time of the linear (ripple-shaped) fold.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.balReady
signature: abbrev balReady (δ k : ℕ) : ℕ
docstring: Extracted ready-time of the balanced (lookahead) fold.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.linReady_zero
signature: theorem linReady_zero (δ : ℕ) : linReady δ 0 = 0

name: PLLND.Lookahead.linReady_succ
signature: theorem linReady_succ (δ n : ℕ) : linReady δ (n + 1) = max (linReady δ n) 0 + δ

name: PLLND.Lookahead.linReady_bound
signature: theorem linReady_bound (δ n : ℕ) : linReady δ n = n * δ
docstring: The ripple-shaped fold has delay `n·δ` — linear in the fold depth.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.balReady_zero
signature: theorem balReady_zero (δ : ℕ) : balReady δ 0 = 0

name: PLLND.Lookahead.balReady_succ
signature:
theorem balReady_succ (δ k : ℕ) :
    balReady δ (k + 1) = max (balReady δ k) (balReady δ k) + δ
docstring:
Each level of the balanced tree merges two identical subtrees — `σ = max`
of equal ready-times — and pays one cell delay: `balₖ₊₁ = max balₖ balₖ + δ`.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.balReady_bound
signature: theorem balReady_bound (δ k : ℕ) : balReady δ k = k * δ
docstring:
**The balanced fold has delay `k·δ`** — depth `k` over `2ᵏ` leaves, so
logarithmic in the leaf count.  By induction on the depth.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.lt_two_pow_pred
signature: theorem lt_two_pow_pred (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) : k < 2 ^ k - 1
docstring: `k < 2ᵏ - 1` for `k ≥ 2`: the balanced depth is below the linear length.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.lookahead_beats_ripple
signature:
theorem lookahead_beats_ripple (δ k : ℕ) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    balReady δ k < linReady δ (2 ^ k - 1)
docstring:
**Carry-lookahead beats ripple: proof restructuring is speed-up.**  The
balanced fold `balFold k` and the ripple-shaped fold `linFold (2ᵏ - 1)` derive
the *same* `◯gp` from the *same* `2ᵏ - 1` merge cells — the balanced tree only
re-associates them — yet the balanced delay `k·δ` is strictly below the linear
`(2ᵏ - 1)·δ`.  Delay is `◯`-nesting depth; the lookahead is the shallow proof.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.dMERGE
signature: def dMERGE : ℕ
docstring: Nominal prefix-merge delay (ps), taken equal to the carry cell.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.gate2v
docstring:
A 2-input cell carrying a delay **and** a value: the output is ready at
`max` of the inputs plus `δ`, and its value is `f` of the input values.  The
delay component is exactly `gate2`'s.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.envV
signature: def envV (δ : ℕ) (f : A → A → A) (a : A) : Env (M := ℕ) (fun _ => A) Γ
docstring:
The environment with a non-trivial value layer: merge cell `f` of delay `δ`,
and a leaf pair of value `a` ready at `0`.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.linGP
signature: abbrev linGP (δ : ℕ) (f : A → A → A) (a : A) (n : ℕ) : A
docstring: The group pair computed by the ripple-shaped fold.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.balGP
signature: abbrev balGP (δ : ℕ) (f : A → A → A) (a : A) (k : ℕ) : A
docstring: The group pair computed by the balanced (lookahead) fold.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.linGP_zero
signature: theorem linGP_zero : linGP δ f a 0 = a

name: PLLND.Lookahead.linGP_succ
signature: theorem linGP_succ (n : ℕ) : linGP δ f a (n + 1) = f (linGP δ f a n) a

name: PLLND.Lookahead.balGP_zero
signature: theorem balGP_zero : balGP δ f a 0 = a

name: PLLND.Lookahead.balGP_succ
signature:
theorem balGP_succ (k : ℕ) :
    balGP δ f a (k + 1) = f (balGP δ f a k) (balGP δ f a k)

name: PLLND.Lookahead.linGP_append
signature:
theorem linGP_append (hf : ∀ x y z : A, f (f x y) z = f x (f y z)) (m n : ℕ) :
    f (linGP δ f a m) (linGP δ f a n) = linGP δ f a (m + n + 1)
docstring:
Concatenating two ripple-shaped folds gives a longer ripple-shaped fold.
**This is the only place associativity is used.**

name: PLLND.Lookahead.balGP_eq_linGP
signature:
theorem balGP_eq_linGP (hf : ∀ x y z : A, f (f x y) z = f x (f y z)) (k : ℕ) :
    balGP δ f a k = linGP δ f a (2 ^ k - 1)
docstring:
**The two folds compute the same group carry.**  For *any* associative merge,
the balanced fold of depth `k` and the ripple-shaped fold of length `2ᵏ - 1` ---
which combine the same `2ᵏ` leaf pairs --- produce the same value.  Re-association
is therefore sound: the lookahead computes what the ripple computes, faster.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.linGP_delay
signature:
theorem linGP_delay (n : ℕ) :
    (Tm.eval (· + ·) 0 (fun _ => A) (linFold n) (envV δ f a)).1 = linReady δ n
docstring:
The value layer does not disturb the timing: the very evaluation that
produces the group pair reproduces the linear delay bound.

name: PLLND.Lookahead.balGP_delay
signature:
theorem balGP_delay (k : ℕ) :
    (Tm.eval (· + ·) 0 (fun _ => A) (balFold k) (envV δ f a)).1 = balReady δ k
docstring:
Likewise for the balanced fold: one evaluation yields both the group pair
and the logarithmic delay bound.

name: PLLND.GP
signature: abbrev GP
docstring: A carry `(generate, propagate)` pair.

name: PLLND.gpMerge
signature: def gpMerge (u v : GP) : GP
docstring:
The carry-merge (prefix) operator
`(g, p) ∘ (g', p') = (g ∨ (p ∧ g'), p ∧ p')`.

name: PLLND.gpMerge_assoc
signature:
theorem gpMerge_assoc :
    ∀ x y z : GP, gpMerge (gpMerge x y) z = gpMerge x (gpMerge y z)
docstring:
The carry merge is associative --- the algebraic fact every prefix adder
exploits.  By case analysis on the six bits, so **axiom-free**.

name: PLLND.lookahead_eq_ripple_gp
signature:
theorem lookahead_eq_ripple_gp (δ : ℕ) (a : GP) (k : ℕ) :
    balGP δ gpMerge a k = linGP δ gpMerge a (2 ^ k - 1)
docstring:
**Lookahead and ripple compute the same carry.**  At the actual carry
algebra: the depth-`k` balanced fold and the length-`2ᵏ - 1` ripple fold of the
same leaf pair produce the same group `(generate, propagate)` pair.  Together
with `lookahead_beats_ripple` --- which is strictly faster --- this says the two
networks compute the *same function* at different cost, so the speed-up is a
re-association of the proof and not a change of what is proved.

name: PLLND.RippleN.Oc
signature: abbrev Oc

name: PLLND.RippleN.Op
signature: abbrev Op

name: PLLND.RippleN.Γ
signature: abbrev Γ : List PLLFormula
docstring:
The netlist, **independent of the width `n`**: one reusable full-adder
carry cell `◯c ⊃ ◯p ⊃ ◯c`, the propagate line `◯p`, and the carry-in `◯c`.

name: PLLND.RippleN.ripple
signature:
def ripple : ℕ → Tm Γ Oc
  | 0     => .var (.there (.there .here))                                 -- carry-in
  | n + 1 => .app (.app (.var .here) (ripple n)) (.var (.there .here))    -- g (ripple n) p
docstring:
**The n-bit ripple carry chain as a proof term**: the single carry cell
applied `n` times to the carry-in.  `ripple n : Γ ⊢ ◯c`.

name: PLLND.RippleN.env
signature: def env (δ tc tp : ℕ) : Env (M := ℕ) B Γ
docstring:
The environment: carry cell delay `δ` (a 2-input gate, so `σ = max`),
carry-in ready at `tc`, propagate ready at `tp`.

name: PLLND.RippleN.ready
signature: abbrev ready (δ tc tp n : ℕ) : ℕ
docstring: The extracted ready-time of the width-`n` carry-out.

name: PLLND.RippleN.ready_zero
signature: theorem ready_zero (δ tc tp : ℕ) : ready δ tc tp 0 = tc
docstring: Base: the width-`0` carry-out *is* the carry-in.

name: PLLND.RippleN.ready_succ
signature:
theorem ready_succ (δ tc tp n : ℕ) :
    ready δ tc tp (n + 1) = max (ready δ tc tp n) tp + δ
docstring:
**The carry recurrence, read off the proof term by `rfl`.**  Each further
cell merges the previous carry with the propagate line (`σ = max`) and pays the
cell delay: `readyₙ₊₁ = max readyₙ tp + δ`.

name: PLLND.RippleN.ready_bound
signature: theorem ready_bound (δ n : ℕ) : ready δ 0 0 n = n * δ
docstring:
**Linear carry delay, by induction on the width.**  With carry-in and
propagate ready at `0`, the `n`-bit ripple carry-out settles at `n·δ`.  Each
induction step is one carry cell in the proof term — critical-path length is
carry-cell nesting depth.

name: PLLND.RippleN.dTopoRipple
signature: def dTopoRipple (δ n : ℕ) : ℕ
docstring:
The **topological longest carry path** of the `n`-bit ripple: the unique
chain through all `n` carry cells, `n·δ`.  There is only one carry path, so it
is trivially sensitisable.

name: PLLND.RippleN.ripple_tight
signature: theorem ripple_tight (δ n : ℕ) : ready δ 0 0 n = dTopoRipple δ n
docstring:
**The ripple carry chain is timing-tight: extraction *equals* topological.**
Contrast `skip_beats_topological` (strict `<`): the carry-skip adder's longest
path is *false*, so extraction beats topology; the ripple's carry path is
unique and sensitisable, so extraction *matches* topology.  The two adders
bracket the general fact — extraction `≤` topological STA, equality iff the
longest path is sensitisable.

name: PLLND.RippleN.ready_mono
signature:
theorem ready_mono (δ : ℕ) {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) :
    ready δ 0 0 n ≤ ready δ 0 0 m
docstring:
**Delay is monotone (indeed linear) in the width.**  More adder bits ⟹ an
at-least-as-long carry delay — the linear blow-up that motivates carry-skip and
carry-lookahead.

name: PLLND.SNt.step
signature:
theorem SNt.step {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ φ}
    (h : SNt t) (hs : Step t t') : SNt t'

name: PLLND.SNt.steps
signature:
theorem SNt.steps {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula} {t t' : Tm Γ φ}
    (hs : Steps t t') : SNt t → SNt t'

name: PLLND.SNt.abort
signature:
theorem SNt.abort {Γ : List PLLFormula} (φ : PLLFormula) {t : Tm Γ .falsePLL}
    (h : SNt t) : SNt (Tm.abort φ t)

name: PLLND.SNt.lam
signature:
theorem SNt.lam {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {b : Tm (φ :: Γ) ψ}
    (h : SNt b) : SNt (Tm.lam b)

name: PLLND.SNt.inl
signature:
theorem SNt.inl {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {a : Tm Γ φ}
    (h : SNt a) : SNt (Tm.inl (ψ := ψ) a)

name: PLLND.SNt.inr
signature:
theorem SNt.inr {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ ψ : PLLFormula} {a : Tm Γ ψ}
    (h : SNt a) : SNt (Tm.inr (φ := φ) a)

name: PLLND.SNt.val
signature:
theorem SNt.val {Γ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula} {a : Tm Γ φ}

signature:
theorem Tm.subst_steps : ∀ {Γ Δ : List PLLFormula} {φ : PLLFormula}
    (t : Tm Γ φ) {σ τ : Sub Γ Δ}, SubSteps σ τ →
    Steps (t.subst σ) (t.subst τ)
  | _, _, _, .var v, _, _, h => h v
  | _, _, _, .abort φ t, _, _, h =>
      Steps.cong (fun hs => .abortCong hs) (t.subst_steps h)
  | _, _, _, .lam t, _, _, h =>
      Steps.cong (fun hs => .lamCong hs) (t.subst_steps h.lift)
  | _, _, _, .app t s, _, _, h =>
      (Steps.cong (fun hs => .appCong₁ hs) (t.subst_steps h)).trans
        (Steps.cong (fun hs => .appCong₂ hs) (s.subst_steps h))
  | _, _, _, .pair t s, _, _, h =>
      (Steps.cong (fun hs => .pairCong₁ hs) (t.subst_steps h)).trans
        (Steps.cong (fun hs => .pairCong₂ hs) (s.subst_steps h))
  | _, _, _, .fst t, _, _, h =>
      Steps.cong (fun hs => .fstCong hs) (t.subst_steps h)
  | _, _, _, .snd t, _, _, h =>
      Steps.cong (fun hs => .sndCong hs) (t.subst_steps h)
  | _, _, _, .inl t, _, _, h =>
      Steps.cong (fun hs => .inlCong hs) (t.subst_steps h)
  | _, _, _, .inr t, _, _, h =>
      Steps.cong (fun hs => .inrCong hs) (t.subst_steps h)
  | _, _, _, .case t u₁ u₂, _, _, h =>
      ((Steps.cong (fun hs => .caseCong₀ hs) (t.subst_steps h)).trans
        (Steps.cong (fun hs => .caseCong₁ hs) (u₁.subst_steps h.lift))).trans
        (Steps.cong (fun hs => .caseCong₂ hs) (u₂.subst_steps h.lift))
  | _, _, _, .val t, _, _, h =>
      Steps.cong (fun hs => .valCong hs) (t.subst_steps h)
  | _, _, _, .bind t u, _, _, h =>
      (Steps.cong (fun hs => .bindCong₁ hs) (t.subst_steps h)).trans
        (Steps.cong (fun hs => .bindCong₂ hs) (u.subst_steps h.lift))

theorem rename_id {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C : PLLFormula} :
    ∀ {A : PLLFormula} (K : Kont Γ C A), K.rename (fun {_} v => v) = K
  | _, .nil => rfl
  | _, .cons u K => by
      show Kont.cons (u.rename (Ren.lift fun {_} v => v))
        (K.rename fun {_} v => v) = _
      rw [show u.rename (Ren.lift fun {_} v => v) = u from
        (u.rename_congr (by lift_cases)).trans u.rename_id, rename_id K]

    (ρ : Ren Γ Δ) (ρ' : Ren Δ Θ) :

    (K.rename ρ).rename ρ' = K.rename (fun v => ρ' (ρ v))
  | _, .nil => rfl
  | _, .cons u K => by
      show Kont.cons ((u.rename ρ.lift).rename ρ'.lift) ((K.rename ρ).rename ρ')
        = Kont.cons (u.rename (Ren.lift fun v => ρ' (ρ v))) (K.rename _)
      rw [Tm.rename_rename, rename_rename ρ ρ' K,
        show u.rename (fun v => Ren.lift ρ' (Ren.lift ρ v))
            = u.rename (Ren.lift fun v => ρ' (ρ v)) from

theorem plug_step_cases : ∀ {Γ : List PLLFormula} {C A : PLLFormula}
    (K : Kont Γ C A) (X : Tm Γ (somehow A)) {y : Tm Γ (somehow C)},
    Step (K.plug X) y →
    (∃ X', Step X X' ∧ y = K.plug X') ∨
    (∃ K', KStep K K' ∧ y = K'.plug X) ∨
    (∃ (s₀ : Tm Γ A) (B : PLLFormula) (u₀ : Tm (A :: Γ) (somehow B))
        (K₀ : Kont Γ C B), X = .val s₀ ∧ K = .cons u₀ K₀ ∧
        y = K₀.plug (u₀.subst1 s₀)) ∨
    (∃ (A₀ : PLLFormula) (t₀ : Tm Γ (somehow A₀))
        (t₁ : Tm (A₀ :: Γ) (somehow A)) (B : PLLFormula)
        (u₀ : Tm (A :: Γ) (somehow B)) (K₀ : Kont Γ C B),
        X = .bind t₀ t₁ ∧ K = .cons u₀ K₀ ∧
        y = K₀.plug (.bind t₀ (.bind t₁ (u₀.rename Ren.skip1))))
docstring:
**Classification of the steps of a plugged term**, for an arbitrary
scrutinee `X`: either `X` steps, or the stack steps, or `X`'s head
constructor meets the innermost frame (`let`-β or `let`-assoc at the
interface).  This is `cut_aux`'s `leftCommute` in continuation clothing;
the scrutinee is kept general precisely so the lemma can be reused for
neutral, `val`- and `bind`-headed `X` alike.

    SNt s → SNt (K.plug (u.subst1 s)) →

docstring:
**The principal lemma** (Lindley–Stark): a `let`-β redex in a stack
context is SN as soon as its contractum-in-context and its value part are.

interface-assoc reduct keeps the first component — the underlying term is
literally unchanged — and shortens the stack, which is exactly the case
bare `Acc`-induction cannot handle and ordinal rank can.

signature:
def SRed : (φ : PLLFormula) → ∀ {Γ : List PLLFormula}, Tm Γ φ → Prop
  | .prop _, _, t => SNt t
  | .falsePLL, _, t => SNt t
  | .ifThen A B, Γ, t => SNt t ∧
      ∀ {Δ : List PLLFormula} (ρ : Ren Γ Δ) (s : Tm Δ A),
        SRed A s → SRed B (.app (t.rename ρ) s)
  | .and A B, _, t => SNt t ∧ SRed A (.fst t) ∧ SRed B (.snd t)
  | .or A B, _, t => SNt t ∧
      (∀ {w}, Steps t (.inl w) → SRed A w) ∧
      (∀ {w}, Steps t (.inr w) → SRed B w)
  | .somehow A, Γ, t => SNt t ∧
      ∀ {Δ : List PLLFormula} (ρ : Ren Γ Δ) {C : PLLFormula}
        (K : Kont Δ C A), KRedP (SRed A) K → SNt (K.plug (t.rename ρ))

the formula.  Only the `◯`-clause differs from the β-fragment
(`PLLReducibility.lean`): the value clause is upgraded to Lindley–Stark
biorthogonality — `t` is reducible at `◯A` when every reducible stack
consumes (every renaming of) it into an SN term.

    (hP : ∀ n, P (A n))
    (hstrict : ∀ n, ¬ Deriv [A (n + 1)] (A n))
    (φ : PLLFormula)
    (habove : ∀ n, Deriv [A n] φ)
    (htrap : ∀ ψ, P ψ → Deriv [ψ] φ → ∃ n, Deriv [ψ] (A n)) :
    ¬ ∃ χ, P χ ∧ Deriv [χ] φ ∧
        (∀ ψ, P ψ → Deriv [ψ] φ → Deriv [ψ] χ)
docstring:
**The `∀p` refutation criterion.**  If a strictly ascending chain `A` of
`P`-formulas lies below `φ` and is cofinal among the `P`-formulas entailing
`φ`, then `φ` has no greatest `P`-antecedent — no pre-interpolant.
